items: Automated surveys.
Analysis of trends.
Analysis of sentiment.
Competitive intelligence.
Visualizing data.

body.text: These insights can help brands create hyper-personalized marketing and implement proactive customer churn reduction strategies.
Web3 and Decentralized Branding

Web3, or decentralized web, is the next generation of the internet. Unlike Web2, where a few big companies own the data and platforms where interactions will occur, Web3 is based on blockchain technology, which allows users to have more ownership and control of their digital identities and assets.

Brands will no longer be hamstrung by a one-way relationship with their customers through companies like Facebook or Instagram to build their community. Rather, brands will have decentralized platforms to utilize that enable a community and allow brands to form more direct and transparent relationships with their customers.

Web3 gives your community control over gatekeepers so you can establish open relationships through decentralized systems and smart-contract management. **Our **[**Web3 design service**](/industries/web3) develops user-friendly interfaces and unified visual designs that activate user-owned ecosystems.

body.text: NFTs, Digital Ownership, and Brand Loyalty Programs
Several years ago, NFTs were wildly popular. The chatter has died down, but marketers still value the fundamental technology. Web3 NFTs create ownership, access, and engagement.
These tokens enable digital ownership and exclusive experiences. NFT rewards are verifiable, tradeable, and unique, unlike company database point systems.

A B2B brand can issue NFT-based client certification credentials or tokenized access to invite-only forums or CEO roundtables. Use NFTs to prove your attendance at events, product feedback sessions, or early betas.
How Brands Are Monetizing Digital Spaces

Limited-edition NFTs that grant VIP access generate new revenue streams for brands. Entertainment companies open Metaverse pop-up shops for virtual and real merchandise preview and purchase, and creators create token-gated communities with paid, exclusive content. AI-powered chatbots personalize visitor journeys, and smart contracts automatically pay royalties on resales.

Modern website design converges both Web3 and AI into one cohesive piece of advanced UI/UX that not only opens up the ability to shape a website's layout based on user behavior but also provides hassle-free, one-click wallet crypto payment, as well as real-time personalized product suggestions. Brands can successfully retain customers through their combination of usable design and new and unique features that provide fun experiences.
The Future of E-Commerce in the Metaverse

As more people shop online, the eCommerce portion of the Metaverse is expected to be robust. Industry insiders expect it to reach [$1 trillion](https://www.business-standard.com/economy/news/india-s-internet-economy-is-estimated-to-reach-1-trillion-by-2030-experts-124051600984_1.html) by 2030 as companies launch and test new products in the virtual space.

Just picture entering a store in the Metaverse where your avatar can walk through the store, you can interact with AI shop associates, and you can try on virtual clothes that fit your digital self. Companies are utilizing the Metaverse to create interactive virtual marketplaces and dynamic virtual stores.

[Gucci](https://www.gucci.com/us/en/st/stories/article/gucci-vault-land-in-the-sandbox?srsltid=AfmBOoohOgkTSsbrUI4HPD047Ionj1mMl6B8IlGinyMuxW2wRsP0IerP) and Nike already have virtual marketplaces where customers can buy NFTs or other virtual things.
Integration of AI and Web3 in Brand Innovation

Integrating AI data intelligence with the decentralized trust of Web3 allows brands to deliver personalized experiences that are open, immersive, and scalable. AI algorithms deliver an unlimited amount of real-time personalized content and product recommendations to users based on their preferences. Meanwhile, blockchain and smart contracts ensure the authenticity of products and create verifiable ownership rights and functional transactions.
Decentralized Autonomous Brands (DABs)

A DAB is a blockchain-based, community-led brand governed by its members. In contrast to traditional brands, DABs use tokens or innovative contract-based platforms to let stakeholders — customers, creators, suppliers, and even fans — vote on crucial actions, campaigns, and projects.
DABs use blockchain technology, making financial, operational, and governance data public and verifiable.
AI in Web3-Driven Marketing Strategies
AI can analyze complex blockchain and off-chain data to determine the optimal marketing strategies. It can track ad clicks, social media activity, and community event participation.
It can correlate conversions and ROI to individual marketing efforts, helping marketers identify what works and what doesn't. AI in Web3 marketing will improve brand engagement and promotion.
Best Practices for Future-Ready Brand Innovation

Dynamic brands drive brand evolution. Companies achieve success through effective brand strategy optimization. They build foundational brand blocks through their commitment to future-ready branding features. The brand can achieve success in competitive situations by implementing future-ready methods.

How to Leverage AI Responsibly

Without proper controls, AI tools can harm firms financially, legally, and reputationally. Google lost [$100 billion](https://www.reuters.com/technology/google-ai-chatbot-bard-offers-inaccurate-information-company-ad-2023-02-08/) in market value (9% stock decline) due to an error in its Bard chatbot in early 2023. In 2014, [Uber was criticized](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-30595406) for raising fares during a Sydney café siege due to increased demand. The corporation had to offer free trips to regain customer trust and reputation.

title: Brand Vision in the Age of AI: How to Stay Relevant and Innovative
author: Alyona Deieieva
excerpt: Interesting fact: Only [30%](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1267028/brand-guidelines/) of companies deliver the brand vision they've set out, and 15% of them haven’t established one yet.

body.text: Interesting fact: Only [30%](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1267028/brand-guidelines/) of companies deliver the brand vision they've set out, and 15% of them haven’t established one yet.
Why do they overlook its importance? A vision determines a company's future. Where is the brand going? What is its goal? What values should it uphold? Why does it matter?
But it's not just any vision. It should be updated regularly and revised.

It's the ability to adapt and evolve with a changing landscape that separates innovative brands that continue to live, grow, adapt, and thrive. Innovation results in new ideas, improved consumer experiences, and expansion. But without it, even storied brands are at risk of aging out. How does creative innovation work, and why is it so essential?
How does brand innovation work, and why is it so important?
Our [Arounda team](https://arounda.agency/about) designed this guide to help you define and create a customer-focused, innovative vision.
Why it matters for your business

items: Clarifies your brand's direction
Anticipates market shifts
Builds customer trust
Keeps your message authentic
Inspires customer engagement
Leverages AI insights

body.text: Why Brand Vision Matters More Than Ever

Do you know what is a brand vision? A vision is crucial when designing a business strategy. It differentiates you from the competition and shapes customer engagement. A brand's purpose and personality can easily become clouded by a lack of a vision statement, leaving marketing and sales activities detached or disconnected.
Brand vision vs. brand identity: Key differences
Brand’s vision and identity are two distinct concepts, and it's essential not to confuse them.

items: **Vision** - It describes the company's long-term goals, values, and impact. It answers the "why" question. Why a company works. A vision unites employees and attracts clients who share it. That’s a simple definition of brand vision.
**Identity** - It's the company's face. It includes logos, colors, design styles, messaging, and tone of voice.

body.text: Vision is the overall picture, whereas identity is how it's portrayed.

Here's an example of our [work](https://arounda.agency/case/gt-protocol) with GT Protocol, an investment platform powered by AI. We **matched vision with identity** by creating a new design and logo. We also helped with user analysis to find out the main pains their target audiences face. We then used this information to make user personas and build a platform that was clear, transparent, and helpful.
Brand vision vs. brand mission: How they work together
Vision and mission are frequently mistaken. To differentiate Vision and Mission, add “-ary” to each adjective.

items: A VISION**ARY** is capable of seeing the future and the company's destiny. Vision statements state our goals.
A MISSION**ARY** helps execute that vision. Thus, a mission statement explains how to attain the vision.

body.text: Among the most popular brand vision examples are [LinkedIn's](https://about.linkedin.com/) vision and mission statements, which ambitiously and clearly show that LinkedIn is transforming itself from a professional networking site to a catalyst for world economic empowerment.

body.alt: LinkedIn Vision and Mission statement screenshot.

body.text: Why every successful business needs a clear brand vision

[62% of consumers](https://ecommercebonsai.com/branding-statistics/) build an emotional connection with brands. Vision makes this connection possible. Vision statements help companies to achieve success because they give them direction. A brand vision is crucial when designing a business strategy. It differentiates you from the competition and shapes customer engagement.
How AI is reshaping branding and customer expectations

AI has democratized branding, changing the scene. The capabilities needed for branding that were once accessible only to large advertising firms are now available to startups. Branding remains essential because all businesses need effective brand management regardless of their size.

The ability of AI to process large customer datasets has revolutionized how brands interact with their customers. Predictive personalization stands as AI's most powerful branding instrument because it uses data and machine learning to forecast what consumers will need and want.

Brands can develop responsive customer experiences through predictive personalization. The implementation of AI by [93% of marketers](https://www.surveymonkey.com/mp/ai-marketing-statistics/) enables them to produce content at a faster rate, gain insights quickly, and make decisions rapidly, which accelerates brand communication and strategy.
How to Define and Develop Your Brand Vision
A compelling vision serves as the foundation for defining business objectives that will shape your future. The steps are simple:
Step 1: Identify your brand's purpose and values

Focus on your brand's values. These ideals are your brand's moral compass. Integration into your vision will reinforce your steadfast commitment to them. Your ideals should resonate with your staff and audience.
Step 2: Understand your market and competition

Your vision needs to align with market goals and industry trends to connect with your target audience. Your idea will gain more power when you understand the current needs of your clients and predict upcoming trends. Your brand should evolve within the larger market framework to stay competitive and maintain freshness.
Step 3: Craft an inspiring vision statement
A Vision Statement (what we will achieve) is a description of a desired outcome that inspires, excites, and helps an organization define its destination.
Key criteria for crafting a Vision Statement

items: **Measurable** — to see the progress
**Vivid** — to be clear and understandable
**Cultural** — to match the company's style
**Reachable** — to make sure it can be done
**Inspiring** — must make people feel something

body.text: Step 4: Communicate and integrate your vision across all touchpoints

Your vision is worth nothing if it just lives in a document. You want your vision to drive your team, be embedded into everything that you say and do, and guide your marketing campaigns, customer service, and more. You want to be aligned with your vision. It is not just the visuals but the tone of voice you use and the culture you foster that bring your vision into every experience. You want your customers to experience the same vision in every interaction. This ultimately builds trust and loyalty, creating a shared vision that you've envisioned with your customers.
Step 5: Continuously evolve and refine your vision

Aspire to the future in your brand's vision statement. You may have achieved some of your objectives, but your vision statement represents your company's utopian future. Your goals and objectives should be clear. And don't worry; as your company grows, so can your brand vision.
Business success depends on visualizing your goal and messaging. Developing your values and designing your website around them are equally important.

Our solutions included modular themes, simple navigation, real-time collaboration, interactive charts, and customized dashboards.
Need [professional branding](/services/branding) for your company? We genuinely love what we do, and we'd be delighted to help you create or revamp your visual identity!
Case Studies: Brands Using AI to Strengthen Their Vision
Several forward-looking companies are taking advantage of AI to enhance and amplify their vision so that it remains relevant, informed by data, and meaningful for their audience.

The vision of [Tesla](https://www.tesla.com/about) is to "accelerate the world's transition to sustainable energy," and AI is integral to realizing that vision:

items: Autonomous Driving
Manufacturing Optimization
Personalized User Experience
Advanced Robotics

body.text: Tesla's innovative AI utilization improves product capabilities, operational efficiencies, and engagement while continuing to improve and demonstrate Tesla's leadership position across categories in automotive technology and beyond.

[Nike](https://www.nike.com/), as the leader in sports clothing and footwear, leverages AI and data to improve performance, fulfill worldwide customer demand and foster unique innovations.
Nike influences AI in this competitive and vigorous market to:

items: Organize the supply chain
Enhance consumer experiences
Promote product development

body.text: Nike uses AI to monitor business norms and stay competitive.
The rise of AI-powered branding in Fintech and SaaS
Here's what you need to know about AI in these two industries:

items: Artificial intelligence in Fintech will top [$50 billion](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1446269/ai-in-fintech-market-size-forecast/) by 2029.
The global AI-created SaaS market will reach a projected valuation of [$1,040 billion](https://www.coherentmarketinsights.com/industry-reports/ai-created-saas-market) by 2032.

body.text: AI technology enables FinTech and SaaS companies to function with advanced intelligence, speed, and personalized capabilities.

The AI technology at [Stripe](https://stripe.com/) and [Revolut](https://www.revolut.com/sv-SE/news/revolut_launches_ai_feature_to_protect_customers_from_card_scams_and_break_the_scammers_spell/) detects fraud while providing immediate financial insights to build trust and innovation throughout the process.

The workflow efficiency of SaaS AI applications like [HubSpot](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm/ai-crm) and [Notion](https://www.notion.com/) increases productivity and brand trust through their ability to predict user requirements and enhance workflow efficiency.

AI enables these firms to stand out from competitors in crowded markets through their ability to deliver hyper-focused, streamlined, seamless experiences. The future belongs to companies that build their brand ethos on AI to predict customer needs while maintaining authenticity, precision, and trustworthiness.

Arounda knows what it takes to create a successful design for an AI-powered Saas company. We worked with [Sinta](https://arounda.agency/case/sinta) to create a distinctive design with unique functionality, focusing on usability and a unified user experience.
Common Pitfalls: Where Brands Fail in the AI Age
In the hopes of discovering new insights, efficiency, and competitive advantages, multiple companies invest substantially in AI systems.
However, many investments fail. We don't always see streamlined operations and engaged employees. Instead, we see disengaged teams, broken workflows, and disappointing ROI. Why?

In their drive to digitize, many corporations forget that businesses are people communities as well as goal-achieving systems. Failing to understand this dual nature is a strategic mistake and detrimental to morale.
Here are the most prevalent AI adoption mistakes to avoid.
Sidestep these AI pitfalls

items: Losing the human spark
Feeding AI with biased data
Letting processes trump people
Trading authenticity for efficiency

body.text: Over-reliance on automation without emotional connection

AI saves marketers [2.5 hours daily](https://www.hubspot.com/state-of-marketing). By eliminating manual labor, automation can increase productivity but also cause overreliance. Speed and volume above quality risk compromise the personalized connection that clients value.
Imagine an email campaign with generic templates over individualized messages. Yes, the procedure becomes more efficient, but recipients may find it impersonal and bland.
**Our specialists recommend** saving the balance between automation and personalized connection.
AI bias and ethical concerns in branding

AI bias happens when algorithms use prejudiced data to make unfair choices. Imagine creating an AI product recommendation system. If the data fed into this system is unbalanced, your recommendations may exclude some demographics. This shows bias.

Imagine your AI-powered marketing system segments clients by purchase history and interaction rates. The use of biased data results in specific audience segments, such as elderly clients and particular regional clients, being undervalued, which leads to fewer targeted offers or recommendations. Clients who receive no attention will develop distrust toward your business because they feel unappreciated.
**Arounda professionals recommend** performing frequent bias audits on your AI models and diversifying your training data to ensure all your customer segments are represented.

Think of this in a larger sense. This concept extends beyond its current scope. Your brand will appear out of touch and discriminatory when consumers notice their preferences are not represented. The negative consequences of this situation lead to reduced customer involvement, elevated customer departure rates, and unfavorable customer reviews, which harm your brand reputation.
Marketing exists to build trust, and rebuilding trust stands as the most challenging aspect of all.
Losing brand authenticity in AI-generated content
[54% of brands](https://www.gartner.com/en/webinar/429879/1033327?utm_campaign=RM_GB_2022_GCSSL_NPP_PR1_CHATBOTWB) use chatbots or conversational AI for customer interactions.

The AI technology creates content that duplicates human writing while producing images and managing customer interactions, but it lacks the emotional connection and personalized touch that consumers desire. The implementation of AI solutions to boost productivity could result in the destruction of personal relationships, which build customer loyalty.

Expert Thoughts AI is great for generating visuals , but the results almost always need tweaking. Raw AI images are flawed 90% of the time — and even small mistakes can make your brand look fake and hurt credibility. Sofia Kostynska, Graphic Designer at Arounda
‍**Arounda recommends** a human-centered approach. Consider AI's effects on autonomy, relatedness, and competency. For example:

items: Does AI improve employee decision-making or enhance micro-management?
Has it replaced human interaction or promoted collaboration?
Does it promote learning and competency or hinder it and atrophy skills?

body.text: The responses should guide your AI implementation.

If you want to be authentic, you need to have a cohesive brand identity and a well-structured website before embarking on AI. The implementation of AI should boost your voice rather than overpower it. Our company provides [website design](/services/web-design) and [brand identity](/services/brand-identity) services to help you achieve the right results.
Practical Tips for Staying Relevant and Innovative

While up to [85 million](https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_Future_of_Jobs_Report_2025.pdf) jobs could be displaced by AI by this time next year, 97 million jobs will be created through collaboration with human partners with AI. To survive and thrive in the AI economy, you need to evolve into it as well.
Investing in AI-driven customer insights

More than [two-thirds](https://partners.wsj.com/qualtrics/putting-feedback-into-action/companies-turn-to-ai-as-customer-feedback-wanes/) of consumers would like to do business with companies that create their experience based on data from AI-driven insights.

The implementation of AI-driven customer insights generates substantial information about customers. The analysis shows how customers behave when buying products, their preferences for certain items, as well as their brand-related sentiments and marketing strategy effectiveness. Businesses can use these insights to improve their services, which leads to better customer needs fulfillment, satisfaction, and revenue growth.
Maintaining a human touch in digital experiences

The implementation of AI technology for process streamlining requires a human-centric approach. Customers want personalized experiences, but they also want to maintain personal connections with real people. Businesses should integrate automated touchpoints with human touchpoints to build an experience that recognizes, understands, and values their customers.
Measuring AI's impact on brand perception and loyalty

AI technology changes how customers perceive and interact with brands. The success of your AI-powered interactions can be measured by listening to customer feedback and review responses. The introduction of AI should lead to higher engagement levels and more repeat business. Your Net Promoter Score should be monitored to verify that these technological advancements strengthen customer loyalty.

**Arounda tip**: For new AI features, begin with a pilot group. This enables you to refine the experience so that it feels helpful rather than robotic while still keeping your company's human touch and reaping the advantages of AI.

We know how to make your AI features accessible and easy to use. Besides, we build design based on user insights to create a personalized experience for your audiences. Need professional design help? We know what we’re doing!
Conclusion

Your company’s vision, combined with AI technology that serves your target audience, will establish a solid base for maintaining relevance and authenticity. Your ability to lead market changes depends on collecting feedback and analyzing consumer behavior.

title: Startup Failure: The Branding Mistakes That Kill Early-Stage Firms
author: Alyona Deieieva
excerpt: Do you know how many startup companies fail? Statistics show that [90%](https://www.investopedia.com/articles/personal-finance/040915/how-many-startups-fail-and-why.asp#:~:text=Despite%20their%20promise%2C%20as%20many,first%20five%20to%20te

body.text: Do you know how many startup companies fail? Statistics show that [90%](https://www.investopedia.com/articles/personal-finance/040915/how-many-startups-fail-and-why.asp#:~:text=Despite%20their%20promise%2C%20as%20many,first%20five%20to%20ten%20years.) of new businesses fail to deliver their primary idea to their target consumers. Several variables, including the absence of interested stakeholders, poor operational performance, and inadequate process adjustments, cause a high failure rate.

However, a major reason young companies struggle to connect with their target audience regarding their core concept is the inadequate formation of their brand identity. A company can differentiate itself from competitors and connect with its target audience through branding to establish a distinct identity.
A business that fails to follow effective branding practices will experience significantly reduced chances of success.
Our[Arounda team](https://arounda.agency/about) has written this piece to highlight the common mistakes startups make in branding and provide guidance on how to avoid them.
Is your startup covering the branding basics?

items: Clear brand strategy
Consistent brand positioning and messaging
Sharp differentiation from competitors
Strong brand identity
Cohesive digital presence and brand experience
Proven trust and credibility

body.text: The Role of Branding in Startup Success

A company's identity is defined through branding. A brand requires a strategy, together with a distinctive tone of voice, recognizable logo, unified color scheme, and consistent font to establish its unique identity. Branding provides startups with both direction and clarity. It draws attention and connects audiences.

Startup branding extends beyond the combination of a tagline and logo. Your brand needs to express your company values while establishing itself as distinct from other competitors. This can be achieved in two ways: first, by embedding brand values into customer support, and second, by developing a distinctive brand voice through compelling content marketing. A startup can differentiate itself from competitors while building audience trust and recognition through the development of a well-designed brand that communicates its personality and message.
Branding Mistakes That Kill Early-Stage Startups

Globally, there are more than [150 million](https://techstartups.com/2025/03/03/startup-statistics-20-surprising-facts-you-need-to-know-in-2025/) startups, with about 50 million new companies opening annually, and most of them won’t make it. So, why do startups fail? Poor brand identity development is a significant contributor to startup failure rates. Understanding and avoiding fundamental branding errors — from identity issues to communication difficulty and inconsistent scaling — can make you the next digital unicorn and escape the fate of the many who fail despite promising products.
Your startup can avoid needless setbacks and failure if you are aware of these pitfalls.
1. Ignoring Brand Strategy

One fatal error that can lead to the downfall of your brand is the failure to develop a comprehensive brand strategy. Your brand may be clear to you, but did you write it all down? Do your customers and your team know all about it?
Imagine having an All-Star team but no game plan. How does it go? You'll lose. How good your team is depends on how good your plan is on paper.
Why Having a Clear Brand Strategy is Crucial

Businesses with thought-out digital brand strategies convert sales at a rate that is [2.5](https://www.consultancy.uk/news/2328/mckinsey-digital-brand-capabilities-eat-the-competition) times higher than that of businesses with less clear digital strategies.
Your startup is missing out on growth and consistent messaging to its ideal target customers if it designs brand identities without a strategy.

A brand strategy guides marketing and business objectives. It makes your brand look more consistent across platforms. You are demonstrating a single, unmistakable, and genuine voice. You're not misguiding clients. They understand you.
Your success can be sustained, and your place in the market established with the aid of a well-thought-out brand strategy.
How to Define Your Brand Vision and Mission

A company's brand vision defines the future impact of its business on the global community. The goal is to reflect your brand values and make sustainable change, not just increase revenue or market share.
Your mission statements should reflect your brand values and describe how you're achieving your vision.
**Arounda experts suggest** following these steps to create a meaningful brand vision:

items: Consider your brand's values.
Know your audience.
Establish your UVP.
State your brand's purpose.
Be brief and actionable.
Test and improve.

body.text: Every innovative tech-driven company in the world possesses a distinct brand vision that serves as its guiding light. The brand vision enables these companies to stand out in competitive markets while keeping their direction clear. Here's our brand's vision and mission — we hope it helps you shape yours.
2. Weak or Inconsistent Brand Identity

A company's success depends on its brand identity. The unique visual and behavioral aspects of a brand, which differentiate it from competitors, determine how customers view it. A company's identity goes beyond its logos and color schemes because it encompasses how the audience perceives it and how the company presents itself to the public.
The Cost of an Unprofessional Brand Image

Your branding materials with inconsistencies will confuse your audience while damaging the overall power of your brand. When your social media profiles and website display different color schemes and layouts, it becomes challenging for customers to remember and connect with your brand. Brand recognition, together with trust and customer loyalty, suffer when your branding materials show inconsistencies.
How to Create a Strong Visual Identity
Investing in creating a **full range of branding assets** is essential to combating the problem of an amateurish brand image.
This includes:

items: Designing a distinctive logo that reflects your brand's ethos.
Selecting colors that appeal to your target audience.
Creating marketing materials that consistently communicate your brand's message.

body.text: To strengthen your brand identity, **our team suggests**:

items: Aligning color schemes and layouts on the website and social media profiles.
Investing in visual branding assets.
Fostering customer loyalty by showing consistency.

body.text: From logos to entire design systems, Arounda helps companies build or upgrade brand identities.
Here's one of our branding projects, [Galaxy](/works/galaxy). Our team worked with Galaxy to create a visual brand that will never go out of style.
Does your company need a professional touch? We're passionate about our work and would love to help you create or rebuild your visual identity!
3. Failing to Differentiate from Competitors

Your company needs to develop its brand identity if it shares too many similarities with competitors. Your marketing strategy needs to be unique to attract and keep customer interest. The loss of uniqueness and value proposition occurs when companies merge with rivals, which results in decreased brand recognition and lower customer involvement.
The Danger of Blending In

[77%](https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/digital-silk-highlights-top-branding-statistics-for-2025-1034289079) of buyers base their decisions solely on brand names. A brand that lacks uniqueness makes it challenging for potential customers to understand why they should select your brand. Companies that provide similar products or services need a brand identity and narrative to establish their differentiation.
How to Stand Out in a Crowded Market
Your brand needs evaluation to maintain market competitiveness while using branding tactics that effectively present your core values and strengths to the market.
**Our Arounda specialists suggest** reassessing the visuals and messaging in your marketing approach to highlight your company's uniqueness.
4. Neglecting Brand Positioning and Messaging
The failure to address positioning or messaging will negatively impact your marketing efforts.

Your message will fail to stand out in the marketplace and effectively engage your target audience if it is unclear, contradictory, or unoriginal. A strong positioning strategy alone may not be enough to communicate brand value because weak messaging could lead to missed opportunities to build your clientele.
Crafting a Clear and Compelling Value Proposition
Value propositions explain a product or service's distinct value to customers. It responds to the “Why should I buy from you?” question.
To design an **appealing value proposition**, add the following critical elements:

items: **Grab attention with a headline.** It draws attention to your product and encourages further investigation. Clear, crisp, and memorable headlines work.
**Consider target customers' needs.** This aspect outlines your target market and the issues or demands your product or service solves.
**Highlight benefits and features.** Your product's features make it special, while its benefits are what your target audience expects from using it.

**Display your USP.** Unique Selling Points (USPs) distinguish products and services from the competition. Your USP should reflect your capabilities and be clearly and consistently expressed in your value proposition.
**Show social proof.** Share reviews, ratings, and case studies to prove your service works.

**Create a forceful call to action.** Your CTA needs to be both direct and compelling, no matter what action you want your audience to take. A strong call-to-action (CTA) should drive sales by encouraging your audience to take action.

body.text: Aligning Messaging with Customer Pain Points

Why do most startups fail? They're not trying to align their messaging with the target audience's problems. Excellent messaging addresses the issues that your audience faces directly rather than merely summarizing what you have to offer. Instead of purchasing goods or services, customers buy solutions to their problems.
You will lose your way if you dismiss their complaints or use general statements.

Identify their specific annoyances and time-consuming inefficiencies that cost them money, and develop your value proposition to address these pain points. Avoid using industry jargon and use their own language when communicating.
Put your product forward as the solution after demonstrating empathy. Your message grabs their interest, gains their trust, and motivates them to act when it is in line with their goals and issues.
Here’s** Arounda’s piece of advice**:

items: Simple and unique messaging creates wonders.
Find your audience’s pains and suggest solutions.
Align your team with brand positioning and messaging.

body.text: 5. Poor Digital Presence and Brand Experience

More than 4 billion internet users start their search for new products and services through online channels. Your business will remain undetectable to both local and global customers if you do not establish an online presence.

Your offer will not be noticed by people if they cannot locate you. Google alone processes over 8 billion searches daily. If your startup has a poor digital presence or performs poorly, you are providing opportunities for your competitors.
The Impact of a Weak Website and Social Media Strategy

Your company's website and social media accounts often influence first impressions of your business. Users will leave a website that loads slowly, is hard to use, or is out of date. If your social media accounts are disorganized or neglected, they will appear unprofessional.

Every opportunity to build credibility matters during the early stages of startup development. Your credibility suffers when your digital design is poor, your branding is inconsistent, and your content is outdated.
A clean, fast, and consistent online presence is essential to stay ahead of others and provide them with an easy way to win.

A professional and user-friendly website is a key strategy to avoid startup failure. Our [web design](/services/web-design) services will help your business succeed in the competitive environment. Here's an example of our work with [Marketspotter](https://arounda.agency/case/marketspotter), where we helped change a hard-to-navigate platform into clear, intuitive visuals without losing depth.

How UX and Content Influence Brand Perception
Almost every industry is crowded now. Therefore, customers will make a choice based on their first impression of your brand.

The first thing they see is your website. Having a great site is a big deal, as [88%](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/in/business/software/website-statistics/?via=hemin74) of users never return to websites with poor UX.

[Great UX](/blog/how-to-improve-user-experience-with-web-form-design) is all about making people comfortable on your website. You must comprehend what users need and what obstacles they face, together with their wants and limitations. The elements of colors, fonts, and images matter, but they are not the only factors. Your website's success depends on how users can easily locate content and how fast they can interact with it, while all elements function harmoniously.
Make sure your **UX answers these questions**:

items: **Can I locate it?** Do readers readily navigate your content?
**Do I understand?** Is your language easy to understand by a broad audience? Can audiences with visual or other impairments understand your content?
**Is it usable?** Does your audience know how to use your site?
**Am I content?** Does your website serve a purpose? How enjoyable was this experience?

body.text: 6. Not Building Trust and Credibility
If people don't trust you, they won't buy from you. That's why startups fail. It's really that simple.

Early-stage businesses that lack credible case studies, accurate contact information, and testimonials will experience financial losses. Your new business needs consistency, along with transparency and proven results to make a good impression.
Why Trust is Everything for a New Brand
Brand trust means that people believe a business can keep its promises.

A brand establishes trust through its dependable, honest, and consistent bond with its customer base. Customers tend to remain loyal to brands because they trust their promises and fundamental values. Your company should focus on developing strong customer relationships, which lead to customer comfort in choosing your brand over competitors, rather than just maintaining repeat purchases.
The Role of Customer Reviews and Testimonials

Client reviews and case studies generate trust. They are a powerful approach to generating authority, confidence, and clients. Studies reveal that over [98%](https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbesbusinessdevelopmentcouncil/2024/07/11/how-reviews-and-ratings-affect-clients-buying-decisions/) of shoppers check online reviews before making a purchase. Thus, professional service providers must actively seek and encourage good client feedback.

body.text: How Startups Can Avoid These Branding Mistakes

Learning from the mistakes of others can be a valuable lesson. The aforementioned common mistakes can help you prevent your own startup failure. Although every company has different problems, **our professionals** can provide insightful advice on how to deal with typical mistakes and problems.
Developing a Strategic Branding Plan
Modern branding relies on brand strategy. Developing a [brand strategy](/blog/how-much-does-branding-cost-breakdown-by-service) involves more than merely reaching several objectives.

Through strategic branding, audiences develop an instinctive bond with brands because they see them as active entities. A brand needs to present a unique belief system and individual personality along with a consistent tone and messaging that addresses customer challenges.
Here are some of the most essential steps in **building your brand strategy**:
**1.** Figure out who your customer is.
**2.** Create a market niche.
**3.** Develop a distinctive message.
**4.** Develop a striking visual identity.
**5.** Regularly evaluate and improve your strategy.
Investing in Professional Branding and Design
One of the most common causes for startups failing is that their websites don't convey their essence. Businesses typically struggle with these issues due to design.

Did you know that [75%](https://www.yaguara.co/branding-statistics/) of shoppers remember brands by their logo? Now, would you work with a company that has pixelated logos and poorly structured materials? Good design adds professionalism and boosts your brand's industry authority.

Arounda knows design goes beyond aesthetics. This strong instrument affects your audience's perception of your brand. Our talented designers collaborate closely with companies to create impactful, premium [designs](/services/ui-ux-design).

Creating a Consistent and Authentic Brand Voice

Building a real relationship with your audience requires finding your brand voice. The selection of tone and style is important because it is essential to ensure that the communication aligns with brand values and achieves the desired audience reception.
Here's how you can do it:

items: **Think about your internal communication.** Examine how your leadership and employees interact internally and externally. Does everyone use the same tone, or do they vary in tone?
**Establish your brand's ideals.** Your voice should be grounded in principles such as innovation, reliability, and social responsibility, ensuring it consistently aligns with your objectives.
**Develop comprehensive brand voice guidelines.** Document your brand rules to preserve consistency and avoid being among the 15% of organizations without them.
**Regularly analyze and improve your brand voice approach.** To keep your voice current as trends and preferences evolve, periodically review your plan, performance data, and feedback.

body.text: #1. Decision-making process.

How do users decide what and when to buy? B2C decisions are often emotional and immediate. B2B purchases involve multiple stakeholders, longer sales cycles, and layers of approval. So, branding must build **rational trust** and convey long-term value across an organization.
#2. Audience complexity.

B2C brands speak to individuals. B2B brands speak to cross-functional teams (from CEOs, CTOs, and finance officers to end users). Each of them has different concerns. You should balance technical credibility with business relevance and answers to deep and diverse field questions.
#3. Emotional appeal.
The emotional hook in B2B comes from trust, reputation, and reliability. Not impulse (“now,” “only today”...) or lifestyle!
#4. Sales cycle and relationship depth.
B2C interactions are often short-term. B2B relationships are for the long term. This means that branding should focus on consistency throughout the entire lifecycle.
#5. Value communication.

In B2C, benefits are often simple and immediate. In B2B, the value is layered (think ROI, integration, support, security, scalability). Your brand must articulate this complexity clearly but without overwhelming the audience. Challenging, right?
Arounda branding experts have solutions and step-by-step instructions to transform each challenge into brilliant persuasive performance.

Expert Thoughts In SaaS and Fintech, a strong visual identity builds trust. For a recent project, we chose a color palette and typography that balanced innovation and professionalism. By aligning the logo and illustrations with the target audience, we saw a noticeable boost in brand recognition and trust from the start. Alyona Deeva Lead Brand Designer

1. Define Your Brand Strategy
Every successful brand begins with a clear strategy. Without one, you’re just adding noise.
Start by answering the big questions!

items: Who are you really speaking to?

What do you want your company to be known for?

body.text: 2. Establish Brand Trust Through Thought Leadership

Because they will get advice not from Google or Chat GPT (they don’t know if it’s a reliable source), they get it from the expert! And this is YOU!
Publish insights backed by data. Share your point of view on emerging trends. Show your expertise; don’t just claim it.
How to do it? Website blog, e-courses, social media, expert interviews, checklists, cases, etc.

3. Invest in Visual Identity and Consistency
Your brand identity should be a consistent visual system that reflects your strategy, signals credibility, and creates an emotional connection. It's your logo, colors, typeface, and tone of voice.

Every touchpoint with all [brand attributes](/blog/brand-attributes-definition-importance-and-examples) should feel like part of one story. From your website to your pitch decks to your LinkedIn posts.

What do you expect as a B2B buyer? Relevance and no generic messaging. Right?
So, use data to tailor your communications. Segment your audience based on roles, company size, industry, or behavior. Create texts that directly address their needs.
Personalization in B2B isn’t about inserting a first name into an email. You have to show that you understand clients’ specific challenges and offer tailored solutions before they ask.

This builds trust faster, opens more doors, and turns your brand into a true partner!

Another important thing in brand authority is “**who says it with you.”**

Collaborating with respected names in your industry instantly boosts credibility! It can be a co-hosted webinar, a joint case study, being and speaking at the same event, or just cooperating with big dogs.
If your brand appears next to a known name, prospects assume you're in the same league. That’s the power of social proof in B2B.

body.text: When you’ve done everything right, it's time to measure the impact.
Measuring the Impact of B2B Branding in SaaS and Fintech

Branding can feel intangible until you can actually track the results. It’s not as instant as ad clicks or demo sign-ups, but a strong brand delivers long-term, compounding outcomes. You should know what to measure and how to connect branding to business outcomes.
Key branding metrics
We recommend tracking metrics that reflect trust, relevance, and strategic visibility.
**1. Branded search volume. **When prospects search your company name or branded terms, it signals growing market recognition.
**2. Direct traffic. **An increase in direct visits to your site (vs. referrals or ads) often indicates brand familiarity.
**3. Engagement quality (behavioral metrics) - **time on site, pages per session, scroll depth, repeat visits. They indicate how well your brand messaging and experience resonate with your audience.
**4. Share of voice. **Analyze mentions in digital media, podcasts, reports, LinkedIn, and niche forums. A rising SOV signals increasing influence within your category.
**5. Branded traffic conversion rate. **This tells you if brand awareness is translating into qualified leads.

**6. Customer perception metrics (qualitative). **Include NPS, brand sentiment surveys, and buyer feedback. These insights will show you if your brand is aligned with how your market sees you. And if not, what needs adjusting.
Tracking brand authority through media mentions and backlinks

Do you know how the industry talks about you when you're not in the room? The more your name appears in respected media, trusted platforms, and high-quality content, the more weight your brand carries.
*Q: How to monitor ****media mentions****?*
*A: We recommend tracking with Google Alerts, Mention or Brand24, and BuzzSumo. *
*Q: Why it’s important? *
*A: You can understand how visible and credible your brand is becoming in your space. When industry blogs, analysts, or news sites reference your company, it signals growing influence.*
*Q: What to look for?*
*A: Type of publication (mainstream media vs. niche blogs), sentiment (positive, neutral, or negative), volume over time (monthly/quarterly growth), relevance to your target audience or industry. *
*Q: What about ****backlinks****? *
*A: Backlinks are digital endorsements. When respected domains link to your site, it signals that your content (and, by extension, your brand) is valuable.*
*Q: How to track it?*
*A: Use Ahrefs, SEMrush, or Moz to know the total number of backlinks, referring domains, domain authority of sites linking to you, and new vs. lost links over time. *
Brand authority tells partners, prospects, and investors: “This company knows its space, and the industry knows it too.”

Strong branding lowers your Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) and increases your Customer Lifetime Value (LTV). How exactly?

items: **Lower CAC.** When prospects already trust your brand, they move through the funnel faster. Less time convincing, more time converting.
**Higher LTV.** Brand loyalty leads to longer relationships, more renewals, and higher upsell potential. Clients who believe in your brand are more likely to grow with you.

excerpt: ‍It’s not working.

body.text: ‍**It’s not working.**
That’s the sentence no product owner wants to hear. Not from users, not from investors, and definitely not from the team that built it. Right?

If your product feels clunky, confusing, or unintuitive, your users will leave, and even the most powerful features can go unnoticed or unused. What will help? Usability, excellent user experience! Because a great UX makes your products and all cool features work beautifully and really help people.
**Is that your goal?**

If yes, then [our Arounda team](https://arounda.agency/about) found 10 [UX design](/services/ui-ux-design) quotes to emphasize how important usability is and explain how to make things work better for your business. It may change how you see your product. Ready, steady, go!
1. “Usability is about people and how they understand and use things, not about technology.”

Digital products must have great tech (frameworks, features, and functions) to hit the market. That’s not a secret, of course. But usability? From our experience, many product owners pay huge attention to tech but neglect usability.
Usability is about people and how they understand and use things, not about technology. Steve Krug

The best UX starts not with code but with [empathy](/blog/empathy-in-ux-design-how-to-improve-conversion-rate). And we consider UX to be the most important trigger for your product to be understood, loved, and grown.
Do you know 3 questions users have when they open your app or website? Here they are:

items: What is this?
What can I do here?
What should I click next?

body.text: If answers aren’t obvious, you’ve already lost users.
Now, want to impress people and make your product genuinely usable?
**What Arounda team recommends**

items: Watch how people interact with your product. Where do they pause, hesitate, or click the wrong button?
Don’t overestimate your users’ patience because they’re not here to explore every feature. They’re here to get a job done, so make it fast and obvious.
Prioritize clarity over cleverness. People need helpful and fast solutions; they won’t examine everything to say, “Oh, that’s so clever!”
Use plain language and familiar patterns.
Create with beginners in mind (especially in the Web3 industry).

body.text: You create a product for people, not for machines! Usability is the human side of tech. So, always prioritize people, and you will win the market race.
2. “Good design is like a refrigerator—when it works, no one notices, but when it doesn’t, it stinks.”
How often do you care about your refrigerator? Probably not so often until it leaks, stops cooling, or starts making weird noises. That's exactly how users experience digital products.
Good design is like a refrigerator—when it works, no one notices, but when it doesn't, it stinks. Irene Au

Great design often goes unnoticed because it's doing its job so well. But the moment something breaks (an unclear button, a broken flow, a missing feature), the friction becomes glaring. And your product becomes the problem.
**What Arounda team recommends**

items: Regular [UX audits](/services/ux-audit) help catch issues before they start to "smell".
Simplify workflows. If a task takes five clicks, can it be done in three?
Don't let tech lead design. Just because your team can build a feature doesn't mean it's needed or usable.
Respect cognitive load. Every unclear label or unexpected behavior adds mental effort. Keep it light.
Celebrate seamlessness. If users don't notice your interface, it's a successful experience.

body.text: If you notice some problems but are unsure about [UX audit](/services/ux-audit), check our projects, the processes, and the results.
Usability ≠ a colorful design. It's about not disturbing. And when your product just works, users won't say a word because they'll be too busy getting value.
3. “The best products don’t focus on features, they focus on clarity.”
Features = more value? More tools should mean more power?
Not quite.
The best products don't focus on features, they focus on clarity. Jon Bolt

Jon Bolt’s thought is one of our favorite [user experience design](/services/ui-ux-design) quotes. It’s a sharp reminder that clarity always trumps complexity. And the best products aren’t the ones packed with every possible function; they’re the ones that make users feel confident, in control, and focused from the first click.
**What Arounda team recommends**

items: Define your core use case. What problem is your product hired to solve? Design everything around that first.
Resist feature creep. More features mean more friction unless they’re seamlessly integrated and crystal clear.
Design for the first-time user. Experts might explore, but new users need direction. Give them a clear path.
Test for understanding. Ask users what they think a feature does. Their answers will show you what’s clear and what’s not.

body.text: Clarity builds trust!
4. “Design isn’t finished until somebody is using it.”
It’s easy to celebrate a design when it’s polished, prototyped, and ready for handoff. But the real test doesn’t begin until someone outside your team clicks, taps, scrolls, or swipes.
Design isn't finished until somebody is using it. Brenda Laurel

Too often, companies treat design like a deliverable instead of a process. But [product design](/) isn't finished at launch because it evolves with every insight, bug report, and behavior pattern your users reveal. What was a great solution 6 months ago now can't work anymore because people's behavior and market conditions could change.
That's why we focus not just on what we create but on how it's experienced over time! Usability is a moving target, and improvement is part of the product's lifecycle.
That's why we focus not just on what we create but on how it's experienced over time! Usability is a moving target, and improvement is part of the product's lifecycle.
**What Arounda team recommends**

items: Get your product in front of real users as soon as possible. Insights live in feedback.
Use analytics and heatmaps to reveal what’s working. What users say and what they do can be very different.
Iterate intentionally. Treat user behavior like data and adjust your design based on real patterns.
Build a feedback loop into your roadmap.
Accept that no design is ever “finished”. The best products always evolve.

body.text: If you're building or scaling a product, version 1 is just the beginning. The most successful digital products conduct redesigns to refine clarity, remove friction, and align the product with how people actually use it. They see a [redesign](https://arounda.agency/solutions/product-redesign) as a strategic investment in long-term growth.
How do you know if you need a redesign? Here are 6 common warning signs.
5. “Pay attention to what users do, not what they say.”
User interviews and surveys are valuable, but if you're building a product based only on what users say, you might solve the wrong problems.
**Actions speak louder than words in UX**!
Pay attention to what users do, not what they say. Jakob Nielsen

Users often think they know what they want or say they’d use a certain feature, but their actual behavior tells the real story. That’s why we always back up opinions with observation and recommend doing this for every product’s team.
**What Arounda team recommends**

items: Use session recordings and heatmaps to observe real behavior without interrupting the user experience. You can use Hotjar or FullStory.
Watch onboarding closely because where users drop off says more than a hundred interviews ever could.
Create usability tests with tasks (not questions). Ask users to complete a goal and observe where they get stuck.
Prioritize behavioral data (task completion rate, time on task, or bounce rate) because it's a clearer indicator of usability than opinions.
Don’t take requests at face value. When users ask for a feature, try to dig deeper and realize what problem they are trying to solve. You might find a better solution.

body.text: Expert Thoughts During usability tests, users often talk about their problems, wishes, and features they think they would use. But it's much more important to observe where they face difficulties and what's really behind those problems. Julia Didyk, Product designer
In [product design](/), what users promise to do doesn’t equal what they actually do. The sooner you observe that the better your product becomes.
6. “The next big thing is the one that makes the last big thing usable.”
Innovation shows the directions, but usability drives the adoption.

Think about how many "next big things" have flopped because they were too complicated, technical, or disconnected from the user's world! You don't have to reinvent the wheel; you can make it more enjoyable, faster, and more beautiful with new features or some adjustments. The real winners are the ones who make those breakthroughs usable for everyday people.
The next big thing is the one that makes the last big thing usable. Blake Ross
If you're building or investing in “the next big thing,” here’s how to make sure it will be accepted.
**What Arounda team recommends**

items: Simplify the experience without dumbing it down.
Translate complexity into clarity. Use onboarding, tooltips, and UI flows that guide without overwhelming.
Look at usability as a growth strategy.
Invest in UX early. Don’t wait until your tech is built! Design should evolve with development, not after it.
Test with non-experts.

body.text: In the race to build what’s next, usability is often the secret advantage. We at Arounda design Web3, Fintech, AI, and Healthcare products and always consider whether this or that feature is clear. Will people understand our design? We test, observe, and improve. It’s especially important in the Web3 world as it’s something new for billions of people.

Take a look at our [Web3 case studies](https://arounda.agency/works) to get a better picture. And here is our design of [Astra](https://arounda.agency/case/astra), a platform for excellent Web3 trading experience.
7. “If a user is having a problem, it’s our problem.”

Instead of assuming the user needs more patience, better instructions, or training, product teams must take full ownership. If people can’t use what you’ve built, the product isn’t working as intended. And no matter how advanced the backend or how sleek the interface is!
If a user is having a problem, it's our problem. Steve Jobs
This quote stands out among the most powerful quotes about user experience because it shifts the responsibility from the user to the team behind the product.
When you take responsibility for friction, you get opportunities to improve usability, retain customers, and boost satisfaction.
**What Arounda team recommends**

items: Every complaint is a data point. Use them to identify patterns in friction.
Join a few support calls or watch user testing videos. You’ll see where pain points live.
Don’t let user frustration get stuck in the support inbox. Route it to the team that can fix it.
Avoid blaming “user error.” Instead, ask: What could we change to make this issue disappear?
Revisit your onboarding and help content regularly.

body.text: Taking ownership of user problems builds trust. And trust, in product terms, is what keeps users coming back.
8. “The best interface is no interface.”

How can a digital product not have an interface? It might sound like one of the most thought-provoking user interface quotes. But it means we should design interactions that get out of the user’s way. When tasks feel seamless (unlocking your car by walking up to it or confirming payment with Face ID). Users don’t think about the interface. They think about the result. That’s the point.
The best interface is no interface. Golden Krishna
**What Arounda team recommends**

items: Focus on outcomes, not screens. Answer the questions: What does the user want to achieve? And how fast can we help them get there?
Reduce choices and steps where possible.
Use automation where it makes sense.
Design interactions that feel natural (swiping, tapping, or using voice).
Rethink default flows. Sometimes, removing a screen entirely is better than redesigning it.

body.text: The best interface might just be the one your users barely notice! Fewer clicks, smarter defaults, predictive design, and automation that minimize manual input.

We have an example for you - Sinta, an HR platform with customizable templates, AI-powered tools, and recorded video transcripts. [Discover our design case](https://arounda.agency/case/sinta) to understand what we mean by “feel natural”.
9. “People ignore design that ignores people.”
If your product isn't built with people in mind, they'll walk away. And no matter how brilliant the tech behind it is! Nobody loves to be ignored.
People ignore design that ignores people. Frank Chimero
**Check these 3 “if” when users will leave:**

items: If they can’t find what they’re looking for.
If a flow doesn’t feel intuitive and clear.
If your product makes them feel overwhelmed.

body.text: Respect your user. This means listening deeply, designing inclusively, and creating experiences that feel tailored.
**What Arounda team recommends**

items: Start with user research, and there is no place for guesses. What are their pain points, behaviors, and goals?
Don't wait until the launch. Get feedback on wireframes, flows, and even copy.
Accessibility and inclusivity are part of smart business.
Use storytelling in design. Make people feel something. Clear communication and thoughtful interactions matter.
Avoid the trap of building for yourself. Your team may know the product inside out, but your user doesn’t!

body.text: When you center people in your process, they’ll reward you with engagement, loyalty, and growth.

That’s why we are so focused on [human-centered design services](/services/ui-ux-design) and have it as our mission. Our designers align products with real user needs and care that every screen, flow, and feature serves a clear purpose.
**And do you know what keeps us motivated?** Our happy clients!

Throughout the entire project all I saw was sheer will to keep pushing forward and adapting to whatever the next request was. Terrific job and we couldn't have done it without you. Ola Olusoga, Vice President at WordPress
10. “If you think good design is expensive, you should look at the cost of bad design.”
Investing in great design might feel like a luxury, but in reality, it's a safeguard against something far more costly. Bad user experience. No conversions. Redesign (again).
If you think good design is expensive, you should look at the cost of bad design. Dr. Ralf Speth

Poor design confuses users, increases support costs, tanks conversion rates, and damages trust. It slows teams down, leads to rework, and ultimately stalls growth. So, bad design is invisible until it becomes a problem. And by then, you're not just spending money! You're losing opportunities.
Actually, we've seen it time and again. And teams spend months fixing what could've been solved with thoughtful design from the start.
**What Arounda team recommends**

items: Budget for UX early because fixing poor design after launch costs exponentially more than doing it right the first time.
Prioritize usability as a KPI.
Don't separate design from business. They're connected. Better design = better outcomes.
Redesign when the data says so. That's a design signal, not a product issue.

body.text: Our team designs for impact and helps founders and businesses avoid the hidden costs of poor design with clear, scalable, human-centered solutions. So, if you're just starting or need a strategic redesign, we make sure your product works for your users and reaches business goals.
Final Thoughts

These quotes weren't just words from experts. They were hard-earned insights from years of creating products that succeed because they're usable, clear, and human-centered. The best founders and product leaders understand that design is direction, not decoration. They make users feel something and do something. Faster, easier, and with joy.
Do you want your product to stand out? It needs more than good code or great features. It needs to connect, anticipate, guide, and delight the people using it. In short - great UX.
**So let's light a new star on the market!** [Contact us](https://arounda.agency/contact), and our experts will help you with the brightest part - meaningful and user-first digital experiences.

title: Top Mobile Menu Design Inspirations for 2026
author: Valeriia Serohina
excerpt: Do you know how to impress your users? Create a super cool mobile menu design so they can scroll through a sleek new app and instantly find that one feature they need. No frustration! Only the menu that just *gets* them. Effortless, intuiti

body.text: Do you know how to impress your users? Create a super cool mobile menu design so they can scroll through a sleek new app and instantly find that one feature they need. No frustration! Only the menu that just *gets* them. Effortless, intuitive, even a little delightful.
That’s not the magic, there are no secret keys, it’s just well-thought-out work.

Our [Arounda team](https://arounda.agency/about) scoured famous apps to bring you 10 outstanding mobile menu design examples. But that’s not all! We will also tell you some insights from our design cases to inspire you or explain how it all works. Let’s drive engagement, boost retention, and delight your users!
Why it matters for your business

items: Seamless user experience
Higher conversions
Stronger brand image
Better retention
Improved search rankings
Faster load times
Lower bounce rates
Competitive edge

body.text: Article Key Takeaways

In mobile apps, a menu is one of the first things to set the user experience. If it’s messy and hard to follow, people will leave out of frustration. With the amount of design patterns today, from bottom bars to gestures, you can’t always get it correct.

The secret sauce is to keep menus simple, clear, and aligned with how people actually use their phones. At Arounda, we have 9+ years of [product design](/) experience, and we have witnessed how the correct UX choices drive engagement and retention.

In this article, we compiled ten mobile menu design examples and described why each one is effective. We also offer our expert opinion on how those same principles apply in actual projects, and why good menu design is important for usability and business success.
The Importance of Mobile Menu Design in 2026
No matter what it is - a futuristic bottom navigation, a smart AI-driven menu, or a gesture-based UI, **they must feel like second nature**!
Mobile UX today is a strategic driver of engagement, conversions, and retention. And the opposite: a poorly structured menu leads to frustration, drop-offs, and lost revenue.
**Why we consider the design of mobile menu so important**

items: It is the gateway to your product, a first touch.
It impacts conversion rates and retention because navigation complexity is a conversion killer.

It adapts to user behaviors - mobile-first audience. Traditional hamburger menus are now being replaced or supplemented by bottom navigation bars, gesture-based interactions, floating action buttons (FABs), and AI-powered predictive menus.

It must meet SEO, core web vitals, and accessibility compliance. Google’s ranking factors emphasize mobile usability and accessibility, and compliance with [WCAG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/wcag3-intro/) (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) is also essential to accommodate users with different abilities.
It provides seamless omnichannel integration. The mobile menu should provide a fluid, frictionless journey that aligns with omnichannel UX strategies.

body.text: Well, if you care about your business - invest in user-centered mobile design. But to make the right decisions, let’s see what works and why (to analyze, inspire, and get ready).
Interesting Mobile Statistics
**74%** of users will return to a site that offers a good mobile UX
**55%** of global web traffic goes from mobile device
**40%** higher conversion rates with mobile-optimized sites
Top 10 Mobile Menu Design Examples
Carry about how not to lose customers? A frictionless menu can help. We have 10 famous examples that set new standards for usability and innovation.
1. Stripe: A Simple yet Powerful Sliding Menu

[Stripe](https://stripe.com) is an online payment processing platform that allows businesses to accept payments, manage subscriptions, and handle financial operations with ease. Despite its complex functionality, Stripe's mobile UX prioritizes clarity, ease of navigation, and quick access to key tools.
**Key features of Stripe’s mobile menu:**

items: Sliding sidebar navigation that appears on demand and keeps key options easily accessible.
Well-structured categories (clearly labeled sections) for quick access.
Minimalist yet informative design (clean aesthetic, monochrome color scheme, clear typography, and every option is logical and concise).
Seamless multi-level navigation (users can tap into different sections, and the interface smoothly transitions between categories).

body.text: **Arounda point!**
Stripe proves that even complex platforms can achieve a frictionless and intuitive UX through smart menu design.
2. Spotify: Minimalist Menu with Focused Search
[Spotify](https://open.spotify.com)'s design is a masterclass in simplicity and engagement. The interface prioritizes quick access to content and offers a clutter-free experience.
**Key features of Spotify’s mobile menu:**

items: Bottom navigation bar for core functions (no cognitive overload!).
The categorized browse sections enhance user experience by providing visual hierarchy and organization.
Consistent dark mode UI for readability and reducing eye strain.
Clean and engaging look with bold typography and vibrant category cards.
Intuitive gesture-based interaction or swipe-friendly navigation.
Quick access to search and music categories.

body.text: **Arounda point!**
Spotify’s mobile menu perfectly balances minimalism and usability, making it a benchmark for seamless mobile UX.
3. Airbnb: Sleek and Intuitive Dropdowns

[Airbnb](https://www.airbnb.com)’s design is a prime example of intuitive navigation combined with a visually appealing interface. It’s a platform for travelers worldwide, so it must be seamless, clear for everyone, and guide users effortlessly from exploration to booking.
**Key features of Airbnb’s mobile menu:**

items: Minimalist top navigation with smart dropdowns (clean and highly functional).
Progressive disclosure (users only see what’s necessary at each step).
Context-aware menu for personalized UX (the menu dynamically adjusts based on user intent).
Persistent bottom navigation for quick access (hybrid approach combines the best of dropdowns and fixed navigation bars).
Visual hierarchy and readability (ample spacing, clear typography, and well-structured sections).

body.text: **Arounda point!**
Airbnb demonstrates how thoughtful design can simplify complex interactions and make travel planning smooth and enjoyable.
4. Amazon: Multi-Level Navigation for Complex Menus

[Amazon](https://www.amazon.com) is the world’s largest e-commerce platform, offering everything from consumer goods to cloud services (AWS). It has millions of products across thousands of categories, so Amazon’s mobile UX must handle vast amounts of information and allow users to quickly find what they need.
**Key features of Amazon’s mobile menu:**

items: Expandable multi-level sidebar navigation.
Customized shopping experience.
Sticky search and cart icons for quick access.
Visual hierarchy and clear categorization.
Integration of account and order management (it’s a one-stop navigation hub for both purchasing and account management).
High-contrast text and large touch areas make navigation easy for all audiences.

body.text: **Arounda point!**
Amazon is a great example of a platform dealing with extensive content. It shows that even complex navigation can be user-friendly, scalable, and efficient.
5. TikTok: Icon-Driven Bottom Navigation

[TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/explore) design is built for speed, efficiency, and minimal friction. Unlike traditional text-heavy menus, TikTok has icon-driven bottom navigation. This design choice simplifies usability and keeps a strong focus on content engagement.
**Key features of TikTok’s mobile menu:**

items: Minimalist bottom navigation bar (a five-icon layout, placed at the bottom of the screen for thumb-friendly accessibility).
Swipe gestures instead of taps. Users can swipe up/down to explore videos, right/left to navigate creator profiles and tap to engage with content.
Strong visual hierarchy with high-contrast icons for immediate recognition without labels.
The central "+" button stands out with its bold color and larger sizing, showing its primary function.
Quick access to content discovery, creation, and interactions fuels TikTok’s addictiveness.
Thumb-friendly design (every essential action is within easy reach of the user’s thumb).

body.text: **Arounda point!**
No deep menus, no confusion. Just pure content-driven navigation. TikTok shows that a well-structured, minimalist design can enhance user experience and provide high engagement and accessibility.
6. Duolingo: Fun and Engaging Navigation Elements

What do we like in [Duolingo](https://www.duolingo.com)? It gamifies education and makes language acquisition interactive, engaging, and accessible. Its mobile UX motivates users, using playful visuals, progress tracking, and reward-based interactions.
**Key features of Duolingo’s mobile menu:**

items: Duolingo follows a five-icon bottom navigation layout, so users can easily switch between core sections of the app.
The bottom menu keeps all essential features within easy reach.
[UI design](/services/ui-ux-design) ensures users keep returning daily for lessons.
It uses vibrant colors, fun illustrations, and micro-animations to make navigation lively and engaging.
Icons often have subtle movements to reinforce actions and reward user progress.
The app keeps a visible progress bar at the top, showing how far users have advanced in their lessons (it motivates people and gives them a clear sense of achievement).
The mobile menu integrates daily streaks, leaderboards, rewards, and goal-setting. This approach turns boring language learning into an interactive challenge.

body.text: **Arounda point!**
Duolingo shows that user experience can be fun, delightful, and habit-forming with the right design.
7. Notion: Adaptive Mobile Menus for Productivity Apps

Individuals and teams use [Notion](https://www.notion.com) to organize tasks, manage documents, and create structured workflows. It has complex functionality, but the design focuses on adaptability and ease of navigation.
**Key features of Notion’s mobile menu:**

items: Adaptive sidebar for multi-level navigation
Swipe gestures to expand, collapse, and switch between pages (a very useful feature for users handling multiple projects at once).
Universal search for instant access.
Quick access toolbar for core actions (users can work efficiently on a small mobile screen).
Dark mode, customizable workspaces, and floating action buttons improve the overall user experience.

body.text: **Arounda point!**
Notion balances flexibility with simplicity. Even feature-rich productivity apps can have a user-friendly interface and support complex workflows at the same time.
8. Netflix: Personalized Content-Driven Navigation

[Netflix](https://www.netflix.com/ua-en/)’s success relies on personalized recommendations and a seamless user experience. It allows viewers to find and enjoy content without friction quickly. The mobile app menu design is content-first, personalized, and highly intuitive, with a focus on effortless content discovery.
**Key features of Netflix’s mobile menu:**

items: Netflix keeps things simple with a three-to-four icon at the bottom navigation bar.
AI-driven personalized content navigation.
Persistent mini-player for multitasking.
Gesture-based UI for quick interaction.
Strong visual hierarchy with auto-play previews

body.text: **Arounda point!**
With a content-first approach, highly personalized experience, and effortless discovery, users spend less time searching and more time watching.
9. Etsy: Category-Based Menus with a Creative Edge
[Etsy](https://www.etsy.com) is a global marketplace for handmade, vintage, and unique goods. Its mobile UX focuses on inspiring shopping experiences to help users find the perfect item.
**Key features of Etsy’s mobile menu:**

items: A five-icon bottom navigation system for quick access to the most important sections.
A well-structured category-based navigation.
Search functionality with image previews, trending collections, and AI-generated suggestions.
The "Sell on Etsy" section makes it easy for shop owners to manage listings, view analytics, and process orders.
Quick access to discounts and personalized recommendations.
Aesthetic UI with rich imagery makes shopping enjoyable.
Quick access to wishlists, deals, and favorites increases engagement.

body.text: **Arounda point!**
Shopping must be a delightful experience. Etsy has a creative and category-driven menu that proves that e-commerce navigation can be both functional and inspiring.
10. Uber: Simplified Menus for Quick Navigation

[Uber](https://www.uber.com/ua/en/) is a ride-hailing and mobility service that offers everything from standard rides to food delivery (Uber Eats) and micro-mobility options. People often use the app on the go, so speed, clarity, and frictionless interaction are very important here.
**Key features of Uber’s mobile menu:**

items: The bottom menu is lean and intuitive, with only essential options.
One-tap actions for speed.
Default options (like saved locations and preferred payment methods) streamline the process.
A live map view integration allows users to monitor trip progress, change destinations, and see driver details without digging into multiple menu layers.
The "Wallet" section is easily accessible, so users can manage payments, apply discounts, or split fares without confusion at checkout.
The black-and-white color scheme ensures clarity in bright and low-light conditions (especially useful for nighttime riders).
Users can book a ride, track their trip, or manage payments in just a few taps.

body.text: **Arounda point!**
Uber understands its audience, so the design is optimized for use in fast-paced environments where speed is critical.
