title: Brand Differentiation: A Strategic Method to Brand Success
author: Alyona Deieieva
excerpt: Every business wants to be recognized and even revered so that customers choose it over the competition every single time. But how do you do this? Create a strong brand differentiation strategy! It’s not only about a unique logo or an eye-c

body.text: Every business wants to be recognized and even revered so that customers choose it over the competition every single time. But how do you do this? Create a strong brand differentiation strategy! It’s not only about a unique logo or an eye-catching tagline. And it’s absolutely not with cliches like “We are innovation leaders,” “Tailored just for you,” or “We care …”!

Brand differentiation is about connecting your brand’s unique value proposition to your customers' everyday needs and desires. But here’s the pinch! During our 8+ years of experience, we at [Arounda](/) noticed that many businesses struggle to pinpoint what truly makes them different or fail to communicate it effectively. That’s why we are here to help. Ready to transform your brand?
**In this article:**

items: Learn how to craft a compelling brand identity.
Find out how important design is in the branding process.
Get insights and expert advice you can apply immediately to give your brand that unique edge.

body.text: Understanding Brand Differentiation

Nowadays, consumers have endless choices, right? So, you must clearly understand how to differentiate your brand, why it is critical for your business's success, and how it influences the way consumers perceive it. Let's find answers.
The Importance of Setting Your Business Apart
The main accent is on the customer's entire experience, not on a unique product or service (although it should be). **What does it include? **

items: Visual identity
Customer service
Marketing messages
Overall narrative that defines your brand

body.text: Differentiation carves out a niche for your business in the industry and creates a loyal customer base that feels connected to what your brand stands for.
How Brand Differentiation Impacts Consumer Perception
Do you want to differentiate your brand? Design a unique brand identity that resonates on an emotional level!
**Exercise:** Remember the emotions popular brands (Pepsi, Adidas, Volvo) offer. Now, think about what emotion your brand has or wants to create.

When consumers can easily identify (feel) what makes your brand different, they are more likely to choose your product/service over competitors. Is it easy to create a perception? Oh, definitely not. Perception is built through consistent messaging, unique brand elements, and experiences that reinforce your brand's unique selling propositions (USPs). Your task is not to make your brand noticed, but to make it remembered and preferred.
How all those things works? Well, take a look at the differentiation strategy examples to understand it better.
Examples of Effective Strategies
Apple’s design philosophy

Apple stands out due to its minimalist design and user-friendly interface. They applied design-centric and user-centric approaches (with clarity and consistency) to create a powerful brand image that appeals to a broad demographic. They have a strong and unchanged philosophy of “think different” and follow it in every element. This is about their way to success. Just look at the most valuable brands worldwide in 2025, where Apple took first place.
**Brand value in billions of US dollars**
**$340.4** Microsoft
**What can you learn?** Of course, you can’t repeat their way, and there is no need. Your main task is to make a difference!
Patagonia’s environmental commitment

Outdoor clothing giant Patagonia has differentiated itself through its strong commitment to environmental sustainability. This is their business model with strong environmental ethics (from sourcing sustainable materials to advocating for environmental causes). What has set the brand apart? Its philosophy, ethics, and processes (generally brand identity) resonate deeply with eco-conscious consumers.
**Patagonia**

items: Leadership
Workers
Monitoring
Emissions
Recycling
Initiatives
Giving
Activism
Truth
Striving

body.text: **What can you learn? **Know your audience, do market research, and be active and empathetic.
Spotify’s Personalization

Spotify has revolutionized the music streaming industry. It offers personalized playlists and recommendations. How Spotify differentiates itself? Showing how well it understands its users’ musical tastes and preferences. This brand uses data analytics to offer personalized music experiences (tailored playlists). This approach improved user engagement and set new industry standards for customer interaction.

**What can you learn? **The more personalized is your services/products, the more users love you will get. And one very important thing - tone of voice. Define it, and use it everywhere and every time (it’s how your brand sounds)!
Okay, you got a dose of inspiration from famous brands, and it’s time to do something. Let’s start from the very beginning - unique value proposition!
Identifying Your Unique Value Proposition

Your unique value proposition (UVP) captures what makes your business special and communicates the distinct value you offer that your competitors do not. Our Arounda experts offer you the step-by-step instruction of defining your brand's core values.
Defining Your Brand's Core Values

What are the brand's core values? They are the principles that guide every aspect of your business (from internal decisions to external communications), resonate deeply with your target audience, and reflect what your brand stands for. **Here's what you need to do to define them:**

items: **Reflect on your mission**

body.text: Consider why your company exists except to make a profit.
**Answer these questions:** What are the driving forces behind your business? How do you want to impact your customers and the wider community?

items: **Personify your brand**

body.text: Align your values with brand personality.
**Answer this question: **Is it professional, playful, innovative, or friendly?

items: **Look at past successes**

body.text: Identify what your audience liked earlier.
**Answer these questions:** Which products, services, or campaigns were most successful? What do they say about your brand values?

items: **Engage stakeholders**

body.text: Don't define your values alone.
**Answer this question: **What do your employees, customers, and other stakeholders think and feel your brand represents? It's important because they interact with the brand the most.

items: **Be clear about values **

body.text: Once you've defined your values, articulate them clearly. This will form the basis for all your branding efforts.
**Exercise:** Define your values and ask yourself if they are clear, have one exact meaning, and really represent your brand. Then, ask the same questions to your stakeholders.
Conducting Market Research to Find Opportunities for Differentiation
You should know the market! Market research helps you identify gaps your brand can fill and find opportunities for differentiation. **Here’s how you can do it:**

items: Analyze competitor offerings (products, services, marketing strategies, and customer feedback) to find areas where your brand could better meet consumer needs.
Survey potential customers (surveys, focus groups, and interviews) to gather user feedback about their needs, preferences, and perceptions of your brand versus competitors.
Stay updated with industry reports, news, and trends to catch the market shifts and align your differentiation strategies with market waves.
Conduct a **SWOT **analysis to see where your brand stands in the market and where it can excel.
Use data analytics tools to get customer data and insights into their behavior and preferences, revealing unique niches within the market that your brand can serve.

body.text: The next practical step is to design a brand identity. We have exciting insights for you!
Crafting a Compelling Brand Identity

A [compelling brand identity](/services/brand-identity) is everything that tells about your brand; it’s what people see, feel, and hear in every interaction your business has with the market. To craft a truly remarkable brand identity, you must develop a brand personality and design memorable visual elements.
Developing a Distinctive Brand Personality
Brand personality refers to the human characteristics associated with a brand. It influences how your customers feel about and interact with your offerings. **What you have to do:**

items: Decide what emotion you want your brand to evoke in your audience (trust, excitement, reliability, etc.). And remember that chosen emotion should be consistently reflected in all your communications!
Research your audience’s lifestyles, beliefs, and behaviors to align the brand’s personality with customer values (this is like a mirror of the values and expectations of your target audience).
Make sure that your brand personality is consistent across all platforms (from your website to social media to customer service) to avoid confusion.

Use** **storytelling to bring your brand’s personality to life. People love interesting stories, so don’t hesitate to tell stories that illustrate your brand’s values and mission. Storytelling makes your brand relatable and memorable, even if it is very technical!
Think of using frameworks like the Brand Archetype wheel to identify which archetypes closely align with your brand. This can help you guide your content's and interactions' tone and manner.

body.text: Designing Memorable Visual Elements

Memorable design can significantly enhance brand recognition and emotional connection with your audience. **But how to design it?** We will explain and even show you on our own case - [WordPress](https://case.arounda.agency/case/wordpress).

items: Design a simple yet iconic logo that is easily recognizable and universal across multiple media. It should reflect your brand's personality and values at a glance.

Learn more about color psychology! Choose colors that reflect the emotions and traits you want associated with your brand. Blue is associated with trust and stability, while orange - is with creativity and enthusiasm.
Choose typography that matches your brand's personality. The right font can convey seriousness, whimsy, elegance, or friendship. Make sure it's readable regardless of size or medium.

Develop a visual theme that ties all your visual elements together (website design, social media graphics, marketing materials, product packaging, etc.). Consistency makes your brand recognizable, and this is also your brand identity!
Design must be an iterative process! Gather feedback and be ready to changes again and again to stay relevant and engaging.

Invest in [professional design services](/). Professional designers provide insights and expertise, know current trends, conduct competitor and market research correctly, and finally, save your time and budget on unnecessary or ineffective processes.

body.text: Arounda design tips

items: Be consistent, not repetitive
Avoid clutter in your designs, make it simple
Design with the emotional connection in mind
Infuse deeper meaning into your logos and symbols
Choose a typeface that reinforces your brand personality
Regularly collect feedback and be willing to make adjustments

body.text: Doubt the role of design in the differentiation of your brand? Well, let's talk about design influence.
Design’s Influence on Building Brand Identity

Did you know that [55%](https://institute.uschamber.com/what-makes-a-good-first-impression/) of brand first impressions are visual? As expert designers, we confidently say that design is a fundamental tool for building a strong, coherent brand identity that engages and retains customers. Let’s explore different aspects of design that contribute to forming a brand’s identity.
Visual Identity and Consistency

Visual identity is synonymous with your brand. It includes a logo, color palette, typography, and imagery. Design elements create a visual language that communicates your brand's ethos and mission without words. **Here's how you can do it:**

items: Develop a visual strategy harmonizing all visual elements to project a unified image. To strengthen your market position, people should feel this strategic alignment in all branding materials.
Introduce dynamic elements in your visual design that adapt to different contexts, keep the core identity, and provide freshness without losing familiarity.
Apply visual positioning techniques that match your brand with desired market perceptions (luxury, reliability, innovation, etc.) through deliberate design choices in color and form.
Prepare** **comprehensive brand guidelines detailing the usage of visual elements in all materials and media.

body.text: Take a look at one of our Arounda brand identity work.
Find more examples and inspirations [here](https://dribbble.com/arounda_branding).
User Experience (UX) and Interface Design
[Advanced UX and UI design](/services/ui-ux-design) set meaningful connections with users. Make an accent on intuitive, seamless, and rewarding interactions with your brand. **How to do it:**

items: Incorporate principles of behavioral science to guide user behavior through design. It will improve user engagement and drive desired actions.
Design interfaces that simplify complexity and reduce cognitive load.
Craft designs that are accessible to all users (including those with disabilities), and ensure your brand is inclusive and compliant with global standards (WCAG, EAA, etc.).
Make sure your digital presence is fully functional across all devices and platforms. It is called responsive design and must be a rule for every product/service design!
Regularly test different designs (A/B testing) with real segments of your audience to refine elements that best resonate with users.

body.text: Interested in seeing real-world examples? Take a look at our [works](/works).
Arounda expert tips

items: **Data visualization** Apply data visualization techniques to communicate complex information simply and attractively.
**Adaptability & customization** Design brand elements that adapt contextually to different cultures or market segments, showcasing sensitivity and customization.
**Predictive analytics** Develop interfaces that anticipate user actions and streamline user flows based on predictive analytics.
**AI technologies for UI** Employ AI technologies to create adaptive and intelligent UIs that evolve based on user behavior and preferences.

body.text: Packaging and Physical Product Design

The design of packaging and physical products does more than hold your goods! It demonstrates the essence of your brand, is a critical touchpoint for customer interaction, and creates the first physical impression. **What you should pay attention to:**

items: **Sensory Design**. The tactile and visual appeal of your packaging creates a memorable first impression that invites engagement.
**Eco-Innovative Design**. Use sustainable design practices that reflect environmental responsibility to connect with the eco-conscious consumer.
**Functional Aesthetics**. Combine aesthetics with functionality in your product design to solve consumer problems in stylish, innovative ways.

body.text: Brands with Strong Design-Led Differentiation

We want to show you some examples of brands that excel in design-led differentiation. These brands demonstrate that effective design is about visually striking design and embedding design thinking into the core of a brand's identity.
Google
Google's products, such as Google Search and Google Maps, underscore its mission to make powerful technology accessible and easy to use. Its UI design is simple and clear.
Apple
Apple leads the tech industry in part because of its emphasis on sleek, user-friendly design, which extends to products, software, and physical stores.
Coca-Cola
The company's distinctive script logo, dynamic ribbon, and consistent use of red strengthen brand recognition.
Nike
Nike's logo is simple yet powerful. Its product lines focus on design, and through both function and form, the company speaks directly to athletes and sports enthusiasts.
Visual is a great tool, but don't forget about communication!
Communicating Your Differentiation Strategy

The next step after design is creating effective communication to reinforce your brand’s unique market position. Focus also on creating consistent brand messaging and using multiple channels to reach your intended audience.
Creating Consistent Brand Messaging
Consistent brand messaging means that every piece of content you produce reinforces your brand’s unique value proposition and core values. **How to do it?**

items: Develop a messaging framework that outlines key messages, tone, and language guidelines. This framework is a reference for all brand communications.
Use** **storytelling to make your brand messaging more engaging and memorable. Craft stories that embody your brand’s values and differentiation points.
Ensure that everyone in your company understands and can express differentiation strategy. This internal alignment strengthens your brand voice across all touchpoints.
Gather customer feedback on your messaging and adjust your strategy based on this input to keep it relevant and impactful.

body.text: Take a look at our two different works with different communication styles.
This one is enthusiastic and innovative.
And this one is lively and cheerful.
Leveraging Multiple Channels for Maximum Impact
You can find your target audience even in places you didn't expect. That’s why we recommend using multiple communication channels. **How you can do it:**

items: Adopt an integrated marketing approach that coordinates your messaging across all channels (from digital marketing to traditional advertising and public relations). Create your brand’s voice.

Harness the power of SEO, content marketing, and social media to make your differentiation messages visible and catch the place where your audience spends their time online. But don’t forget to tailor content to fit the unique format and audience of each channel.
Participate in or host events that align with your brand identity and values. It’s your opportunity to showcase your unique value proposition and expand your audience.
Form partnerships with other brands or influencers who share similar values or have access to your target audience. It’s about additional credibility to your brand.
Use data analytics to personalize your messaging to different audience segments.

body.text: What’s next?
Implementing Differentiation Across Your Business

Every element of your organization must align with your unique brand identity, but how can you do it? Integrate branding differentiation into product development and train your team to embody your brand's unique identity.
Integrating Branding Differentiation into Product Development
Product development is not just about creating products or services; it's about bringing your brand's unique value proposition to every offering. **Here's what we recommend to do:**

items: Develop unique features or enhancements that address specific customer needs not met by competitors.
Involve your customers in the product development process (through feedback loops, beta testing, or crowd-sourced ideas).
If your differentiation relies on sustainability, make sure that this is reflected in your product development (from sourcing materials to production processes).
Encourage collaboration between departments (marketing, R&D, sales) because all aspects of the product must reflect the differentiation strategy.

body.text: Training Your Team to Embody Your Brand's Unique Identity
Your employees are ambassadors of your brand! Their understanding and execution of your brand's identity are very important, so don't hesitate to train them. **Here's how you can do this:**

items: Organize brand training workshops.
Reward brand-aligned behaviors.
Communicate consistently in different ways (internal newsletters, intranets, meetings, etc.).
Implement feedback systems for employees to get their insights or concerns.

body.text: And finally, the last stage is measuring the impact.
Measuring the Impact and Adapting Your Strategy

Key metrics will show you the effectiveness (or not) of your differentiation strategy so you can continue this path or make adjustments based on those insights. That's why we recommend not to hesitate to measure and refine your differentiation strategy.
Key Metrics for Evaluating Brand Differentiation
We gather several key metrics that can provide insight into how well your brand stands out in the marketplace.

items: Brand awareness
Retention rates
Conversion rates
Market share
Customer satisfaction index
Engagement rates

body.text: Making Adjustments to Enhance Your Brand's Distinctiveness
​​Based on the metrics, you can continue the processes (if everything goes great) or find areas where your brand can be improved. **Here's how:**

items: If brand awareness is low, make messaging clearer and more impactful. Analyze your audience and what doesn't work.
Consider market share insights to continuously innovate your products/services and keep your brand relevant.
Improve the customer experience at every touchpoint (better train staff, improve service levels, fine-tune products, etc.).

Don't be afraid of a [redesign](/solutions/product-redesign) (branding, all design, marketing materials, or updating your digital presence) if you've tried everything and are still unsatisfied with the results.

body.text: Differentiation as a Path to Long-Term Brand Success

A well-executed differentiation strategy provides a sustainable competitive advantage because it delivers real value to consumers, fosters emotional connections with customers, and justifies premium pricing strategies. This strategy also increases brand loyalty and advocacy. But there is no time to relax as it requires ongoing innovation and adaptation to stay ahead.
Final Thoughts

Differentiation is the heart and soul of your brand. It turns everyday interactions into emotional connections. Your brand should have a [unique identity](/services/brand-identity), consistently deliver on promises, connect deeply with your audience, and turn transactions into relationships.

We’re sure that you can do everything, but if you doubt, or want to save your time, our Arounda team is here to provide expert help and make your brand truly unique. Ready to set your brand apart? [Contact us](/contact) today!

title: SPA vs MPA: Which Web Architecture is Best for Your Startup
author: Andrii Medintsev
excerpt: You are a startup founder or tech leader; you're juggling a million decisions, and each one is critical to your success. You worry about every step you take, doubt if it works for your business or not. Sounds familiar? Now, you have to choo

body.text: You are a startup founder or tech leader; you're juggling a million decisions, and each one is critical to your success. You worry about every step you take, doubt if it works for your business or not. Sounds familiar? Now, you have to choose the right architecture for your app. It can set the stage for long-term success or future headaches.

You've probably heard about Single-Page Applications (SPAs) and Multi-Page Applications (MPAs), but which one is the right fit for your startup? It's not only a technical choice; it's about how your product feels to users, how fast it can scale, and how easily you can manage it down the line. Our [Arounda team](/) has 8+ years of experience, and we will help you decide. We will tell you everything you need to know about SPA vs MPA, and by the end of this article, you'll feel confident in choosing the architecture that will drive your startup's success.
In this article:

items: Find out the difference between SPA and MPA architecture.
Explore design and development considerations for single-page and multi-page applications.
Learn everything you need to know about these architecture types to make informed decisions.

body.text: Introduction to Single-Page and Multi-Page Web Models

The choice of web application architecture significantly impacts user experience, performance, and future scalability. Depending on startup goals and technical needs, SPAs and MPAs have distinct strengths and ideal use cases.
Definition of SPAs and MPAs

**A Single-Page Application (SPA)** is a web application that loads a single HTML page and dynamically updates content as users interact with the app. Instead of reloading entire pages, only the necessary components change. SPA creates a seamless, fast, and responsive experience.

**A Multi-Page Application (MPA)** consists of multiple pages, where each new interaction or request from the user leads to a full-page refresh. MPAs are the traditional web model. Each function or category of the website has its own dedicated page.
Key differences

items: Offers fast, seamless, and interactive user experience with minimal disruptions.
Reduces page reloads and provides near-instant interactions. Loads a single HTML page, and content is dynamically updated without page refreshes.
Can feel faster to users because the app doesn’t reload entire pages. However, SPAs may require more initial loading time, especially complex ones.
Often requires additional setup (server-side rendering or prerendering) to be fully optimized for search engines.
Is easier to scale for apps that rely on user interaction and need to load data without reloading the page.
More emphasis on the front end. Needs a more complex frontend setup and heavy reliance on JavaScript frameworks.
Has smooth navigation without traditional page reloads and looks more like a desktop application.
Offers a structured, clear, and organized user experience, but is slower because it refreshes the entire page as users navigate.
Each new interaction results in a full-page reload.
Is sometimes slower during navigation but can load faster initially due to its segmented content-loading structure.
Has excellent SEO performance thanks to unique URLs for each page that are easily crawled by search engines.
Is better suited for large-scale websites with vast content across different categories or functions.
Needs more backend logic with individual pages requiring separate rendering.
Has traditional navigation with clear page reloads. It’s ideal for complex or content-heavy sites.

body.text: Single page app vs multi page app examples

Let’s look at Google’s Gmail. It’s an ideal example of an SPA. When you open the app, every interaction (from opening emails to switching folders) is smooth and instantaneous without page reloads. Opposite is BBC News as a clear example of an MPA. It has different articles, sections, and categories. Such multi page application delivers a more traditional, content-heavy web experience.
Single-page app

items: Gmail
Trello
Spotify Web Player
Netflix
Facebook

body.text: Multi-page app

items: BBC News
Amazon
Wikipedia
Airbnb
eBay

body.text: Architecture and Performance

Deciding between SPA app and MPA app? Pay attention to the technical architecture. Because it affects how the application handles requests, processes data, and delivers content. We will discuss their technical differences, compare performance, and explain how architecture affects the user experience.
SPA architecture and how it differs from MPA

**Single-page applications** follow a client-side rendering model, where the entire application is loaded upfront or incrementally as users interact with it. We recommend using common JavaScript frameworks: React, Angular, and Vue.js.
Key components of SPA architecture include client-side rendering (CSR), routing, and state management.

items: CSR involves rendering content in the browser, with further content fetched through AJAX calls to APIs.
The router handles client-side routing. It allows the app to dynamically load new components when URLs change (even if the user remains on the same HTML page).

State management libraries (Redux or Vuex) keep the app's state synchronized across components and user interactions, so this type of architecture is a versatile and efficient solution for large applications.

body.text: SPA's pros & cons
Pros

items: Fast, interactive user experience after the first load.
Efficient API calls and component-specific data retrieval.
Rich UI features such as drag and drop, infinite scrolling, and real-time updates without reloading the page.

body.text: Cons

items: Slower initial loading, especially for large applications.
Requires additional configuration to optimize for SEO.
Heavy reliance on JavaScript can create performance bottlenecks if not managed properly.

body.text: **Multi-page applications** follow a server-side rendering (SSR) model. It means that each page is fully rendered on the server before being sent to the client. The server processes the request, gathers necessary data, and returns a fully-rendered HTML page for each navigation interaction to a new page.

MPAs use server-side routing, so each time a user clicks a link or submits a form, the server handles the navigation and sends back a new page. While MPAs are often faster for initial load, each navigation-requiring interaction incurs a round-trip to the server, causing full page reloads. It can result in a slower and more fragmented user experience than SPAs.
MPA's pros & cons
Pros

items: Easy to implement SEO, as each page has a unique URL and metadata.
Easier to manage the state as each page is independent of the others.
Better suited for large websites with individual, content-rich pages.

body.text: Cons

items: Completely reloading a page leads to slower navigation and potentially lower performance.
The user experience can feel disjointed due to frequent load interruptions.
Repeated data retrieval can lead to increased bandwidth usage.

body.text: Performance comparison

**SPAs** offer fast, fluid experiences after the initial page load, with data fetched and rendered dynamically in the background via AJAX or other asynchronous methods. They can suffer from slower initial load times, but lazy loading strategies can mitigate this. User interactions are nearly instantaneous, and SPAs often use modern browser caching mechanisms to minimize future load times.

**MPAs** load individual pages faster due to their optimization for specific functions, but this introduces latency that may affect user experience. Initial load time is faster for MPAs, but subsequent interaction speed is slower due to server-side rendering. MPAs also benefit from server-side caching mechanisms, but this may cause more interruptions in content flow due to separate page reloads.
For a better understanding

Imagine you're at a coffee shop with an MPA architecture. Each time you want to place an order, you must get back in line, submit a new order, and wait for the barista to make your drink from scratch.
In a SPA coffee shop, you wave to the barista and boom—your coffee order is updated without you ever leaving your seat.
Impact of architecture on user experience

SPAs create a more engaging experience in real-time. Users don't need to wait for the entire page to reload. They feel more in control. This is important for applications requiring constant interaction. MPAs feel more organized and predictable. They're ideal for users who are focused more on content consumption or step-by-step navigation.
Which Web Architecture is Best for Your Startup?
You should define your startup’s goals, the type of application you’re building, and your target users. And then use our quick guide to decide!
**Choose an SPA if:**

items: Your product relies on real-time interactions (for example, live chat, social media, task management apps).
You want to deliver a smooth, app-like experience with minimal page reloads.
You can handle the extra technical complexity of optimizing for SEO and managing app state across sessions.

body.text: **Choose an MPA if:**

items: Your website is content-heavy, and SEO is a priority (for example, e-commerce sites and news platforms).
You need a more traditional, step-by-step navigation flow for users (for instance, multi-step forms and checkout processes).
You want easier, more straightforward development and scalability for large-scale, multi-function websites.

body.text: Arounda tip
If you can't decide between the two, consider a hybrid approach. Use an SPA for highly interactive parts of your application, and an MPA for content-heavy or SEO-critical pages.
User Experience and Interactivity

Users and their goals must be your main priority to reach success! That’s why you should care about the user experience and interactivity. The app's architecture influences performance and user interaction quality. Let’s discover how to do everything right.
User experience

**SPAs** provide a smooth, fluid user experience by updating only the necessary data on the page, avoiding jarring page reloads. Real-time data fetching and dynamic content updates create an app-like experience in a browser. But this can cause a heavier initial load, causing a slight delay in first-time interactions.

**MPAs** offer an excellent UX with linear and hierarchical navigation. Each new page serves a distinct function and provides users with a clear beginning, middle, and end of their journey. MPAs excel in environments with traditional web experiences. But full page reloads can lead to longer wait times during navigation.
At Arounda, we know how to create a perfect UX and we will be glad to share it with you! Just [take a look](/works).
Interactivity and responsiveness

**SPA **provides a high level of interactivity and responsiveness. It’s ideal for applications requiring frequent user input or data updates. SPAs handle interactions entirely on the client side, meaning clicks, form submissions, and other user actions are processed instantly without waiting for the server to respond. This architecture often uses animations or subtle effects to maintain continuity (it’s more engaging for users).

**MPA** offers robust functionality but lacks the same level of responsiveness as SPAs. Each interaction requires communication with the server to fetch a new page, so there’s often a slight delay as the entire page reloads. MPAs are not for users who expect real-time updates, but they are perfect in environments where user interaction is more transactional or informational.
Main point

items: SPAs offer superior interactivity for apps that require real-time data updates and user actions (e.g., collaboration tools, live chat, dynamic dashboards).
MPAs are suitable for applications where user interactions are more predictable and content-driven (e.g., online stores or CMS).

body.text: Considerations for designing user interfaces in each model
**Designing for SPAs, we recommend:**

items: Focus on transitions and feedback. Use animations, loading indicators, or skeleton screens to let users know when content is updated or fetched in the background.
Make sure that your SPA is optimized for performance. Implement lazy loading for non-critical resources, compressing assets, and minimizing the use of large JavaScript libraries.
Use libraries like Redux or Vuex. They guarantee that the UI updates consistently without errors as users interact with the app.
Adopt a mobile-first design approach to remain consistent with the experience across devices.

body.text: **Designing for MPAs, we recommend:**

items: Provide a clear navigation structure. Users should always know where they are on the site and how to return to previous pages. Breadcrumbs, navigation bars, and footer links play a vital role here.
Focus on server-side optimizations like caching, pre-rendering, and reducing database query times to minimize the time it takes for new pages to load.
Ensure each page has properly structured metadata, optimized images, and fast loading times to improve search engine rankings.
Maintain consistency in design elements like typography, color schemes, and layout.

body.text: Development Considerations

The choice between a Single-Page Application and a Multi-Page Application significantly impacts development, testing, debugging, scalability, and maintenance. Our expert will show you technical nuances, challenges, and best practices.
Development process
**SPA development process**

SPAs are user-friendly applications that rely on client-side technologies, with much of the logic handled in the browser. The development process focuses on creating a dynamic, interactive frontend supported by APIs for data fetching. Most SPAs are built using JavaScript frameworks like React, Angular, or Vue.js. This allows developers to create reusable components and manage the state efficiently.

The backend, typically RESTful or GraphQL, serves as a data provider, allowing developers to design an API that delivers data to the frontend while keeping business logic in the backend. SPAs often handle real-time updates, with technologies like WebSockets to provide a more responsive and interactive user experience.
**MPA development process**

MPAs are backend-focused web applications, with each page rendered server-side and sent to the client as a complete HTML document. Developers use PHP, Ruby on Rails, Django, or ASP.NET technologies to create more traditional web development workflows.

They also need to optimize server response times and fast page loading. For this task, caching mechanisms, SSR, and database query optimization are great. SEO optimization is also a key aspect of MPA development, as each page generates distinct URLs, requiring proper metadata, optimized images, and fast loading times to rank well in search engines.
Testing and debugging differences
**Testing and debugging in SPAs**

items: Tools like Jest (for React) and Mocha (for Vue.js) help developers isolate and test individual components to ensure that they work as expected both independently and as part of the overall app.

Because SPAs manage most of their data and state on the client side, testing state transitions (with libraries like Redux or Vuex) is critical to avoid bugs in how data flows through the app. This also includes testing asynchronous data fetching to ensure API calls are handled correctly.
Use browser developer tools (like Chrome DevTools) to inspect the DOM, monitor network requests, and debug JavaScript errors in real time.

body.text: **Testing and debugging in MPAs**

items: MPAs require testing server-side rendering, database queries, and API responses. Tools like RSpec (for Ruby on Rails) and JUnit (for Java) help automate these tests.
Automated UI testing tools (like Selenium or Cypress) can help ensure that forms, navigation links, and interactive elements function correctly across the app.
Use tools like Google Lighthouse to test page performance, SEO readiness, and accessibility.

body.text: Scalability and maintenance considerations
**SPAs**

items: SPAs can scale well with new features and components due to JavaScript framework modularity. However, managing frontend state and asynchronous data fetching can become challenging, requiring state management tools (Redux or MobX).
API-driven SPAs improve scalability by decoupling APIs and introducing microservices for specific functionality. This enables independent scaling of individual application parts.

SPAs require complex maintenance due to JavaScript reliance, client-side routing, state management, and API integrations. Regular updates to JavaScript frameworks like React or Vue ensure compatibility.

body.text: **MPAs**

items: Scaling the backend requires additional server resources for individual page requests, often necessitating horizontal scaling. Tools like load balancers and Content Delivery Networks help distribute loads and reduce latency.
MPAs are ideal for content-heavy websites. They allow easy page addition without affecting architecture, seamless integration with CMS, and individual page optimization for performance.
MPAs are easier to maintain for small to medium-sized websites due to their independent functionality, but maintaining design consistency can become challenging as the application grows.

body.text: Key point

items: SPAs are ideal for interactive applications because they focus on managing frontend complexity and client-side state.
MPAs are easier to maintain and scale content-wise but rely heavily on server-side optimizations for scalability and performance.

body.text: Design for different types of applications
The design process presents different challenges, and choosing the right type of architecture will impact your app's usability, scalability, and user satisfaction.
Common design challenges for SPAs

items: SPAs require responsive, intuitive UI design for dynamic user interaction. Provide clear visual cues and seamless transitions to keep the user aware of changing contexts.
SPAs face challenges informing users about app updates (including loading indicators, progress bars, and instant feedback) while managing state changes and ensuring a smooth experience.
SPAs can experience slow initial load times. Design strategies like skeleton screens or lazy loading can reduce perceived load times and improve user satisfaction.

Designers should create clear hierarchies, breadcrumbs, tabs, and persistent navigation bars to guide users through dynamic content. We also suggest using modular components and subtle animations to create a sense of fluidity.

body.text: Ensuring design consistency across multiple pages in MPAs

items: A design system or style guide ensures uniformity in typography, colors, and UI components across all pages, especially for large-scale websites with multiple teams working on different parts.

MPAs require frequent page reloads. Designers must align layouts and navigation elements for smooth transitions (especially in multi-step processes like shopping carts, sign-ups, or multi-step forms).
MPAs require flexible layouts for various purposes. Arounda experts suggest creating grid systems, defining layout templates, and establishing clear spacing, padding, and alignment guidelines.
Traditional navigation systems are complex and can cause user confusion. Use mega menus, breadcrumbs, and sidebars for structured access and predictive search for quick content discovery.
To create purposeful micro-interactions across multiple pages, use subtle hover effects, button animations, and scroll-triggered transitions.

body.text: Designing for SPA and MPA requires deep expertise and understanding of how architecture affects user interaction and experience. Faced with design challenges? We offer a helping [UI/UX](/services/ui-ux-design) hand!
Considerations for choosing the right model

The right web architecture directly impacts your app's performance, UX, and design approach. Your decision should match your business goals, user expectations, and design vision. Here's a quick summary of key differences.
SPA

items: Seamless, real-time user interaction
Requires optimization
Fast post-initial load
Best for feature-rich apps
Dynamic content, transitions
Frontend-focused, JavaScript-heavy

body.text: MPA

items: Structured, traditional user interaction
SEO-friendly
Quick initial load, slower navigation
Ideal for content-heavy sites
Consistency across multiple pages
Backend-heavy, simpler to manage

body.text: But if you are still comparing MPA vs SPA, have doubts, and can't choose - [contact us today](/contact)! Our Arounda expert design and development team will guide you toward the best solution for your business to create a flawless user experience!

title: How To Design Products With Goal-directed Design
author: Valeriia Serohina
excerpt: What should you have for designing a product that will win the market? A keen eye for aesthetics, a checklist of features, or a repetitive plan of your competitors? No, you should have an empathetic understanding of your users, their motiva

body.text: What should you have for designing a product that will win the market? A keen eye for aesthetics, a checklist of features, or a repetitive plan of your competitors? No, you should have an empathetic understanding of your users, their motivations, and the challenges they face. It's key that [we](/) (designers) name "goal-directed design". This is a methodology that places users' objectives at the core of your product development process to ensure that every feature, interaction, and design decision matches with what truly matters to them.

Your main task is not to develop a product but to create a digital solution that becomes an integral part of users' daily lives, and they will love it. [Our experts](/about) decided to help you with this and gathered all essential information on goal directed design and how to do it for your product.
In this article:

items: Find out how goal-directed design leads to higher user satisfaction and better business results.
Learn how to understand your users 100%.
Get practical tips to guide you in your own design process.

body.text: What Is Goal-Directed Design?

Goal-directed design is a user-centered approach with accent on understanding and addressing end users' goals. It focuses on how a product fits into users' lives and helps them achieve their desired outcomes effectively. Firstle, we analyze user behavior, motivations, and pain points. Then, it is important to define user personas to represent users' goals, frustrations, and needs. Focusing on real data and insights derived from user observation, we will avoid designing for hypothetical users.
Goal-directed design

items: User goals as a top priority
Persona development
Scenario-based approach
Problem-solving
Iterative user testing
Contextual fit
Value Creation

body.text: Simple design

items: Surface-level features
Generic user profiles (assumptions)
Feature-driven approach
Visual aesthetics
Assumption-based design
One-size-fits-all
Ease of Build

body.text: Types of User Goals

Each person is an individual with feelings, emotions, lifestyle, and hobbies, right? The same is true of goal-directed design! Understanding the various types of user goals is important and helpful to crafting an experience that meets user needs, improves their experience, influences [retention](/blog/how-to-increase-customer-retention-and-get-more-profit-from-your-saas), and reaches business goals. There are three main user goals: experience, end, and life goals. If you know how to work with them, you can design more effectively and deliver product value in a meaningful way.
Experience Goals

Experience goals are the emotional and sensory desires users have while interacting with a product. These goals can include feeling confident, avoiding frustration, or enjoying a pleasant, effortless experience.
**Your main question here: **"How do users want to feel?".

Imagine you create a financial app. What goals may users have? For example, control over their finances or confidence in the platform's security. Clear data visualization, simple workflows, and accessible support channels are the design elements that help achieve these goals.
What's important
A strong emotional connection is vital for user retention and loyalty.
End Goals

End goals are specific outcomes users want to achieve through a product (e.g., buy something, schedule a meeting, or learn a new skill). They are the primary reason users engage with a product: they have a task and want a solution that efficiently gets them to the finish line.
**Your main question here: **"What task does the user want to accomplish?".

Imagine you design an e-commerce website that sells laptops, PCs, smartphones, etc. Make it easy for users to compare products, add them to the cart, and complete the purchase without confusion or unnecessary steps.
What's important
Users want to find value in your product, and meeting end goals effectively will determine if they come back to the website or app.
Life Goals

Life goals are long-term aspirations that users want to achieve that go beyond their immediate interaction with a product. These goals are closely related to their identity, motivation, and values. They may include improving health, achieving professional success, or developing meaningful relationships.
**Your main question here: **"How will my product affect the future of people?".

For example, what is the life goal of designers who use the design tool? Probably, building a successful freelance career. How will your tool help them achieve this goal? By promoting creativity, effective project management, and easy client communication. If you meet the users' long-term vision, you can ensure the tool remains an essential part of their lives. What will you get? Increased engagement and loyalty!
What's important

You should create a product that will stay with users for a long time and help them achieve their goals again and again by adding new features, redesigning due to new trends, collecting feedback for improvements, and so on.
Research for Goals

The main rule of a goal-directed design is understanding user needs, motivations, and behaviors. Successful products balance user satisfaction with business viability and technical feasibility. There are several goal types, and now we offer you different techniques and tools for qualitative research.
Life Goals
Life goals research helps understand a user's identity and long-term aspirations. If it is qualitative, your product design will increase user loyalty and engagement.

Business Goals

It's about the organization's objectives for a product (profitability, market share, user acquisition, brand positioning, and differentiation). They help match the design with the company's strategic aims and offer appropriate features.

body.text: But how to uncover the root cause behind user behavior and decisions? How to avoid the surface-level issues and get a deeper understanding of the real purposes and motivations behind users' actions? The best technique we use and can recommend is the **5 Whys.**
Technique 5 Whys for Right Understanding User Real Purposes
The 5 Whys methodology is a structured research method that aims to understand the underlying purpose or motivation behind user problems.
**Here’s how it works:**

items: Identify a problematic user behavior or statement.
Ask ‘Why’ to understand user behavior. (Why are the users behaving that way? Remember that the first answer is usually a surface-level explanation).
Continue asking “why” about each subsequent answer until you reach the underlying user goal or purpose (Typically, five times).

body.text: **Let’s look at an example of the 5 Whys in practice.**
Imagine you are working on improving the onboarding experience for a productivity app and notice that users are not completing the process.
**1st Why**:
**Why** are users not completing the onboarding process?
The answer can be, “Users find the onboarding steps too long and overwhelming.”
**2nd Why**:
**Why** do users find the onboarding steps overwhelming?
The answer can be, “The onboarding asks for too much information at once, and it makes them feel overwhelmed.”
**3rd Why**:
**Why** does asking for too much information make them feel overwhelmed?
The answer can be, “Users want to start using the app immediately and don’t see the immediate value of giving all that information upfront.”
**4th Why**:
**Why** do users want to start using the app immediately?
The answer can be, “They have a specific task or goal they want to achieve right away and see the onboarding as a barrier to getting started.”
**5th Why**:
**Why** is it important for users to achieve that task right away?
Users feel that productivity apps should save time, not consume it, and they expect to get value from the app immediately.

So, we found out that the primary user goal is **to start** using the app **immediately**. What should you do? Enhance user productivity without delays, enable a quicker onboarding process that focuses on essential steps, and allow users to skip the onboarding and come back later if needed. Only now can you start the design process or [redesign](/solutions/product-redesign) your product.
**Benefits of using the 5 Whys technique**

items: Reveals deeper motivations
Aligns design with real needs
Identifies clear direction for improvement
Reduces false perceptions

body.text: **Arounda Tips for Effectively Applying the 5 Whys**

items: Be non-judgmental. Users must feel comfortable explaining their reasoning to get to the root of the problem.
Base your questions on real data from user interviews, usability testing, or customer feedback.
Collaborate with team members.
Know when to stop. Although the technique is called the 5 Whys, the number is a guideline. Sometimes, you need fewer or more iterations to uncover the root cause.
Focus on goals, not symptoms, to create value beyond simply fixing surface issues.

body.text: Interested how the final results look like? Welcome to [our case studies](/works) to see what is this “goal-directed design”. And now it’s time to uncover the entire goal-directed design process!
How to Design Useful Products with Goal-Centered Design?

The goal-centered approach helps create functional, useful, and enjoyable products, emphasizing effective [user interface design](/services/ui-ux-design) as a key component. We offer the following plan for designing useful products.
**Step 1**
Develop detailed personas according to user research, and try to understand why users want your product.
**Step 2**
Build scenarios that reflect real-world situations in which people will use your product and prioritize the features that will help them reach their goals.
**Step 3**
Try to make tasks simple and reduce complexity in the [UI design](/services/ui-ux-design). Avoid overloading the interface with features or decorations that do not serve the user's purpose.
**Step 4**

Provide well-thought-out guidance (e.g., onboarding tips, tooltips, or gamification elements) and immediate informative feedback (e.g., a confirmation message or visual change when the user completes the task).
**Step 5**
Create an [adaptive UI](/services/ui-concept) and multiple pathways to goal achievement because everyone is different, including their needs and convenient process styles.
**Step 6**
Conduct usability testing and iterate based on feedback to optimize the product and better serve users' objectives.
**Step 7**
Align design with business and technical goals to ensure that the product delivers value to both users and stakeholders.
Interesting UI/UX Statistics
**200%** A well-designed user interface can increase conversion rates by almost
**400%** A flawless UX can give an impressive increase of up to
Useful Products Design Process

All businesses want to craft a useful and successful product. To do so, you have to develop a structured process that meets all aspects of user and business goals. If we compare traditional design approaches to goal-centered approaches, the first prioritizes aesthetics or trends, and the second focuses on delivering true value. At Arounda, we love the second one. Now, let's discover the key stages of the design process.
1. Research
Explore user behaviors, needs, and pain points. We conduct research in three stages:

items: Stakeholder interviews
User interviews and ethnographic studies
Competitive analysis

body.text: Why deep research is so important? Because designing features based on assumptions or general design biases will not solve the real users' problems.
2. Modeling

The next step is modeling, where you should develop personas representing user archetypes (demographics, behaviors, goals, and frustrations). Then, think about scenarios and use cases that depict real-world situations. And one more thing—the "one-size-fits-all" approach doesn't work anymore!
3. Requirements Definition
Identify product requirements from user research and scenarios and divide them into three categories:

items: **Functional requirements **outline the product's functionality to support user and business goals.
**Experience requirements **determine the user experience for a seamless, intuitive, and enjoyable interaction.
**Technical and business requirements** balance user needs, technical feasibility, and business constraints to provide realistic, achievable solutions that will drive business success.

body.text: 4. Framework Definition

The framework definition phase is important in creating a product's structural blueprint. This includes creating an **interaction framework** to visualize user journeys using storyboards, flow diagrams, and navigation maps. Then, designers create **wireframes** to outline key content areas and functionalities. Finally, they validate wireframes through **feedback loops** to show real input.
5. Refinement
The refinement stage involves a visual designer transforming wireframes and structural designs into polished products. It has three main processes:

items: Crafting **high-fidelity prototypes** to test branding, layout, and color schemes of the final product.
Keeping a **consistent visual language** and aligning [UI design](/services/ui-ux-design) with brand guidelines.
**Iterative usability testing** to identify areas of confusion or distraction.

body.text: 6. Development Support
The final stage is [development](/services/web-development) support to accurately translate a product vision into a functional solution. This involves:

items: **Design handoff**, where designers and UX specialists work with developers to implement all aspects correctly.
**Regular** **cross-team collaboration** to prevent deviations due to technical constraints or miscommunication.
**Post-development**, when the design team performs a design quality assurance check to maintain visual fidelity, functionality, and usability.

body.text: We understand how challenging it can be to manage every stage of the design process and maintain the highest quality. That's why we're here—to help and guide you through it all. Our [UI/UX design](/services/ui-ux-design) services will lead your product from concept to success easily and flawlessly.
Final Thoughts

Crafting a handy product is not about designing software. It means touching your users' lives and becoming their best friends. Goal-directed design is your key to creating products that inspire trust, bring satisfaction, and build long-lasting relationships with your users.

We at Arounda know that this process requires empathy, insight, and a great commitment to quality. These are our core principles. And we will be very happy to become your copilot on this trip and bring your vision to life with clarity and excellence. [Let's build products](/contact) that resonate, inspire, and change lives.

title: UX for AI: 10 Tips for Perfecting AI Product Metrics
author: Valeriia Serohina
excerpt: Did you know that today, [35%](https://www.authorityhacker.com/ai-statistics/) of businesses use AI, and 90% of leading enterprises invest in AI technologies? But we at [Arounda](/) noticed (as UX/UI experts) that many companies focus mostl

body.text: Did you know that today, [35%](https://www.authorityhacker.com/ai-statistics/) of businesses use AI, and 90% of leading enterprises invest in AI technologies? But we at [Arounda](/) noticed (as UX/UI experts) that many companies focus mostly on technical aspects and forget about the human factor. The true measure of an AI product's impact depends on its power to connect with users, solve their problems, and integrate perfectly into their lives or work environments. Here is where UX for AI becomes a game changer. We have created [170+ successful projects](/works) and have much to share with you to influence the results of your product.
**In this article: **

items: Learn about the importance of well-designed UI/UX for AI products.
Discover strategies to influence the results of AI products through UX design.
Take a look at our Arounda ideas and tips on how to create a powerful UX for AI.

body.text: Why UX is Crucial for AI Product Success

When developing AI products, the biggest accent is on machine learning models, data pipelines, automation capabilities, etc. But if people don't understand what to do and how to use these features, they get frustrated and quit. As a result, you'll get a high churn rate, right? That's why UX is crucial for success.
The benefits of UX design for AI products

items: Makes it easier to use
Provides transparency
Improves business results
Increases user engagement and retention
Builds trust and confidence
Helps to win the competition

body.text: We want to show you the main benefits of UX design for AI products:

items: It simplifies complex AI products with intuitive interfaces, clear visualizations, and thoughtful interactions.
Sometimes, artificial intelligence systems can be very complicated for users. A well-designed UX provides transparency in decision-making and data usage.
UX design demonstrates functionality in a pleasant and understandable way to attract and retain users.
Good UX design clearly shows the value and makes sure that the product is functional and meets the user's needs.

body.text: The Role of User Interface in AI Products

Imagine you have a recipe for a complicated dish. It tells you how to cook, but how you present the dish will differentiate it from the competition. You can serve the same meal simply and unattractively or like a 3-star Michelin restaurant. This is what the UI does, turning a technically complex product into a fantastic tool that users admire. With a well-designed UI, you can add real value to your product and increase engagement. [Arounda experts](/about) highlight the following key aspects of UI design for AI products.
Usability

A user-friendly interface allows people to achieve their goals efficiently and enjoyably and speaks the user's language. This is the basis of UI design. **For example,** Google Analytics (Google's AI tool) has very complex data processes running in the background. But thanks to a great UI, it presents information in an easy-to-understand format: clear graphs, easy navigation, and concise summaries.

An excellent feature for improving usability is a guided onboarding process that includes step-by-step interactive tutorials, gamification, videos, etc. If you are interested in creating the perfect user onboarding, welcome to [our course](/email-courses).
Familiarity

UI familiarity means using common patterns and design elements that users already know. Reduce cognitive load and make the transition to new AI technologies without problems! You can use familiar icons, layouts, and navigation patterns, such as prominent search, to make your AI product intuitive. Users won't spend time learning new UI paradigms because they want to focus on the AI functionality.** Keep in mind** that 94% of first impressions of a product's UI are related to design.
Accessibility
Your AI product should be accessible to everyone, regardless of their abilities or disabilities. This is an accessible design!

Did you know that more than 1 billion people in the world have some form of disability (according to the World Health Organization)? That's why digital businesses must meet specific accessibility standards. For example, the [European Accessibility Act](https://ec.europa.eu/social/main.jsp?catId=1202) emphasizes that all digital companies must have accessible interfaces by 2025; otherwise, there will be **legal and financial consequences**. And while this is a barrier for some companies, it is a new market opportunity for others.
Branding

Your product's UI is a powerful expression of your brand identity. Each element (color palette, logos, typography, etc.) should match your brand values and message. Customizable UI elements create a consistent and recognizable UX and reflect a reputation for reliability. **To show you an example**, our Arounda team has branded a fintech project [Klasha](https://case.arounda.agency/case/klasha). Welcome to our case study to see how we did it!
Interesting fact
Consistent branding across all platforms can increase revenue by up to 23%
Retention

Retention is another reason to invest in UI design. Bain & Company researched that a 5% increase in customer retention can boost profits by 25% to 95%. A well-designed UI attracts users, keeps them loyal, and fosters long-term engagement.

[How to increase retention](/blog/how-to-increase-customer-retention-and-get-more-profit-from-your-saas)? We recommend using gamification elements (progress tracking, badges, or rewards). But the main accent is personalization! **For example**, Spotify uses AI to create personalized playlists and suggestions. The app has a flawless UI design that is visually very engaging.
For a better user understanding, we offer to talk about the evolution of human interaction. Ready?
Evolution of Human Interaction
The relationship between humans and technology has evolved significantly. The focus has shifted from functionality to user experience.
Evolution stages of human interaction

items: Command-Line Interfaces (CLI)
Graphical User Interfaces (GUI)
AI-Driven Systems

body.text: Initially, the CLI provided interaction through text commands. It required specialized knowledge. Then, a GUI made the technology more accessible to the general public so that non-experts could navigate complex systems. Today, the development of AI makes this interaction more dynamic, personalized, and context-aware.

AI can predict user needs, adapt to individual preferences, and learn from each cooperation. However, only thoughtful UX design for AI can realize this potential. The challenge is to make AI products natural, intuitive, and even human. At Arounda, we take the following principles in mind:

items: **Voice interfaces and natural language processing** (like Siri, Alexa, and Google Assistant).
**Context-aware systems** (e.g., a smart home system that can learn the user's daily routine and adjust the environment accordingly).
**Emotional AI** (systems that can detect and respond to human emotions, facial expressions, or voice tone).
**Adaptive interfaces** (personalized content, offers, and even changing the layout or functionality based on user preferences).
**Data-driven UX** (analyzing user behavior to make informed design decisions, optimize user flows, and identify real-time pain points).

body.text: The simplest tip nowadays is to do everything with the user in mind!
Adapting UX to New User Behaviors

UX for AI products requires a deep understanding of user behavior. Our experts have researched how UX design adapts to changes and have used this information in our work, and now we want to share it with you.

items: Users expect AI to understand their preferences, predict actions, and offer relevant suggestions without explicit instructions.

body.text: **What to do?** Focus on creating personalized and intelligent experiences. For example, at Arounda we include predictive text, smart search, customized dashboards, etc.

items: Users want to know how AI uses their data.

body.text: **What to do?** Everything should be transparent and clear! People need to understand how AI decisions are made. This can include clear explanations, data management tools, and the ability to customize AI behavior.

items: Users want to have a seamless multimodal experience.

body.text: **What to do?** Create interfaces consistent with different input methods (voice, text, touch, and even gestures) and provide a smooth transition between them.

items: Users often don't know how to use new AI features or find existing training methods difficult to understand.

body.text: **What to do?** Create interactive tutorials, tips, gamified instruction, and just-in-time learning prompts. Our designers always make learning a natural part of the user journey.

items: Users prioritize ethical considerations.

Main point
UX design should create an innovative AI experience that fully meets users' expectations and values.
Which AI Product KPIs Can Design Improve?

Key performance indicators (KPIs) measure the success of an AI product and reflect its impact on users and businesses. Of course, AI technology, its features, and market demand play key roles, but UX can significantly influence these indicators. Here's a look at some of the key AI product KPIs that thoughtful design can improve.

items: **User engagement** (time spent on the platform, frequency of interactions, or the number of features used per session).
**User retention** (churn rate, monthly active users, or customer lifetime value).
**Conversion rates** (signup conversion rate, free-to-paid conversion rate, or purchase rate).
**User satisfaction** (net promoter score, customer satisfaction score, or star ratings in app stores).
**Efficiency and productivity** (task completion time, error reduction, or output quality increase).
**Adoption and usage rates** (daily active users, new user signups, or feature adoption rates).

body.text: Now we have the complete puzzle, and we are ready to answer the main question: **"What UX strategies influence the results of your AI product?"**. Let's go!
Strategies to Impact AI Product Results Through UX Design

If you thought AI product development was just about coding, you were wrong. It's also about creating unique experiences that deeply engage with users to achieve powerful results. The following strategies will maximize your product's impact if you're working on UX for machine learning, UX for generative AI, or broader UX for AI.

items: 47% Generative AI
36% Machine Learning
25% AI Service Robotics

body.text: Align the AI's Personality with User Expectations

Adapt the AI's communication style to the context and target audience. First, conduct thorough user research to create the right AI personality. Then, think about the style. For example, a friendly, conversational tone is ideal for generative AI. But the design of machine learning tools needs a more formal, professional tone. The main task is to know your users!
Design User-Centric Interfaces
We recommend designing a simple and clear UI/UX to help users navigate difficult functions without confusion. Remember that AI is a complex technology, and your task is to make it an intuitive tool.
Learn more about how we craft a [user-oriented design for AI products](/industries/ai).
Incorporate Personalization and Flexibility

Use AI power to personalize content, recommendations, and UI. For example, you can create customized content generators and templates. Users will love this because it saves them time and gives them a feeling of uniqueness. Offer flexibility in interaction modes (guided and manual modes) for people of different skill levels.
Facilitate Continuous User Feedback

Regular feedback loops help to identify problems early in the process, provide more targeted and effective updates, and guide ongoing improvements. Our team recommends integrating feedback mechanisms directly into the product. What works well: in-app surveys, feedback buttons, or user forums.
Implement Explainable AI (XAI) Principles

Create interfaces that clearly explain AI processes and solutions. Why? Because users want to understand how decisions are made, and XAI principles help build trust and confidence. For example, look at the financial and healthcare industries, where decisions can have significant consequences. UX should be well-thought-out with detailed explanations. Otherwise, it costs a lot of money or human lives.
Ensure High-Quality Data Collection

Nowadays, information is money. The data quality of AI systems directly affects the existence of your product. People use a lot of resources to check it. Therefore, design UX features that make it easier to collect accurate and relevant data. For example, user-friendly forms, clear instructions, and data validation. Users want to easily enter clean data and use tools to pre-process data. UX design here helps significantly increase the efficiency of AI.
Prioritize Ethical Design and Data Privacy

AI systems process increasing amounts of personal data. That's why ethical considerations and data privacy are very important. The UX for artificial intelligence products requires transparency and user control to ensure trust in creating personalized content. We recommend implementing clear privacy and consent controls in the UI.
Use A/B Testing for UX Optimization

A/B testing optimizes UX design by comparing different versions of interface elements to see which performs better. Conduct A/B tests regularly on key UI elements, such as layout, color schemes, or button placements. From our experience, it really helps increase user interaction and satisfaction.
Measure UX Impact and Iterate

Even if you're doing great, don't forget to use analytics tools to collect information about how design shifts affect engagement, satisfaction, and other KPIs. After all, there is no constant user behavior, and everything can change. Regular improvements based on user feedback and performance data keep the product evolving to meet user needs.
Handle Errors
No AI system is perfect, and errors will happen. How should the error handling process look to keep users' trust or frustrate them?

Create clear error messages that help users solve problems, avoid technical jargon, and provide practical steps. The system should offer an easy way to fix or report the error and provide suggestions for troubleshooting or automatic corrections to recover quickly. **Remember, the design must be well thought out!**

items: **Responsive design** Your AI product's interface should easily adapt to different devices and screen sizes.
**Load times and performance** Minimize load times by optimizing resources, using efficient algorithms, and caching where appropriate.
**Micro-interactions** Small details like hover effects, button animations, and on-action feedback can significantly improve the user experience.
**Security in mind** Integrate multi-factor authentication and secure data handling into the user journey without compromising ease of use.

body.text: Final Thoughts

It's no secret that artificial intelligence has become a friend to users and businesses. And its power will become stronger and stronger. Therefore, the success of AI products depends not only on the genius of algorithms but also on the quality of user experience. [UX design for AI](/industries/ai) is a bridge that connects advanced technologies with people who use them. **The main question is: how do you design this bridge?**

The strategies we've described in this article are important steps toward designing intuitive, engaging, and effective experiences. They help create interfaces that adapt to new user behaviors, are flexible enough to grow with user needs, and robust enough to handle the complexities of AI.

We know that staying on top of design is challenging and time-consuming, so our Arounda team will be happy to be your caring partner and perfect the AI future together! [Contact us](/contact) to find out how our UX/UI design services can help push your product to success.

author: Valeriia Serohina
