body.text: What are the top priorities for any business: money, number of users, satisfied customers? All together, right? In other words, high conversion! The secret lies not in complex algorithms or expensive ad campaigns but in understanding your users on a deeper, more human level. This is about empathy in [UX design](/services/ui-ux-design). Why? Because you can't grab a cup of coffee and have a friendly conversation with each of your users. But you can show deep understanding (empathy) through the screen.

For us at [Arounda](/), empathy-driven design is the foundation for [all our projects](/works). Clients often ask us about their low conversions, and the answer lies on the surface — because of a bad UX design. That's why our team decided to share our experience and prepare this article to solve some common problems.
In this article:

items: Find out what empathy is in UI/UX design and how it differs from sympathy.
Learn how to improve empathy in your design.
Discover how to conduct user research to improve product KPIs.
Get insights, practical tips, and examples from Arounda experts.

body.text: What is Empathy in UI/UX Design

Empathy in design goes beyond aesthetics. It's about creating experiences that connect with users on a personal level. You need to step into the users' shoes and understand their needs and difficulties during interaction with your product.

We recommend answering the question: "What does my customer really want to achieve, and how can I make it as easy as possible?". The answer will help you see potential problems or the complexity of some processes. Remember that people with unique needs are behind every click, tap, or swipe. Make them feel valued and supported, and they will love your product, trust it, and come back again and again.
Main point
Empathy helps to create intuitive and user-centered designs and to turn users into loyal customers.
Empathy = higher conversions
Sympathy vs. Empathy

We can understand sympathy and empathy in relationships, for example, but what are empathy and sympathy in UX? Sympathy helps you understand the user's pain but doesn't necessarily fix the cause. Empathy goes deeper to understand the user's experience and create relevant solutions.

**Let's look at an example:** the checkout process in e-commerce. You notice that users are leaving their shopping carts during the checkout process. The designer assumed that users were simply confused about the steps and suggested adding tooltips or pop-ups to help them. These features are well-intentioned, but they don't remove the reasons why users drop orders. This is UX sympathy! If the designer takes a step back and explores the entire emotional user journey (conducts user research, identifies hot spots, and understands the specific frustrations they face) to understand the reasons, this will be UX empathy.
UX Sympathy Features

items: Tooltips and instructional pop-ups
Progress indicators
Error messages and warnings
Overexplaining features
Adjustments instead of research

body.text: UX Empathy Features

items: Simplified user flow
Personalized experiences
Flexible options
Emotional support elements
Resolved problems before they occur

body.text: Improving and Analyzing Empathy in UX Design

Empathy in UX design is not a once-and-done thing! You should constantly improve your understanding of users and measure how well your design solutions meet their needs. It's about new strategies and actionable insights. At Arounda, we have the following plan for developing and analyzing empathy.
Understand Problem

Do you know how your users feel: overwhelmed, confused, or anxious? And why do they feel so? **Here is the point:** you must understand the emotions to design solutions that address the core issues. We start with comprehensive research using tools like [user personas](/blog/what-are-personas) and [customer journey maps](/blog/mapping-the-customer-journey-important-aspects-to-keep-in-mind) to see what customers are going through at every touchpoint. Our designers match out their pain points, motivations, and expectations to gain a holistic view of the real problems.
Reduce Your Own Biases

If you think some features are great and clear, they may be different for users. Always question assumptions about user desires and behavior, as well as assumptions about their behavior. We involve cross-functional teams and user testing to eliminate blind spots and make sure the final design meets actual user needs. **Observation and feedback are what work—not your guesswork!**
Analyze Empathy

Start by tracking key usability metrics: task completion rates, time to complete tasks, or bounce rates. Then, compare the results with user feedback. Heatmaps and session recordings can also show where users struggle, lose interest, or quit tasks. Remember to do it regularly.

We have a great financial project—[Infinity](https://case.arounda.agency/case/infinity)—where you can see an example of empathetic design. For this type of project (finance), it is very important to guarantee convenience because users feel stressed when they think about any financial operations. This is where empathetic UX comes into play. Just take a look at the results!

items: 80% User satisfaction rate Our Web 3.0 development and design services left most users satisfied.
40% User retention rate Arounda's efforts helped Infinity retain a significant portion of users.
25% Mobile users increase As seen in our crypto case study, a new mobile app is what users want the most.
5% Conversion rate Infinity's convenience prompts users to complete their desired actions within the app.

body.text: Develop Empathy Maps

An empathy map explores what a user says, thinks, feels, and does. Consider **Dropbox**'s early approach to design. Their team found that users had trouble getting set up, especially understanding how files synced between devices. They created an empathy map and found that users felt confused (feeling), found the process too complicated (thinking), and expressed frustration with file syncing issues (saying). This led Dropbox to develop a more visual, simplified setup process with clear step-by-step instructions. **The result:** reduced user drop-off rates.
*P.S. We will tell you more about the empathy map in the next section. *
Observe Users in the Context

Watch users in their natural environment! You will see nuances such as distractions, physical limitations, and emotional reactions because you design for real-world conditions, not ideal scenarios. For instance, by observing how a user struggles with a mobile app in a noisy, fast-paced place, you can [redesign](/solutions/product-redesign) the interface with larger buttons and a simplified layout.
Conduct Surveys and Interviews

Surveys can uncover broad trends in user behavior, while one-on-one interviews allow for exploring in-depth perspectives and emotions. Ask open-ended questions like, “What was the most frustrating part of your experience?” or “How did you feel while using this feature?”. Our designers always combine qualitative insights from interviews with quantitative data from surveys. This is how we get a full picture for more empathetic design solutions.
Empathy Map

An empathy map is an essential tool in the empathy design process. It covers the full emotional, cognitive, and behavioral spectrum of users. This is how you can increase trust and satisfaction and get higher conversion rates. To get a well-designed empathy map, divide it into four parts, each representing a different aspect of the user experience.

items: What the user says
What the user thinks
What the user feels
What the user does

Integrating empathy helps identify pain points, behaviors, and emotional triggers that impact key performance indicators (e.g., user retention, satisfaction, engagement, task completion rates, conversion rates). body.text: Conduct Empathy Interviews

Ask open questions and encourage users to share their experiences, concerns, and emotions in a natural, conversational format. **The goal:** to understand what users did, why they did it, and how it affected their experience.
Track Power User Behavior

Tracking power users (those who interact with your product the most) provides valuable insights into user retention and loyalty. It lets you prioritize design improvements that benefit power users and broader user segments and take action to redesign or simplify certain features.
Monitor Happy Paths

A happy path describes an ideal user journey where everything works as expected, and the user reaches their goal without facing any difficulties. Tracking these paths helps you understand how users behave when they have a flawless experience and what features or elements contribute to this positive flow.
Use Heatmaps and Session Recordings

Heatmaps and session recordings are valuable tools for real-time user behavior analysis. You can see where they click, scroll, or abandon tasks. As a result, you can optimize design elements like navigation, call-to-action buttons, or page layout.
Build Empathy Maps from Research

As we discussed earlier, empathy maps help visualize and analyze user research. They provide a shared understanding of user emotions, behaviors, and frustrations to design intuitive and emotionally resonant solutions.
Update User Personas Regularly

User personas are not static. They evolve as your product and user base grow. That’s why you should regularly update personas based on new user research to align with your audience’s changing needs, behaviors, and expectations.
Practice Empathy at Every Stage of the Design Process

To effectively apply empathy in design, make it a core principle throughout every process stage—from ideation and wireframing to prototyping and testing. This approach helps avoid redesigns and makes your final product valuable for users.
Avoid Unconscious Biases in Research

Assumptions are a trap! Unconscious biases can skew your understanding of user needs, leading to design decisions that don't fit your target audience. Make sure your sample is diverse and representative of your broader audience, and use objective data to support quality insights.
Conduct Your Research in a Natural Environment

Observe users in their natural environment: at home, at work, or on the go. You will understand the real challenges and difficulties they face daily. This approach allows you to empathize more effectively with users and develop solutions that fit naturally into their lives.
Iterate Solutions with Prototypes and MVPs

Prototypes and MVPs help you test ideas with real people, gather feedback, and make improvements before launching a feature or product. This method reduces the risk of releasing features that miss the mark.

If you need help with your [prototypes or MVPs](/solutions/mvp), our Arounda team is here to help! We've designed well-received products and generated over $1 billion in revenue for our startup clients. So don't worry—you're in good hands.

Empathetic designs require a mindset shift and appropriate tools to align design decisions with user needs and emotions. Our team created a list of powerful tools that help us foster empathy in the design process.

body.text: Now, we want to show you what the empathy process looks like. Take our project, Altflow, as an example.
Our Examples of Empathic Design: Altflow

Altflow is an AI-powered tool for creating SEO-optimized articles. When we talk about AI tools, empathy plays a critical role. Our approach was not just to understand the functional needs of users (copywriters, marketing teams, and SEO professionals) but to understand their emotional challenges.

We realized that content creators and SEO specialists face pressure to produce high-quality content quickly. Many tools offer automation, but users often feel disconnected from the final output (as the generated content may lack a human touch or brand consistency). They need articles that feel personalized, aligned with the brand tone, and require minimal manual editing.
Core features list

items: Human and AI editing

body.text: We integrated the human and AI editing features to solve the problem of user frustration. It combines the efficiency of AI and human editing, allowing users to create SEO-optimized content while controlling the editing process quickly.

items: Blog generator prompts for brands

body.text: Every brand has its unique voice, tone, and style. A one-size-fits-all content generator couldn't capture this diversity. Realizing this, we designed this feature to show the uniqueness of each brand. It gives users peace of mind because they know that the articles they create will match their messaging and tone, and they don't need significant edits.

items: Templates

body.text: Users often struggle with maintaining consistency across articles, especially with multiple clients or brands. We designed the pre-built templates for easy creation of different content. This results in faster, high-quality content, reduced cognitive load, and enhanced efficiency.

items: Multi-brand management and workspaces

body.text: Managing different styles, keywords, and article structures across different projects can be very hard. During our research, we identified a key emotional pain point: disorganized and stressful workflow. To address this, our designers introduced the Multi-brand Management and Workspaces feature. It allows users to create customized prompts, article generation settings, and templates for each brand within the same platform.
Our Arounda designers always use empathy in UI/UX design. We have [different projects](/works) to show you where you can find inspiration.
Final Thoughts

Users expect brands to understand them, and empathy in [UX design](/services/ui-ux-design) helps to fulfill this expectation. When you design with empathy, you create experiences that directly respond to users' needs, problems, and desires, fostering deeper connections. This approach helps build trust, reduce friction, improve key performance indicators, and achieve your goals.

At Arounda, we specialize in creating human-centered UI/UX or [redesign](/solutions/product-redesign) solutions and [MVPs](/solutions/mvp) for various industries. We've helped more than 170 businesses succeed and would love to help improve yours. Let us be your caring, empathetic partner.

body.text: The Role of User Interface in AI Products

Imagine you have a recipe for a complicated dish. It tells you how to cook, but how you present the dish will differentiate it from the competition. You can serve the same meal simply and unattractively or like a 3-star Michelin restaurant. This is what the UI does, turning a technically complex product into a fantastic tool that users admire. With a well-designed UI, you can add real value to your product and increase engagement. [Arounda experts](/about) highlight the following key aspects of [UI design](/services/ui-ux-design) for AI products.
Usability

A user-friendly interface allows people to achieve their goals efficiently and enjoyably and speaks the user's language. This is the basis of UI design. **For example,** Google Analytics (Google's AI tool) has very complex data processes running in the background. But thanks to a great UI, it presents information in an easy-to-understand format: clear graphs, easy navigation, and concise summaries.

An excellent feature for improving usability is a guided onboarding process that includes step-by-step interactive tutorials, gamification, videos, etc. If you are interested in creating the perfect user onboarding, welcome to [our course](/email-courses).
Familiarity

UI familiarity means using common patterns and design elements that users already know. Reduce cognitive load and make the transition to new AI technologies without problems! You can use familiar icons, layouts, and navigation patterns, such as prominent search, to make your AI product intuitive. Users won't spend time learning new UI paradigms because they want to focus on the AI functionality.** Keep in mind** that 94% of first impressions of a product's UI are related to design.
Accessibility
Your AI product should be accessible to everyone, regardless of their abilities or disabilities. This is an accessible design!

Did you know that more than 1 billion people in the world have some form of disability (according to the World Health Organization)? That's why digital businesses must meet specific accessibility standards. For example, the [European Accessibility Act](https://ec.europa.eu/social/main.jsp?catId=1202) emphasizes that all digital companies must have accessible interfaces; otherwise, there will be legal and financial consequences. And while this is a barrier for some companies, it is a new market opportunity for others.
Branding

Your product's UI is a powerful expression of your [brand identity](/services/brand-identity). Each element (color palette, logos, typography, etc.) should match your brand values and message. Customizable UI elements create a consistent and recognizable UX and reflect a reputation for reliability. **To show you an example**, our Arounda team has branded a fintech project [Klasha](https://case.arounda.agency/case/klasha). Therefore, design UX features that make it easier to collect accurate and relevant data. For example, user-friendly forms, clear instructions, and data validation. Users want to easily enter clean data and use tools to pre-process data. UX design here helps significantly increase the efficiency of AI.
Prioritize Ethical Design and Data Privacy

AI systems process increasing amounts of personal data. That's why ethical considerations and data privacy are very important. The UX for artificial intelligence products requires transparency and user control to ensure trust in creating personalized content. We recommend implementing clear privacy and consent controls in the UI.
Use A/B Testing for UX Optimization

A/B testing optimizes UX design by comparing different versions of interface elements to see which performs better. Conduct A/B tests regularly on key UI elements, such as layout, color schemes, or button placements. From our experience, it really helps increase user interaction and satisfaction.
Measure UX Impact and Iterate

Even if you're doing great, don't forget to use analytics tools to collect information about how design shifts affect engagement, satisfaction, and other KPIs. After all, there is no constant user behavior, and everything can change. Regular improvements based on user feedback and performance data keep the product evolving to meet user needs.
Handle Errors
No AI system is perfect, and errors will happen. How should the error handling process look to keep users' trust or frustrate them?

Create clear error messages that help users solve problems, avoid technical jargon, and provide practical steps. The system should offer an easy way to fix or report the error and provide suggestions for troubleshooting or automatic corrections to recover quickly. **Remember, the design must be well thought out!**
Arounda tips

items: **Responsive design** Your AI product's interface should easily adapt to different devices and screen sizes.
**Load times and performance** Minimize load times by optimizing resources, using efficient algorithms, and caching where appropriate.
**Micro-interactions** Small details like hover effects, button animations, and on-action feedback can significantly improve the user experience.
**Security in mind** Integrate multi-factor authentication and secure data handling into the user journey without compromising ease of use.

body.text: Final Thoughts

It's no secret that artificial intelligence has become a friend to users and businesses. And its power will become stronger and stronger. Therefore, the success of AI products depends not only on the genius of algorithms but also on the quality of user experience. [UX design for AI](/industries/ai) is a bridge that connects advanced technologies with people who use them. **The main question is: how do you design this bridge?**

The strategies we've described in this article are important steps toward designing intuitive, engaging, and effective experiences. They help create interfaces that adapt to new user behaviors, are flexible enough to grow with user needs, and robust enough to handle the complexities of AI.

We know that staying on top of design is challenging and time-consuming, so our Arounda team will be happy to be your caring partner and perfect the AI future together! [Contact us](/contact) to find out how our [UX/UI design](/services/ui-ux-design) services can help push your product to success.

title: How to Increase Customer Retention and Get More Profit From Your SaaS
author: Vlad Gavriluk
excerpt: The SaaS market is highly competitive. Many companies are constantly improving and entering the market. This has led to high churn rates as customers demand a more valuable user experience. Imagine spending countless hours and resources to

body.text: The SaaS market is highly competitive. Many companies are constantly improving and entering the market. This has led to high churn rates as customers demand a more valuable user experience. Imagine spending countless hours and resources to attract new users and then watching them leave. It's frustrating, right? This is where effective SaaS retention strategies become your weapons. These strategies can turn dissatisfied users into loyal customers. And they will help you reduce churn and increase revenue.

At Arounda, we have rich experience in the [SaaS industry](/industries/saas) and can help you find the key to sustainable growth. Let's find out how to turn fleeting visitors into loyal clients and increase profits.
In this article:

items: Find out why user retention in SaaS is important, its benefits, and key metrics.
Learn about and choose the best SaaS customer retention strategies.
Discover practical examples and get our expert insights.

body.text: What is Customer Retention?

SaaS customer retention is the ability of a company to maintain user subscriptions and purchases over time. It focuses on regular income over one-time sales (unlike traditional businesses). Retention involves developing loyalty, ensuring customer satisfaction, and continuously delivering value to users for long-term success.
Why SaaS retention is important

items: **Cost efficiency** Focusing on retention can significantly reduce customer acquisition costs and increase the return on investment by up to five times.
**Competitive Edge** High SaaS customer retention rates indicate a healthy, customer-centric business that consistently meets or exceeds customer expectations, setting it apart from competitors.

**Revenue growth** SaaS customer retention strategies enhance customer lifetime value (CLV) by encouraging users to invest in premium features, upgrades, and add-ons, thereby significantly increasing SaaS revenue.

body.text: Key Metrics
Here, we provide the most important metrics and show how to calculate them. They will help you measure SaaS retention and keep your finger on the pulse.

items: **Churn Rate:** This is the percentage of customers who cancel their subscriptions during a certain period. A high churn rate indicates potential problems with your product or customer satisfaction.

body.text: **Formula:** *Churn Rate = (Number of customers lost during a period / number of customers at the start of the period) x 100*
**FYI:** If you have less than 5% monthly - it's a good rate. If you see more than 7% monthly, choose another strategy or think about a UI/UX audit to identify the problems.

items: **Retention Rate:** This is the percentage of customers who continue to use your services during a specified period. Higher retention rates indicate successful SaaS retention strategies.

body.text: **Formula:** *Retention Rate = ((Number of customers at the end of a period - New customers acquired during the period) / Number of customers at the start of the period) x 100*
**FYI: **If you have over 90% monthly - great job. But if less than 80% monthly, it's time to find the reasons and take action.

items: **Customer Lifetime Value (CLV): **It shows the total revenue you can expect from a single customer over the entire period of his/her relationship with your company. A higher CLV means that each customer receives more value, boosting overall SaaS retention.

body.text: **Formula:** *CLV = Average revenue per customer x Average customer lifespan*
**FYI: **A good rate is when CLV is 3 times higher than the Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC). Bad CLV is less than 1.5 times the CAC.** **

items: **Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) Growth**: Positive MRR growth indicates effective customer retention strategies of SaaS. It reflects the increase in revenue from existing customers, including renewals and upsells.

body.text: **Formula:** *MRR Growth = ((MRR at the end of the period - MRR at the start of the period) / MRR at the start of the period) x 100*

**FYI: **The good rate is over 10% monthly, and the bad rate is below 2% monthly. If you have low rates, consider choosing a new SaaS retention strategy, [UX audit](/services/ux-audit), and/or [redesign](/solutions/product-redesign).
Are you interested in why most SaaS products fail and what you can do about it? [Read our article to find out](/blog/how-to-launch-your-saas-product-and-get-tractions).

Well, we've explored customer retention and its importance, and now we know how to calculate the key metrics. If all those rates are high, that's perfect! But if not? You need to change something. We invite you to explore the benefits of implementing SaaS retention strategies and choose the best for your business.
Benefits of SaaS retention strategies

items: Increased customer lifetime value
Reduced churn rates
Higher revenue and profitability
Stronger customer relationships
Better market positioning
Efficient use of resources

body.text: Best SaaS Customer Retention Strategies

How to increase customer retention in SaaS and get more profit? Choose the right strategy. Effective customer retention strategies for your SaaS business are crucial to ensure customer loyalty and satisfaction. And, of course, increase revenue. We are experts in the SaaS industry, so our team gathered the most useful tips to share with you. Let's go!
Enhancing Customer Onboarding

[Customer onboarding](/blog/saas-onboarding-increase-customer-loyalty-and-retention) is the initial interaction with a SaaS product. It's like a first date, where the first impression is really important. An effective onboarding process can establish a long-lasting relationship. It directly influences your SaaS retention strategy.
What you need to do:

items: Create personalized experiences that** **can improve the onboarding. In other words, tailor the process based on user profiles and needs.
Provide clear, step-by-step instructions to help users navigate the product effortlessly.
Give proactive support, such as live chats, emails, and scheduled check-ins. This can prevent confusion and frustration.

Think about quick wins.** **Helping users achieve quick wins early in onboarding can boost their confidence and satisfaction. Identify key actions that show the product's value and guide them to complete them.

body.text: Customer onboarding statistics

items: 30% faster revenue growth in SaaS companies with strong onboarding processes.
63% of customers consider the onboarding period when deciding to subscribe to a service or buy a product.
55% of customers say they will stop using a product or service they don't understand.

body.text: *Source: SaaS Capital*
Remember, your product must be enjoyable and easy to navigate! We had an excellent HR project for this task: Gradwork. We improved customer reach by 35% and achieved 80% user satisfaction.
Do you want to know how we did it for our SaaS client? [Explore our case](/case/gradwork) to get interesting insights from our designers.
Coming back to strategies, let’s explore the next one.
Using Data and Analytics

Data and analytics are very important in developing effective SaaS retention strategies. They provide insights into customer behavior, preferences, and pain points that can help you make informed decisions.
What you need to do:

items: Track customer behavior and usage patterns to identify valuable features and prevent frustration. For detailed insights, use tools like Google Analytics, Mixpanel, and Amplitude.
Foresee customer churn by analyzing historical data and identifying trends. It is called predictive analytics, which allows you to implement **targeted** SaaS retention strategies.

Personalize customer interactions and increase relevance and [engagement](/blog/how-saas-customer-engagement-can-be-improved-by-companies). Create personalized emails, product recommendations, and targeted offers based on your user behavior.
Segment customers according to usage patterns, industry, or subscription level. It will help you tailor retention strategies to different groups and provide customized support.

body.text: We understand how challenging it could be to analyze all those numbers, detect the problems, and find the right solutions. You don’t need to worry! Take a deep breath, and just tell us. Our expert team is happy to help you! We offer [well-proven design solutions for your SaaS product](/industries/saas): CRM, analytics, automation, AI data tools, recruitment, ATS, HRM, marketing MAS, and many more.
Creating Customer Success Programs

Creating useful customer success programs is one of the B2B SaaS customer retention strategies for increasing product value. This approach includes dedicated teams, strategic initiatives, and constant engagement to understand and achieve desired results.
What you need to do:

items: Form a team focused on customer success that will work closely with customers. **Aims:** to understand their needs, set goals, and guide them through the product journey.
Ask your customer success managers (CSMs) to do regular check-ins and proactive outreach. It can significantly improve customer relationships and show commitment to clients’ success.
Offer customers extensive educational resources, such as webinars, tutorials, and certification programs. This will enhance the value of your product.
Track users’ well-being with customer health scores and start proactive measures to prevent customer churn.
Customize success plans and outline clear objectives, milestones, and actionable steps.

body.text: **Examples**

**Zoom's **customer success program emphasizes personalized onboarding, regular check-ins, and training resources. The end outcome is better satisfaction and retention rates. **Adobe's** success team offers tailored plans, proactive marketing, and educational materials. They also identify at-risk accounts for retention and revenue.
Important fact
A well-designed user interface can significantly boost conversion rates by up to 200%, while a better UX design can result in up to 400%.
*Source: Forrester*
Delivering Exceptional Customer Support

Successful customer retention strategies in SaaS require effective customer assistance. Of course, users will have questions, problems, and demands. Providing expert support can make a significant difference in retention. Your customers will feel appreciated, understood, and happy. This leads to long-term loyalty, right?
What you need to do:

items: Provide 24-hour support using several channels like email, live chat, phone, and social media to guarantee people can easily reach out for help.
Prevent customer frustration and reduce churn through proactive communication. For example, automated emails or in-app messages can offer tips, reminders, or notifications about potential problems.
Offer a comprehensive knowledge base with articles, FAQs, and tutorials. In this way, users can find solutions themselves, reducing the load on the support team.

Adapt your customer service interactions using client data to significantly improve the user experience. For example, always address users by their first name. You can also identify usage patterns and offer solutions accordingly.

Answer user questions and solve their problem quickly and efficiently. Harvard Business Review emphasizes the importance of timely and effective support. Quick response times and first-contact resolution (FCR) rates are key indicators. Remember that fast solutions increase customer loyalty.

body.text: Customer support statistics

items: 89% of companies now compete primarily on customer experience.
96% of consumers consider customer service to be critical to brand loyalty.
72% of customers expect companies to understand their requirements and address them in advance.

body.text: *Sources: Microsoft, Gartner, Salesforce*
Regular Communication and Engagement

Effective SaaS customer retention strategies need regular communication and engagement. You will preserve brand connections, keep customers informed about product updates, and express gratitude for their loyalty.
What you need to do:

items: Pay attention to client feedback. It provides useful information about customer satisfaction and areas for improvement. You can gather feedback using tools like surveys and NPS.

Send regular newsletters with tips, feature updates, and industry news. You will keep customers informed about what’s going on in your business and industry. They will feel a sense of belonging in your community and raise the chance of a new buy. Mailchimp can help you with regular sending.

Build community. A product-focused community through forums, social media groups, and user events can foster a sense of belonging. Engaged communities offer support, share best practices, and advocate for your brand.
Don’t forget about personalized communication based on user behavior, preferences, and feedback. It will improve relevance and effectiveness.
Offer educational content like tutorials, webinars, free courses, blog articles, and posts. It empowers users and establishes your company as an authority in the field.

body.text: [Our Arounda design team](/about) wants to share a practical example of a user-centric redesign for WordPress, which is the industry leader in content management systems.

**Our results** include improved website design and branding, better-quality marketing materials, a new visual style, an individual marketing approach to each product, retaining more customers through email marketing, and many more. Discover [our WordPress case](/case/wordpress).

Providing Value Through Product Development
Continuous product development is essential for high SaaS customer retention rates. Focusing on ongoing upgrades keeps products relevant and attracts new clients.
What you need to do:

items: Continuously update and refine your product based on customer feedback and market trends. Use agile development methodologies like Scrum or Kanban.
Provide innovation! Strategic features can boost user engagement and satisfaction. They address customer issues and provide significant value.
Create a user-centric design. Your product should be intuitive and user-friendly. Thorough user research, usability testing, and adherence to UX/UI best practices will assist you.
Scale your product with customer growth. It means that its software can handle increased loads and deliver consistent performance.

Integrate with popular tools and provide customization. This will make your product more adaptable to different customer needs. For example, Slack's integration with other software tools has made it a great hub for team collaboration. This step improved the value proposition and retention.

body.text: **More examples**

Spotify, Netflix, and Atlassian are companies that are constantly updating their platforms to keep users interested and satisfied. **Spotify** offers extra functions such as customized playlists, podcast integration, and social sharing options. **Netflix** invests in infrastructure to support its growing audience. **Atlassian** regularly adds new features to its Jira software depending on customer feedback.

Our team ensures product relevance, user satisfaction, and long-term growth. Find out more about our [MVP design service](/solutions/mvp) for startups or [product redesign service](/solutions/product-redesign) for existing companies.
Implementing Loyalty Programs and Incentives
Loyalty programs and incentives can significantly boost customer retention rates. Reward loyal customers! It fosters a strong emotional connection between customers and the brand. Agree?
What you need to do:

items: Offer discounts, exclusive features, early access to new updates, or non-monetary recognition in the community. A reward system that acknowledges and appreciates customer loyalty is very important for people. It's an amazing psychological trick.
Integrate a tiered loyalty program to increase customer engagement with a product. Offer higher tiers with enhanced benefits. By the way, HubSpot effectively uses this strategy.
Encourage customers to refer new users. This can improve retention efforts, attract new customers, and strengthen loyalty.

Provide exclusive offers and content for your loyal customers. People are happy when they get special deals. For example, early access to new features, special discounts, or exclusive webinars and events. Use this strategy for a SaaS boost.

Use gamification. Adults also like playing! [Gamification](/blog/gamification-in-product-design-in-2024-ui-ux) can enhance the engagement and fun of a loyalty program. Incorporate points, badges, leaderboards, and challenges for customer participation.

title: How to Conduct a UX Audit: Examples and Methods
author: Valeriia Serohina
excerpt: How do you think user experience (UX) is critical in today's digital world? Definitely! It can make your product more attractive for users or ruin it. This is why a UX audit is necessary.

body.text: How do you think user experience (UX) is critical in today's digital world? Definitely! It can make your product more attractive for users or ruin it. This is why a UX audit is necessary.

Imagine you enter a beautiful shop with an inviting window display but a cluttered interior. You can't find the products you need, and so many items are in the wrong order. Then, it is hard to find the exit. How do you feel? Perhaps nervous, disappointed, and without any desire to come back.

Similarly, a website or app that looks great but is difficult to navigate will quickly lose users. Fortunately, a UX audit helps to find these pain points, improve the product, and make your users happy! [Our Arounda team](/) shares experience and knowledge about the UX audit process. There is no more time to wait. Let's delve into the article.
**In this article:**

items: Learn how to conduct a user experience audit.
Discover the methods for [UX audit](/services/ux-audit) and explore our examples.
Get expert tips on how to conduct a UX audit.

body.text: What is a UX Audit?

A user experience audit (UX) is a systematic examination of a website's or application's user interface (UI) to detect usability flaws, enhance user satisfaction, and boost conversion rates. It reveals hidden obstacles to a flawless user experience.
Objectives of User Experience Audit
Let's look at the key objectives:

items: A UX audit evaluates a website or app to identify usability issues such as complex navigation, confusing interfaces, and obstacles to better user flow.
It improves user satisfaction by creating an intuitive, engaging, and positive experience. A happy user will return and become your loyal customer.
A UX audit can identify why users do not complete the desired actions or leave the website/app. It suggests practical ideas for increasing conversion rates.

body.text: The main goals are impressive, right? But how do you know when a UX audit is a must? Let's find out.
When is a UX Audit Necessary?
People say: *A stitch in time saves nine*. Therefore, solve problems immediately before they become bigger. But when exactly is "immediately"?

items: If you notice a drop in user engagement metrics (time spent on site, page views, or repeat visits).
If you see high bounce rates. It means that users leave your website or app almost immediately.
If you plan to redesign an app or site. A UX audit will clearly show you what to change, what works well, or whether you don't need a redesign at all.
If you get negative feedback or your users often complain about usability issues. Listen to your customers - that's why you created the product, right?
If your conversion rates are stagnant. It's time to examine the user experience more closely and identify hidden barriers.

body.text: [Learn about](/blog/ux-ui-design-audit-key-benefits-for-your-existing-product) key benefits of UX/UI design audit to get even more insights.
Interesting UX Statistics

items: 90% of users stopped using the app because of poor performance.
88% of online customers say they would not return to a website after a negative user experience.
75% of customers evaluate the credibility of a website based on its aesthetics.

body.text: Well, you've found a reason or reasons to audit UX. It's time to get ready!
How to Prepare for UX Design Audit
Good preparation is the first step to a successful result. Do you agree? Here are the tasks for getting ready for a website user experience audit or UX design audit.
**Task #1:** Gather all the necessary tools and resources, including analytics, survey and feedback tools, and prototype and testing tools.

items: Analytics tools: Google Analytics, Hotjar, and Mixpanel.
Survey and feedback tools: SurveyMonkey, Typeform, and UserVoice.
Prototype and testing tools: Sketch, Figma, and InVision.

body.text: **Task #2:** Set targets and KPIs for the UX audit, such as improving navigation, raising conversion rates, and increasing user satisfaction. Metrics for measuring success include completion rates, time on task, error rates, conversion rates, and others.
**Task #3:** Form or find a team of [UX designers](/blog/how-to-hire-a-ux-designer-top-5-tips), researchers, analysts, and stakeholders (product managers, marketing managers, and development leads).

If you complete all of these tasks, your UX audit process will run easily and effectively. However, it can be difficult to find experienced team members on your own. Don't worry! Our Arounda experts are here to help. [Expand your team](https://arounda.agency/solutions/team-extension) with our professionals and get actionable insights to reach your goals.
How to Conduct a UX Audit
We reached the beginning of the transformation. [Our team](https://arounda.agency/about) has prepared a step-by-step guide to make your UX audit process pleasant and easy.
**Step 1: Define goals and the scope**
You should decide which components of your website or application the team will examine. It can be an entire site/app, or pages, specific sections, user flows...
**Step 2: Collect data for analytics review**

Gather quantitative data using the analytics tools and resources from preparation task #1. They help you understand user behavior. You should concentrate on KPIs like page visits, session duration, bounce rates, and conversion rates. It is also important to gather qualitative data (user feedback). Then, analyze key metrics, identify patterns, and address usability issues.
**Step 3: Conduct heuristic evaluation**
This stage helps identify usability issues in a website or application. You should document findings to understand their impact on user experience.
*P.S. We explain how to conduct the heuristic evaluation in the following section.*
**Step 4: Make user testing**

First, select participants from the target audience (current or new users). Next, conduct testing sessions to track user behavior and gather feedback on your website or app. Finally, analyze the results to identify trends and pain points.
Would you like to get expert tips for user testing? [Read](/blog/7-expert-tips-to-enhance-user-testing) our article.
**Step 5: Gather and interpret the findings**

Collect and analyze information from earlier steps, and highlight critical usability issues with visuals such as charts and heat maps. Then, prioritize and report the findings, create an action plan, and share the report with stakeholders for suggested actions.
**Step 6: Implement recommendations**
Create a plan outlining the actions, deadlines, team members, and their responsibilities.
**Step 7: Track changes and schedule regular audits**
To guarantee efficacy, monitor changes, user behavior, and key metrics. Schedule regular UX audits to improve the user experience over time and remain competitive.

The UX audit process needs careful planning and deployment. If you find the task complicated or require [expert support](/services/ux-audit), our team will help you to create the best user experience possible.
Methods for Conducting UX Audit
You can conduct a UX audit using a variety of approaches to gather detailed information about the user experience. We have collected some of the most effective techniques.

items: Heuristic evaluation
User testing
Analytics Review
Surveys and Feedback

body.text: Heuristic Evaluation

How do we perform [heuristic evaluation](/blog/heuristic-evaluation-ux-a-strategic-tool-in-enhancing-design)? Our team of 3-5 usability experts (depending on the project's size) checks your website or app for compliance with established usability principles (heuristics). We independently review the interface and identify usability issues that might be obscure through user testing alone. Then, we discuss findings and prioritize issues.
Let's take a look at the example of common heuristics.
Nielsen's 10 Usability Heuristics

items: Make sure that your users know what is going on through appropriate feedback.
Use language and concepts familiar to the user.
Provide ways to undo and redo actions.
Provide consistency and follow the standards and conventions.
Design to prevent errors.
Focus on enhancing recognition rather than recall to reduce user memory load.
Allow experienced users to use shortcuts.
Craft a minimalistic design and do not use too many elements (it must be transparent and efficient).
Help your users understand and recover from errors. Use plain and understandable language.
Provide easily available assistance.

body.text: **Real Example:** A retail company used this heuristic method to conduct a website UX audit. The audit showed that the checkout process was too long and complex. As a result, they reduced cart abandonment by 20% by streamlining the checkout process and adding progress indications (source: NNG Group).
User Testing
There are various forms of user testing:

items: **Remote testing** includes users doing tasks in their environment, giving real-world information. Tools like UserTesting and Lookback facilitate this.
**In-person testing** involves observing users in usability labs for immediate feedback.
**A/B testing** compares two-page versions to determine the best user engagement and conversions using popular tools like Optimizely and VWO.

body.text: But you may ask how to select participants. So, use user [personas](/blog/what-are-personas) to guide selection, conduct surveys to filter participants who match your personas, and ensure a diverse group to cover various user behaviors and opinions.

**Real Example:** Airbnb decided to update its website and do user testing. An expert group observed how users interacted with their search filters and saw that it was complicated. They simplified the process, improved user experience and satisfaction, and increased bookings.
Analytics Review
Use different analytics tools to track metrics and analysis like:

items: Bounce rates
Conversion rates
Click-Through rates (CTR)
Exit rates
Session duration
Session recordings
User feedback polls
Analysis of user flows
Event tracking

body.text: We recommend the following tools: Google Analytics, Mixpanel, and Hotjar.

**Real Example:** A SaaS company conducted an analytics review and saw that users gave up on the registration process due to unclear instructions. The company used Hotjar for this purpose. After accepting changes, they improved their conversion rate by 15% (source: Hotjar Case Study).
Find out more about essential UX research methods in [our article](/blog/essential-ux-research-methods-and-how-they-are-used).
Surveys and Feedback

Feedback is important in every business. Direct feedback offers valuable qualitative information, improving understanding of users' motivations, preferences, and pain points. It provides a human perspective to complement the analytics.
If you want to get feedback about a specific service, app, website, or component, you should prepare a good survey. How do you do it correctly? We have some tips.
Effective Survey Tips

items: It must be short. Nobody likes to spend time answering many questions. Focus on key points.
It must be easy to understand. Use plain language and avoid technical jargon.
Ask open-ended questions. Allow users to give detailed answers.
Ask about key areas of interest or known problems.
Provide small rewards to encourage participation. Everybody loves gifts. Respect the user's time!

body.text: **Real Example:** After completing polls, a media corporation discovered that users want more video material. So the marketing department began creating more video content. It improved engagement and satisfaction (source: SurveyMonkey Case Studies).

We also want to share our own experience with you. Our team helped over 170 clients in reaching their goals and successful results. Learn more about [our cases](https://arounda.agency/works); there is so much interesting information. And now, let's find out how we at Arounda conduct a UX audit on a specific case.
Arounda UX Audit Example

Every digital product needs transformation to stay ahead in rapidly developing markets. So, the first step is to get a qualified UX audit. Our clients' main objectives for user experience audits are to detect pain points or validate a new product design before development. For example, let's look at three different projects.
Unlocks Calendar
Unlocks Calendar provides users with future events for unlocking crypto coins/tokens. So they can predict prices, create investment strategies, and understand circulating supplies.
During the UX audit, our expert team detected and successfully fixed **15+ usability issues** with Unlocks Calendar.
GT Protocol
GT Protocol is a Web 3.0 crypto investment platform. Our goals were to make the website unique and creative in the crypto market and user-friendly and intuitive.

After auditing and improvements, customer satisfaction with GT Protocol has increased by **32%**. Also, we reached more excellent customer retention, higher lifetime value, and a stronger brand reputation.
MintySwap

MintySwap is a digital marketplace for crypto collectibles and NFTs. Our tasks were to conduct the UX website audit, help with the UI/UX redesign, and improve functionality. To improve MintySwap, Arounda examined its UI/UX, marketplace functioning, and technical problems. We offered the best ideas and wireframes for this project.
**The results are amazing:** increased engagement by **5%**, traffic - by **22%**, community growth by **two times**, and a **21%** lower bounce rate.
Discover more about the [MintySwap case](https://arounda.agency/case/mintyswap) to get interesting insights. You are also welcome to see [other successful cases](https://arounda.agency/works).
Expert Tips for a Successful UX Design Audit

title: High-converting SaaS Landing Page Best Practices
author: Valeriia Serohina
excerpt: Creating a high-converting SaaS landing page is both an art and a science. It is the initial step to encouraging sign-ups for your solution, driving targeted traffic, and fueling product growth. A killer landing page showcases a SaaS compan

body.text: Creating a high-converting SaaS landing page is both an art and a science. It is the initial step to encouraging sign-ups for your solution, driving targeted traffic, and fueling product growth. A killer landing page showcases a SaaS company’s unique value propositions and benefits. The key to maximizing conversions is effective design, persuasive copy, and seamless user experience.

Arounda excels in designing [high-converting landing pages](/services/landing-page-design) for SaaS companies. With over 250 successful projects across niches and an average rating of 5.0 on Clutch, we create visually stunning and user-friendly landing pages like we did for [VOXE](https://arounda.agency/case/voxe). Our approach ensures every landing page design aligns closely with your business goals, enhancing online presence, driving leads, and converting visitors into loyal customers. This article shares our best practices for crafting a high converting SaaS landing page.
What is a SaaS Landing Page?

A SaaS landing page is a dedicated web page designed to highlight a software-as-a-service (SaaS) product's features and benefits with the primary goal of converting visitors into users. Unlike a homepage, which serves multiple purposes, a landing page is laser-focused on a single goal, such as encouraging sign-ups for a free trial or subscription.
SaaS landing pages are crucial for driving targeted traffic, capturing leads, and increasing conversions by providing a hyper-relevant and compelling experience.
Key Elements of a High Converting Saas Landing Page
To craft the best SaaS landing page, you should meticulously optimize several key elements. When properly implemented, these elements can significantly improve your landing page’s performance.

items: **Hero Section**. It is the first thing visitors notice when they open your page. Your hero section should include an enticing headline, a subheading explaining the value proposition, and a compelling call to action (CTA). Make it clear, concise, and straight to the point to capture attention.

**Features & Benefits**. This section details what your product does and how it benefits the user. Instead of just listing features, explain which customers’ problems they solve. A detailed comparison table of subscription features helps potential customers see the value of each tier.

**Social Proof**. Including testimonials, star ratings, case studies, and logos of notable customers builds trust and credibility. Social proof reassures visitors that your product is worth their time and investment.

**Contact Form**. A contact form is what captures your leads. Position it strategically to ensure it’s easily accessible without overwhelming the visitor. Keeping it simple and asking for minimal information increases completion rates.
**Demo Video**. It showcases your product’s core features and addresses common pain points. It’s particularly useful for complex products that are difficult to explain through text alone.

**Clear CTA**. Your CTA should stand out and be crystal clear. Avoid using multiple CTAs that can confuse the visitor. Instead, use a single, strong CTA to guide users toward the desired action, whether signing up for a free trial, subscribing to a newsletter, or booking a demo.

body.text: SaaS Landing Page Best Practices

[Arounda](https://arounda.agency/about) crafts visually stunning, user-friendly [web](/services/web-design) and [mobile designs](/services/mobile-design) that elevate SaaS landing pages, boosting online presence, lead generation, and customer loyalty. Below, we will share the best practices for creating and optimizing high-converting SaaS landing pages.
Conducting Meticulous Research

A thorough [product discovery research](/services/product-discovery) on your target audience's demographics, preferences, and pain points is the foundation for a high-converting landing page. The research will ensure that your [landing page design](/services/landing-page-design) resonates with your audience and effectively addresses their needs and motivations.
Aligning Design with Business Goals & Brand Identity

Ensure that every design element on your landing page aligns with your business objectives, including the strategic integration of your [brand identity](/services/brand-identity). It will enhance brand awareness, trust, and differentiation from competitors. As a result, you get a unified user experience that drives growth and customer loyalty.
Expertly Implementing UX/UI Principles

Implement best practices in [UX/UI design](/services/ui-ux-design) to create a seamless and intuitive user experience. This includes clear navigation, strategic placement of CTAs, and visually appealing design elements that guide users toward conversion actions. Consider [accessibility](/blog/accessibility-in-ux-best-practices-and-key-principles) and compliance with [WCAG standards](/blog/accessible-vs-inclusive-design----whats-the-difference).
Creating Visually Engaging Content

High-quality images, videos, and graphics make your landing page visually appealing and capture visitors’ attention. Ensure your visuals are relevant to your content and enhance the overall message of your page. [Engaging content](/blog/how-saas-customer-engagement-can-be-improved-by-companies) keeps visitors on your page longer and increases the likelihood of conversion.
Incorporating Compelling Copywriting

The best SaaS landing page uses persuasive copywriting that effectively communicates your unique value proposition. Clearly articulate your product's key features and benefits. Ensure that your messaging addresses the pain points of your target audience and demonstrates how your product provides solutions.
Providing Clear Navigation

While the primary goal of a landing page is to drive a specific action, you need to provide easy navigation to other relevant information. Include links to subpages where users can learn more about your product, read case studies, or access feature descriptions. Yet, keep these links minimal to avoid distractions.
Ensuring Mobile Responsiveness

With more smartphone users accessing websites, your landing page must be mobile-friendly. Test your page on various devices to ensure it loads quickly, is easy to navigate, and displays correctly on all screen sizes. [Responsive design](/blog/responsive-design-best-practices-and-considerations) significantly reduces bounce rates and increases conversions.
Optimizing Page Load Times

A slow-loading SaaS landing page drives visitors away. Use tools like Google PageSpeed Insights to check your page speed and get recommendations for improvements. Optimize images, use a content delivery network (CDN), and minimize the use of heavy scripts to ensure your page loads quickly.
Leveraging A/B Testing

Continuously test different versions of your landing page to see which elements perform best. A/B testing can help you identify what resonates with your audience and refine your page. Test variations of headlines, CTAs, images, and content layouts to find the optimal combination that drives conversions.
Tracking Key Metrics

Monitor your landing page’s performance metrics, including conversion rate, bounce rate, average time on page, and click-through rate (CTR), using tools like Google Analytics and Hotjar. Review these analytics regularly to identify and improve performance through data-driven insights and A/B testing.
Updating Content Regularly

Maintain engagement by keeping your landing page content fresh and up-to-date. Consistently adding new testimonials, case studies, and product updates demonstrates ongoing improvement and keeps visitors interested in your offerings.

The new design effectively showcases the product’s capabilities, making it easy for potential customers to see how Swift can help them make profitable trades quickly. Your SaaS landing page should achieve your conversion goals and drive your business growth. title: What are Wicked Problems? A Design Thinking Perspective
author: Valeriia Serohina
excerpt: Despite tech progress and innovations, societies and businesses still face wicked problems. What are wicked problems? Coined [in the 1970s](https://www.stonybrook.edu/commcms/wicked-problem/about/What-is-a-wicked-problem), the term refers t

body.text: Despite tech progress and innovations, societies and businesses still face wicked problems. What are wicked problems? Coined [in the 1970s](https://www.stonybrook.edu/commcms/wicked-problem/about/What-is-a-wicked-problem), the term refers to complex issues that defy easy solutions due to their incomplete or contradictory nature. In design thinking, these problems lack clear resolutions and require creativity and iterative processes.

Being a design agency, Arounda tackles wicked problems across industries with[tailored solutions](https://arounda.agency/works). Recently, we designed a [fintech](/industries/fintech) platform, [Player's Health](https://arounda.agency/case/players-health), to enhance young athletes' safety and financial management. Through iterative design, we improved new user registration, user experience, and operational efficiency. This article explores what are wicked problems in design thinking with examples.
What are Wicked Problems?

What’s the definition of a wicked problem? Well, the name speaks for itself, as it is a complex issue that is difficult to put into simple words—and almost impossible to solve. What are the characteristics of a wicked problem? It has the following traits:

items: **Complexity and uncertainty**: Wicked problems often involve many interdependent factors that are constantly changing, making it difficult to predict outcomes.
**No clear solution**: Unlike "tame" problems, wicked problems do not have a definitive solution. Any attempt to solve a wicked problem will likely generate new issues.
**Multiple stakeholders**: These problems typically involve various stakeholders with differing perspectives and conflicting interests that challenge consensus.
**Unique nature**: Each wicked problem is unique, meaning that solutions that work in one context may not be applicable in another.
**No definitive problem statement**: Wicked problems are difficult to define clearly, and one's understanding of them may change as new information emerges.

body.text: Types of wicked problems include social policy, environment, economy, and technology issues. What are wicked problems examples? Classic ones include climate change, poverty, healthcare reform, and urbanization. They involve complex interdependencies that require interdisciplinary approaches and long-term strategies to achieve meaningful solutions.
Wicked Problems in Design Thinking: Examples

In [design thinking](/blog/the-five-phases-of-design-thinking), specific issues follow the traits outlined above. What are wicked problems in design thinking? Let's explore examples illustrating the multifaceted challenges designers encounter in addressing ethical dilemmas, cultural diversity, tech advancements, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
Diversity of Design Definitions

Design eludes a singular definition or categorization, as it encompasses a broad spectrum from industrial to [graphic design](/services/graphic-design). The diverse methodologies and ideas under the umbrella of design defy reduction, continually expanding in scope and application. This diversity challenges designers to navigate various approaches and methods without a unified definition, requiring adaptability and openness in practice.
Integration of Arts & Sciences in Design

As design evolves, it increasingly integrates knowledge from both arts and sciences. This integration aims to harness the strengths of each discipline while adapting them to practical design purposes. However, the challenge lies in bridging the gap between these traditionally separate fields. It often leads to tensions between artistic expression and scientific rigor within design practice and education.
Fragmentation vs. Integration of Knowledge

The specialization of knowledge has fragmented traditional liberal arts into increasingly narrow disciplines. Design thinking attempts to counter this fragmentation by seeking integrative approaches and synthesizing diverse knowledge domains. However, achieving meaningful integration across specialized fields takes time and effort. It requires designers to navigate and connect disparate areas of expertise.
Philosophical and Theoretical Divergence in Design Education

Theoretical and practical aspects of design education often diverge, reflecting broader philosophical differences such as [neo-positivism versus pragmatism](https://limbd.org/research-philosophy-positivism-interpretivism-and-pragmatism/). Should we search for universal principles or deal with issues case-by-case? This split complicates the development of cohesive design theories and practices, impacting how design history, theory, and criticism are taught and applied. Bridging this gap fosters a more unified and practical approach to design education and practice.
Design as a Profession and Its Ethical Dimensions

Designers are confronted with ethical considerations, such as sustainability, [inclusivity](/blog/what-is-inclusive-design-main-principles-and-patterns), and social responsibility. These dimensions make them balance creative freedom with moral obligations, requiring difficult decisions that impact the environment and society. Prioritizing these factors is essential for a design practice focused on long-term societal and environmental well-being.
Globalization and Local Adaptation of Design

Globalization spreads design ideas and practices across cultures and raises questions about cultural appropriation and authenticity. Designers must consider the tension between global design trends and the need for locally relevant solutions, respecting cultural diversity and local contexts. Balancing global influences with local adaptation requires sensitivity to cultural nuances and a deep understanding of how design can positively impact communities worldwide.
Technological Advancements and Human-Centered Design

Rapid tech advancements present both opportunities and challenges for [human-centered design](/blog/key-principles-of-human-centered-design). While technologies like [AI & ML](/industries/ai) can enhance efficiency and innovation, they also raise concerns about privacy, equity, and the human experience. Designers must address these ethical implications to create meaningful, empathetic user experiences that enhance human well-being.
Interdisciplinary Collaboration and Communication in Design Teams

Effective design requires interdisciplinary collaboration, yet integrating diverse perspectives and expertise can be challenging. Communication barriers between disciplines, differing methodologies, and conflicting priorities can hinder team cohesion and project success. Designers must develop cross-disciplinary communication, empathy, and collaboration skills to address complex design challenges effectively.
How Design Thinking Addresses Wicked Problems

Wicked problems present unique opportunities for innovation in design thinking. Design thinking is particularly well-suited to addressing these problems because it emphasizes a human-centered approach, iterative development, and collaboration.
Here’s how design thinking helps tackle types of wicked problems:

items: **Empathy and understanding**: Design thinking starts with understanding user needs, motivations, and pain points. This empathetic approach is crucial for addressing the diverse and often conflicting needs of stakeholders involved in wicked problems. Arounda’s [product discovery](/services/product-discovery) service helps uncover user needs, providing a solid foundation for addressing complex issues.

**Iterative design process**: Design thinking's iterative nature allows for continuous learning and adaptation. Prototyping and testing allow designers to explore solutions, learn from failures, and refine their ideas. Our [UI/UX Design service](/services/ui-ux-design) supports this iterative approach, ensuring solutions evolve through continuous feedback and testing.

**Collaboration**: Wicked problems require the input and cooperation of diverse stakeholders. Design thinking fosters a collaborative environment where different perspectives can be integrated into problem-solving. At [Arounda](https://arounda.agency/about), we facilitate collaboration by bringing together diverse insights and expertise.

**Reframing the Problem**: Design thinking encourages looking at problems from different angles. By reframing the problem, designers can uncover new insights and opportunities for innovation. Our [Product redesign](https://arounda.agency/solutions/product-redesign) is ideal if your product needs a fresh look, improved user experience, or enhanced functionality.

**Flexibility and Adaptability**: Design thinking embraces ambiguity and uncertainty, allowing designers to remain flexible and adaptable as they navigate the complexities of wicked problems. Arounda's [UX Audit](/services/ux-audit) service helps ensure products stay competitive and versatile in changing environments.

body.text: With these principles, designers can effectively address the complexities of wicked problems, creating innovative and impactful solutions.
Conclusion
The definition of a wicked problem in design thinking is a complex challenge that resists straightforward solutions due to its evolving and multifaceted nature. They are characterized by:

items: Complexity and uncertainty
Lack of clear solutions
Involvement of multiple stakeholders
Unique nature
No definitive problem statement

body.text: You can tackle wicked problems with design thinking by emphasizing a human-centered approach, iterative development, and collaborative problem-solving.

At Arounda, we pioneer cutting-edge projects that push the boundaries of technology, utilizing robust methodologies like design thinking. We go beyond superficial solutions by ideating, prototyping, and rigorously testing ideas to ensure resilient user experiences. Whether you require support in intricate [UI/UX design](/services/ui-ux-design), branding strategies, or product strategy development,[just get in touch](https://arounda.agency/contact)!

title: How Repetition, Pattern, and Rhythm Work in Design
author: Alyona Deieieva
excerpt: Using repetition, pattern, and rhythm in design sparks debate in the creative industry. Some argue that repeated elements stifle creativity, while others emphasize its importance for achieving stunning visual results and enhancing user expe

body.text: Using repetition, pattern, and rhythm in design sparks debate in the creative industry. Some argue that repeated elements stifle creativity, while others emphasize its importance for achieving stunning visual results and enhancing user experience. Balancing creativity with usability is key to effective holistic design.

[Arounda](https://arounda.agency/about), an expert in [web](/services/web-design) and [UI/UX design](/services/ui-ux-design), crafts innovative solutions for [AI](/industries/ai), [SaaS](/industries/saas), and [Web 3.0](/industries/web3) like [VOXE](https://arounda.agency/case/voxe). Our [brand identity](/services/brand-identity) services make your brand recognizable by consistently using repeated design elements. What is the difference between repetition pattern and rhythm? How do they ensure your brand’s cohesive and engaging presence? This article will share how strategically applying repeated design elements boosts aesthetic appeal and delivers tangible business benefits.
Repetition: Building Brand Consistency and Recognition

What is pattern and repetition? Repetition involves the deliberate use of the same visual elements such as logos, colors, shapes, fonts, and menu items throughout a design. This technique provides a consistent user experience, aligning their expectations with what they see. Additionally, repeating messages reinforces critical information, making it more memorable.
For businesses, repetition serves several important purposes:

items: **Brand Recognition:** By repeating logos and brand elements across various touchpoints—such as websites, social media, packaging, and advertising—businesses reinforce their visual identity. Consistency creates familiarity, helping customers recognize and remember the brand effortlessly.

**Establishing Trust:** Consistent branding instills confidence in consumers. When they encounter familiar elements repeatedly, it signals reliability and professionalism. This trust builds the foundation for brand loyalty and cultivates enduring customer relationships.

**Operational Efficiency:** Internally, repetition streamlines design workflows using templates, style guides, and standardized elements. This reduces production time and costs, ensures consistent branding, and promotes efficient team collaboration and visual coherence.

body.text: Pattern: Enhancing Visual Appeal and User Experience

What is the difference between repetition and pattern? Unlike repetition of the same object, patterns consist of multiple components that recur to create visual harmony and interest. A seamless pattern is characterized by its uninterrupted flow, forming a cohesive whole without clear beginnings or endings. These elements are crucial for designs with extensive use of color, texture, or depth, ensuring a unified and visually appealing outcome.

When integrating patterns into digital design, it's essential to assess their complexity, readability, and UX proximity. This ensures that text remains easily visible against patterned backgrounds, preserving a seamless user experience. In business contexts, patterns are crucial for:

items: **Visual Engagement:** Intriguing patterns capture attention and draw users into design. Whether used in product packaging, digital interfaces, or physical spaces, patterns create a memorable visual impact that enhances brand recall.

**Branding through Environment:** In retail and interior design, patterns on surfaces like walls, floors, or merchandise enhance ambiance and reinforce brand aesthetics. They create a cohesive brand experience that resonates with customers on a subconscious level.
**Differentiation:** Unique custom patterns can distinguish a brand, setting businesses apart. They contribute to brand exclusivity and strengthen brand identity.

body.text: Rhythm: Guiding User Interaction and Navigation

Rhythm in design defines the flow and movement of visual elements. Pattern repetition and rhythm principle of design emphasizes the strategic arrangement of elements to create visual harmony and coherence within compositions. Unlike uniform and static repetition and patterns, rhythm organizes diverse elements in dynamic sequences. There are four types of rhythm: regular, flowing, progressive, and alternating. Each of them varies in the form of element repetition throughout the composition.

Repetition and rhythm examples in design can be seen in the rhythmic arrangement of typography that guides the viewer's eye through a webpage. Rhythm shapes user perception and interaction with content. In business design strategies, it is critical for:

items: **User Experience Optimization:** In digital design, rhythm organizes content and intuitively guides user navigation. Strategic spacing, grid layouts, and interactive elements create a rhythm that enhances usability. It helps reduce bounce rates and increase engagement metrics.

**Emotional Connection:** Different rhythms evoke specific emotions. A steady rhythm conveys stability and reliability, while a dynamic rhythm evokes excitement or urgency. Aligning rhythm with marketing objectives enhances emotional engagement with the brand.

**Consistent Messaging:** Rhythmic consistency reinforces brand messaging. By controlling the pace of information delivery, businesses ensure clarity and coherence in communication strategies. It helps convey brand values and key messages effectively.

body.text: Practical Tips for Designing with Repetition, Pattern, and Rhythm
Strategic implementation of repeated design elements enhances usability, aesthetic appeal, and business outcomes. Here are some tips to maximize their impact:
Repetition

items: **Establish Visual Consistency**: Repeat key design elements such as logos, colors, and typography across all pages and interfaces. This consistency helps users navigate seamlessly and reinforces brand identity.

**Highlight Important Information**: Use repetition to draw attention to critical content or calls to action. For example, you can repeat a vibrant color or a distinct shape to emphasize a promotional banner or a signup button.

**Create Visual Hierarchies**: Employ repetition to establish visual hierarchies within the design. Consistently used elements can guide users through the interface, signaling the importance of different content blocks or navigation paths.
**Enhance Navigation**: Repeat navigation items in predictable locations across pages. This practice ensures users can easily find and access essential features without confusion.

body.text: Pattern

items: **Choose Appropriate Patterns**: Select patterns that complement the brand’s aesthetic and enhance the user experience. Patterns should not overpower content but rather provide visual interest and cohesion.
**Consider Scalability**: Ensure patterns are scalable across various screen sizes and devices. Test patterns to verify readability and visual appeal on both desktop and mobile interfaces.

**Use Patterns for Visual Continuity**: Apply patterns consistently across pages of the same type (e.g., product pages, blog posts) to create a cohesive visual identity. This continuity reinforces the brand’s presence and reinforces user familiarity.
**Balance Visual Complexity**: Avoid overly intricate patterns distracting from the main content. Opt for patterns that add depth and texture without overwhelming the overall design.

body.text: Rhythm

items: **Create Emotional Impact**: Use rhythmic variations to evoke specific emotions or guide user interaction. For instance, a gradual build-up of visual elements can create excitement, while a steady rhythm promotes a sense of calm and reliability.

**Adapt Rhythm to Content**: Tailor the rhythm to suit the content and context of the design. For example, dynamic rhythms may be suitable for interactive interfaces, while a more uniform rhythm may enhance readability in content-heavy pages.

**Guide User Flow**: Design with rhythmic sequences that intuitively guide users through the interface. Utilize spacing, pacing, and interactive elements to create a natural flow from one section to another.

**Keep Consistency in Motion**: Maintain consistency in the pacing and movement of elements throughout the design. Consistent rhythm enhances usability by providing users with predictable navigation and interaction patterns.

body.text: Using these tips, you can create visually appealing designs, optimize user experience, and strengthen brand identity with repetition, pattern, and rhythm. These principles help craft engaging interfaces that drive higher engagement and user satisfaction.
Conclusion

Incorporating repetition, pattern, and rhythm into design strategies isn’t merely about aesthetics—it’s a strategic approach to enhancing business outcomes. From strengthening [brand identity](/services/brand-identity) to improving [user experience](/services/ui-ux-design), these design elements are pivotal in achieving broader business goals. By understanding their impact and implementing them thoughtfully, you can create visually compelling narratives that resonate with your target audiences, driving engagement, loyalty, and business success.
