title: What is Wireframing?
author: Valeriia Serohina
excerpt: Imagine a designer describing how your app will look using words only. You agree based on your imagination, but the result surprises you. This is how the world of design could be if people had never discovered what is wireframing in web des

body.text: Imagine a designer describing how your app will look using words only. You agree based on your imagination, but the result surprises you. This is how the world of design could be if people had never discovered what is wireframing in web design.

[Arounda](https://arounda.agency/about) has extensive experience in [UI/UX design](/services/ui-ux-design), and our experts know how to describe their ideas visually with clarity and efficiency. Wireframes serve as an ideal tool for maintaining transparency for our clients in decision-making. In this article, we'll explain wireframes and why they are important.
What is Wireframing in UX Design?

A wireframe is a blueprint that helps designers and stakeholders align on requirements, keeping conversations focused and constructive. Simply put, it is a two-dimensional outline of a webpage or app.
Wireframes maintain clear communication regarding the page structure, layout, information architecture, user flow, functionality, and intended behaviors. They can be hand-drawn or created digitally.

Wireframes are often presented to stakeholders such as developers, researchers, and investors to agree on concepts before building the actual interface with code. They outline the essential elements of your design, including screen layouts, navigation bars, UI and UX components, and interactive elements.

Usually, wireframing follows research, the creation of user flows, and sometimes UX mapping. For instance, during the [Myso](https://arounda.agency/case/myso) project, we’ve mapped the app flow first and used it to work out wireframes.
Why Use Wireframes
If you are interested in what is wireframing in design, you are probably looking for arguments as to why it should be part of the design process. Wireframing:

items: Saves time and money. Wireframes reduce the number of design phases needed, minimizing costly and time-consuming revisions later in the project.

Visualizes ideas effectively. Wireframes provide a clear visual representation of design ideas, helping designers assess their feasibility in real-world contexts. They are invaluable for validating concepts through user testing before committing to final prototypes.
Enhances user-centered design. By keeping user needs at the forefront, wireframes ensure that designs are intuitive and aligned with user behaviors, ultimately improving the user experience.

Facilitates early feedback. Early-stage wireframes allow stakeholders and users to provide feedback on fundamental design elements and usability considerations, fostering confidence in the final product.

Ensures clear content and functionality placement. Wireframes establish a structured framework for content and functionality, ensuring that these elements are positioned strategically based on user and business requirements. They serve as a collaborative reference point for project teams, promoting clear communication and consensus on project scope.

body.text: Types of Wireframing

To fully understand what is wireframing in web design, let’s focus on its levels: low-, mid-, and high-fidelity. Designers progress through these stages to refine their designs towards the final product. Each level serves distinct purposes aimed at achieving a well-structured and user-centered outcome.
Low-Fidelity

Low-fidelity wireframes focus on layout, navigation, and information architecture. They outline the basic structure and user flows using simple UI elements. They are sketched or created digitally. Tools like Figma facilitate easy creation, sharing, and iteration.
Mid-Fidelity

Mid-fidelity wireframes refine designs with annotations and content, exploring different user flows and UI approaches. This stage defines core functionality and interactions, providing a more transparent framework before adding detailed visual elements.
High-Fidelity

[High-fidelity](/blog/ux-prototypes-low-fidelity-vs-high-fidelity) wireframes resemble early product mockups, incorporating interactive and visual design elements for user testing. They simulate the final product's look and feel with brand elements like fonts and colors, gathering feedback to inform development phases effectively.
Tips for Correct Wireframing

Wireframing marks the initial stages of a project, essential for refining ideas into a polished product. In our collaboration with [Voxe](https://arounda.agency/case/voxe), it optimized communication and agreement on proposals. Here are some tips to streamline your work.
Define Your Design Goals

Before starting, clearly define your design goals. Consider user needs and the actions you want them to take, such as solving a problem or signing up for a service. Align your team around these goals to ensure your wireframes advance the intended objectives.
Choose The Appropriate Size
Match your wireframes to the screen sizes your audience will use:

items: Mobile: 1080 pixels wide by 1920 pixels long
8” Tablet: 800 pixels wide by 1280 pixels long
10” Tablet: 1200 pixels wide by 1920 pixels long
Desktop: 768 pixels wide by 1366 pixels long

body.text: It ensures your design looks appropriate on different devices.
Keep It Simple

Start with grayscale colors, minimal fonts, and simple boxes for graphics. Focus on meeting user requirements at a basic level without getting distracted by details like color schemes. Using real content instead of placeholder text provides a more accurate representation of content-rich interfaces.
Ensure Consistency

Maintain consistent design across all wireframes. Similar components should look the same to prevent confusion and ensure developers can understand and code them accurately. Avoid variations that create uncertainty during development.
Stay Flexible

Remember that even high-fidelity wireframes are still rough drafts. They will need adjustments and modifications to evolve into the final product. Once your design team finalizes the wireframe, collaborate with developers and other creative team members to integrate functionality and make necessary changes.
Summary

Over the past seven years, the Arounda team has experimented with various approaches to project development. To save time and minimize client expenses, we chose to use wireframes. Having completed over 250 UI/UX projects, our designers mastered the art of creating and adapting them for each unique project.

We hope that this post helped you answer the question "What is wireframing in UX?" and understand its role in visualizing ideas, streamlining brainstorming, and boosting confidence in project outcomes. title: What are Conceptual Models?
author: Valeriia Serohina
excerpt: Think about how it feels when you discover a product that's incredibly easy to use. It seems to anticipate your every move, making interactions seamless and intuitive. And you're likely to keep coming back to use it again.

body.text: Think about how it feels when you discover a product that's incredibly easy to use. It seems to anticipate your every move, making interactions seamless and intuitive. And you're likely to keep coming back to use it again.

At Arounda, creating products like this is our top priority. [Check out our work](https://arounda.agency/works): whether it's a financial product, a healthcare project, or a SaaS solution, we're always focused on making user-friendly products. Using conceptual models is key to achieving this. In this article, we'll share our experience in helping boost customer loyalty.
What are the Conceptual Models
Conceptual models are abstract, psychological representations of how to carry out tasks. They are mental maps that people use subconsciously to systematize processes.

In design, these models highlight key concepts, variables, relationships, and assumptions, guiding the creation of user-friendly systems. By aligning interfaces with users' existing mental frameworks, designers make new products more intuitive and easier to use.
What Does a Conceptual Model Consist of?

With extensive experience in [product redesign](https://arounda.agency/solutions/product-redesign), especially in [UI/UX design](/services/ui-ux-design), we create detailed conceptual models. To help you understand these models better, we'll break down their components using a [login page](/blog/10-examples-of-login-page-design-best-practices) as an example of a conceptual model. It will illustrate the three main components: entities, relationships, and constraints.
Entities
Entities are the primary components that users interact with or manipulate within the system. In the context of a login page, the entities include:

items: Username Field: Where users enter their username.
Password Field: Where users enter their password.
Login Button: To submit the login form.
Forgot Password Link: To help users recover their password.

body.text: Relationships
Relationships define how the entities interact or relate to each other within the system. In the case of the login page:

items: The username and password fields must be correctly filled for the login to be successful.
When the user clicks the login button, the system checks the entered username and password against the database for authentication.
Clicking the "Forgot Password" link redirects the user to the password recovery process to regain access to their account.

body.text: These relationships establish the rules and logic governing how the entities (such as fields and buttons) function together to achieve specific tasks or processes.
Constraints

Constraints are limitations that apply to entities or relationships, defining the boundaries and conditions within which the system operates. They ensure the security, usability, and integrity of the system by enforcing rules that govern user interactions and system behaviors. For the login page, it might be:

items: Password Requirements. Constraints may include rules such as minimum character length, including special characters, or the requirement for a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters.
Account Lockout. After multiple failed login attempts, the system may impose a constraint on the account, causing it to be temporarily locked for security reasons.

Security Measures. The "Forgot Password" process may include constraints such as answering security questions or providing a recovery email to verify the user's identity before allowing password reset.

body.text: Why Use Conceptual Models?
What are conceptual models used for? Conceptual models are valuable tools in research for several reasons:

items: They help researchers clearly express their ideas, assumptions, and perspectives.
These models highlight gaps, inconsistencies, or contradictions in existing knowledge, aiding in better understanding.
They ensure that research objectives, questions, and methods are consistent with the underlying concepts and theories, providing a logical basis for interpretation and discussion.
Conceptual models make comparing, integrating, and synthesizing information from different studies or sources easier.
By integrating diverse information, these models help generate new insights, hypotheses, and recommendations.

body.text: What are the Types of Conceptual Models
To fully understand "what are conceptual models," you should explore their three main types. This exploration clarifies your inquiry and aids in choosing the right one for various situations.

items: **Mental Models**. These are people's ideas and expectations based on their experiences. When encountering a new system, users try to fit it into their existing knowledge framework. This mental model shapes how they understand and anticipate the system to function.

**Represented Models. **Created by designers, represented models visually depict how the system works. These can include flowcharts, sketches, and examples. They are tools to help users understand the system's functionality and how to interact with it effectively.

**System Image. **This is the perception users form about the system based on its appearance and behavior. Ideally, the system image aligns with users' mental models and the designers' represented models, ensuring a seamless and intuitive user experience.

body.text: How to Evaluate

[Here at Arounda](https://arounda.agency/about), we always analyze the effectiveness of our chosen working methods. This ensures that we are not wasting the team's time but adding value. It is important to add that evaluating conceptual models is subjective and context-specific, emphasizing the importance of feedback and continual improvement.
When working with conceptual models, it's important to consider these metrics:

items: Clarity. Ensure the model is clear and easy to understand. Minimize ambiguities and use precise definitions to help stakeholders and users grasp its concepts effectively.
Coherence. Check for logical consistency within the model. Ensure that defined components and relationships make sense and align with established theories or empirical evidence where applicable.
Comprehensiveness. Assess the model's scope and coverage. It should encompass all relevant aspects of the problem or system it aims to represent without omitting crucial factors or interactions.

Credibility. Evaluate the model's credibility by examining the sources and methods used in its development. Are the assumptions realistic and supported by evidence or expert consensus? Transparent construction enhances credibility.

Creativity. Consider the originality and innovation of the model. Does it offer new insights or approaches to understanding the problem or system? Creative models may introduce novel perspectives or solutions.

body.text: Also, the evaluation process should be iterative. It helps refine models, making them stronger and more applicable to real-world situations. To evaluate models effectively, we recommend using the following methods:

items: Peer Review. Seek feedback from experts in the field to critique the model. Peer review offers diverse perspectives and identifies strengths and weaknesses that developers may overlook.

Comparison. Compare the conceptual model with existing models or frameworks that address similar problems or systems. Highlighting similarities and differences can uncover unique contributions or areas that need enhancement.

Application. Test the model by applying it to real-world cases or datasets. This empirical validation helps evaluate its practical usefulness, validity across different contexts, and potential limitations under various conditions.

body.text: Summary
At Arounda, we've learned that paying attention to details and deeply engaging with projects is challenging but consistently effective.

Using conceptual models and other methods helps us achieve impressive outcomes. For example, for [MintySwap](https://arounda.agency/case/mintyswap), a user-centered design approach doubled their community size. And for [Myso](https://arounda.agency/case/myso), our enhancements boosted user satisfaction rates to 85%.

We hope that our conceptual modeling examples will inspire you to develop an intuitive, [human-centered design](/blog/key-principles-of-human-centered-design). If you're prepared to enhance your business and seek a partner to create a product encouraging customers to become ambassadors, [contact us](https://arounda.agency/contact).

title: Product Designer vs. UX Designer: Who's the Best Fit?
author: Oleksii Kovalchuk
excerpt: In today’s tech industry, titles and responsibilities may be confusing. Designers are no exception. Although the designation and some duties of product designers and UX designers seem identical, a closer look reveals some essential differen

body.text: In today’s tech industry, titles and responsibilities may be confusing. Designers are no exception. Although the designation and some duties of product designers and UX designers seem identical, a closer look reveals some essential differences between these roles.

Since 2016, Arounda has been helping businesses with [product design](/services/product-discovery) and [UI/UX design](/services/ui-ux-design). In this article, we will outline the critical distinctions and similarities between the specialists responsible for those two tasks.
Who is Who: Product Designer vs User Experience Designer
If there is a question about who would better fit your company's needs, a Product designer or a UX/UI designer, let’s check on both career peculiarities.
Product Designers

A Product Designer is like a jack-of-all-trades. They unite different teams during product development, ensuring the final product is user-friendly, visually appealing, and meets both business and user needs. Their knowledge and skills touch upon various fields, including psychology, user research, marketing, entrepreneurship, and content creation.

Such specialists should know the duties of various professionals, including UX designers,[graphic designers](/blog/10-reasons-why-graphic-design-is-important-for-business), researchers, analysts, prototypers, marketers, and business strategists. They must know the technologies and frameworks developers use to be efficient and fast. They should be able to perform tests, evaluate results, and make alterations.
Here are the key responsibilities of a product designer at each step of product creation:

items: **Discovery: **researching users' needs and problems to locate the main pain points.
**Ideation: **brainstorming ideas, creating initial sketches and wireframes, developing user personas, mapping out user journeys, etc.
**Design: **developing and maintaining a design system, conducting usability testing on prototypes, etc.
**Development and testing**: providing developers with detailed design specifications and guidelines and working closely with them to ensure correct implementation, reviewing the developed product
**Launch and evaluation: **ensuring a successful launch and gathering feedback
**Updates**: continuous testing and improvement**.**

body.text: User Experience Designer (UX)

The main job of UX designers is to improve the visual appearance of products and, thus, the user experience. They focus on developing a logical layout, structure, and navigation scheme that enables the user to interact with the product effectively. Their primary function lies in solving users’ issues. UX designers create mock-ups of how the final product would look and work before the targeted audience accesses it.
Check out our UX/UI Design solutions for [a crypto gambling platform Shuffle](/works), and [a Web3 finance platform MYSO](https://arounda.agency/case/myso), to see the Arounda team in action.
Difference between a UX Designer and a Product Designer

While the roles of a product designer and a UX designer can overlap, the latter is narrower. Product designers work with the same UX tools and methods as UX designers. However, while product designers develop concepts and ideas for the products and guide the product development process, UX designers focus on the product's usability.
Product Designer vs UX Designer Salary

According to [Glassdoor](https://www.glassdoor.com/Salaries/ux-designer-salary-SRCH_KO0,11.htm?countryRedirect=true), product designers earn slightly more than UX designers, reflecting their broader scope of responsibilities. Here is the comparison table for your convenience.
Dual Role Model: Why We Speak about UX & UI together?

So, we discussed the distinction between Product Designer vs User Experience Designer. You might have noticed that we included an Interface designer while speaking of UX. Let's quickly explain why we put UI together with UX experts. Digital product designers are compared to UX designers and other roles of greater importance in digital product design. However, a single professional often covers UX (experience) and UI (interface). Why it happened?

To expand on this, UI designers focus on the visual aspects of a product, such as layout, colors, and typography. In contrast, UX designers ensure the user experience is comprehensive, exceptional, and easy to navigate. Firms value designers who can make both. Efficiently maneuver UI and UX to create highly integrated and user-friendly products. So, one employee uses the combined skills to design visually appealing products with a great user experience. Realizing how UI impacts UX is significant in creating a superior digital product. Here is why so many job-givers require a 2in1 specialist UX/UI designer.
Intriguing Facts from Stats on UX/UI and Product Design

items: Product design isn’t slowing down either. From 2025 to 2030, it’s expected to grow almost [11%](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/product-design-and-development?utm_source=chatgpt.com) annually, with big demand coming from industries like healthcare and consumer tech.
Every dollar you put into UX could bring back a hundred. That’s a [9,900%](https://vwo.com/blog/web-design-statistics/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) return. Pretty incredible, right?

Just by improving your UX design, you could boost your conversion rates by up to [400%](https://vwo.com/blog/web-design-statistics/?utm_source=chatgpt.com). That’s the power of a better user experience.

The UX industry is expected to jump from [$6.4 billion](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/ux-services-market-108780) in 2025 to nearly $55 billion by 2032. That’s a massive 36% growth rate each year.

body.text: Conclusion
Speaking of the main difference between a UX Designer and a Product Designer, we consider that:

items: **UX/UI Designer**. Creates intuitive and visually appealing user interfaces, focusing primarily on the user experience.
**Product Designer.** Oversees the entire product development process, balancing user experience with business goals.

body.text: If you face difficulty choosing a digital Product Designer vs UX Designer, deep dive into the core understanding of each position. The unique contributions of product and UX designers can help you decide which role best fits your company's needs. You may require a wide approach to product development or a specialized focus on user experience. The right designer can make all the difference in creating a successful and user-friendly product.

title: How to Give Good Design Feedback as a Client?
author: Oleksii Kovalchuk
excerpt: Have you ever received feedback from customers that leaves you devastated and empty?

body.text: Have you ever received feedback from customers that leaves you devastated and empty?

As a design firm, we at Arounda know the value of good design feedback. No matter what we're working on, whether it's [UI/UX design](/services/ui-ux-design) or [product redesign](https://arounda.agency/solutions/product-redesign), quality feedback ensures our team stays aligned with clients and their goals. In this article, based on our experience, we'll share the best ways of giving design feedback as a client.
The Importance of Effective Design Feedback
Poor feedback management can [cause new products to fail](/blog/reasons-why-new-products-fail-and-how-to-avoid-it). For several reasons, feedback is essential for both designers and clients.

items: It acts as a reality check, offering valuable insights that designers might miss when they're too close to a project. This feedback is like a mirror, revealing the effectiveness of design choices and guiding improvements.
Feedback fuels innovation by fostering a continuous learning process. It validates design choices and pinpoints areas for refinement, allowing designers to iterate and enhance their products.

Design feedback sharing is part of a collaboration among team members, clients, and stakeholders. It enables thorough review and analysis of design ideas, highlighting strengths and areas for improvement.

body.text: If you know how to give feedback to a designer, you will get better results on a project. Therefore, feedback isn't just a one-time event but a vital part of the iterative design process, ensuring that products evolve to effectively meet user needs.
When to Give Design Feedback?

One of the most popular design feedback questions is finding the best time to share your thoughts. Learn how to choose the right moment, whether you [create a product page](/blog/create-a-product-page-tips-and-tricks) or make a [website redesign](/services/website-redesign). Here are some examples of when to share your suggestions.
Before Work Starts

Use this moment to give comprehensive feedback on previous projects or references. This knowledge will help designers understand your preferences and set guidelines for future collaborations. It also saves time and ensures alignment right from the start.
After The Design Presentation
Explaining underlying principles often clarifies design concepts. This post-presentation feedback fosters informed evaluation and constructive discussions to refine the design direction.
At the Finish Stage

Interrupting the creative process can disrupt flow and productivity. Instead, save feedback for key milestones. This approach allows designers to explore ideas while ensuring timely guidance to steer the project in the desired direction.
Leave the Choice To Your Designers

Encourage an open dialogue, inviting them to specify the best times for feedback. Actively involving them demonstrates trust and respect for their expertise. It will also foster a collaborative environment that promotes innovation and growth.
How to Give Feedback to a Designer

You can explore various methods to give good feedback. However, when it comes to urgent real-time communication, you may not have time to search for this information. Therefore, the main goal is to be constructive and not to offend the person.
Think about whether you would accept the feedback you plan to give if you were in the designer's shoes. Then, use the main life hacks from us that we leverage in the team.
Be Clear and Specific
Identify concrete examples of encountered challenges. Instead of vague preferences, explain why certain elements aren't working and share your reasoning behind the feedback.
Vague feedback can be confusing. Instead, helpful feedback suggests actionable changes, such as adjusting colors, fonts, or the placement of some elements.
Choose the Correct Format

When giving design feedback, think about the best way to deliver it. While general concepts are okay to discuss during the meeting, it's better to point out specific edits. This way, the designer can implement them accurately. Also, it will be more simple for you to have changes reviewed. If you give text edits verbally, be aware of the higher chance for errors and difficulty checking them effectively in that format.
Give Context

Connect your feedback to the project's goals and business objectives. Sharing insights helps align the team and enhances their work. Also, it ensures decisions are aligned with what's best for the project rather than personal preferences.
Provide Actionable Feedback

When offering feedback, provide actionable suggestions and highlight areas for improvement. Rather than prescribing solutions, focus on articulating the problems. Designers should grasp what isn't working and why.
If you have ideas for solutions, feel free to share them. However, remain open to leveraging the designer's experience to determine the optimal approach.
Make It Consolidated

Consolidated feedback is crucial for project efficiency. Conflicting directions can cause delays and confusion. To streamline the process, designate a single point of contact to gather feedback from the team and ensure consensus before providing input. Also, keeping the team small helps maintain focus and clarity in decision-making.
Stay Objective and Professional

Evaluate the design, not the person. Avoid letting personal biases influence your feedback. Approach feedback sessions with politeness and friendliness. Respectful criticism fosters a positive work environment.
Summary
At Arounda, we've learned that no project can thrive in a vacuum without feedback. Refining how we give and receive feedback has made our designers' work more efficient.

With extensive experience in UI/UX and Web Design, working on projects like [VOXE](https://arounda.agency/case/voxe) and [Player’s Health](https://arounda.agency/case/players-health), we can confidently say that insights from the article have been tested in practice.

If you're seeking the right answer to "How to give design feedback?", simply use them as a guide, adapting to your specific needs. If our approach to communication aligns with your values and you're seeking a reliable design partner, don't hesitate to[contact us](https://arounda.agency/contact).

title: How UX Design Can Solve Business Problems
author: Vlad Gavriluk
excerpt: Why UX is important for business? If done well, it facilitates accessibility, provides a competitive advantage, reduces customer support costs, and helps to deal with other problems businesses face.

body.text: Why UX is important for business? If done well, it facilitates accessibility, provides a competitive advantage, reduces customer support costs, and helps to deal with other problems businesses face.

With years of experience creating user-centered designs, conducting in-depth user research, and developing innovative solutions for projects such as [Infinity](https://arounda.agency/case/infinity) and [Voxe](https://arounda.agency/case/voxe), we know how UX can transform your business. Let’s examine why [UX design](/services/ui-ux-design) is worth the time and effort.
The Power of UX Design in Business
Solving UX problems goes beyond appearance — it’s about tackling real business challenges. Take a look at various business problem examples:

items: Enhancing user engagement and retention
Reducing customer support costs
Increasing conversion rates
Simplifying complex processes
Improving overall customer satisfaction

body.text: A problem [one of our clients](https://arounda.agency/case/myso) encountered was satisfying the diverse needs of different clients, such as borrowers, arrangers, and lenders. Our solution was to organize the data and create a comprehensive app flow that effectively met these diverse needs.

Another challenge was updating an existing platform to modern standards. To solve this, we aimed to update the original platform with a Web 3.0 look, ensuring it remains relevant and appealing in the current digital landscape.
Investing in UX design brings numerous benefits that can positively impact a business’s bottom line:

items: **Boosting conversion rates.** Many companies' top goal is increasing conversion rates. Good UX design is essential for this. Companies that address UX problems create smoother, more intuitive user journeys, leading to higher conversions. One way to raise the number of completed transactions is to make the checkout experience easier. Fixing UX design problem examples like obscured calls to action, complex navigation, and slow loading will increase conversion rates.

**Early issue identification**. UX design involves creating prototypes and wireframes, which allows designers and developers to test and refine the product before significant resources are invested in development. This technique assists in identifying and addressing possible difficulties early on, eliminating the need for expensive adjustments later in the development cycle.

**Iterative testing**. Using iterative testing and feedback loops throughout the design phase allows developers to make changes depending on real-world user interactions and feedback. This proactive strategy guarantees that the final product meets user requirements and expectations, saving time and money.

**Regulatory compliance**. Many areas have legislative standards for digital accessibility (such as the ADA in the United States and the WCAG recommendations). Ensuring compliance from the start may help avoid legal concerns and possible penalties, saving money and safeguarding the brand's image.

**Wider audience reach**. Accessible designs cater to a broader audience, increasing the potential customer base. This inclusivity can lead to higher user satisfaction and loyalty, as more people can successfully use the product.

**Brand loyalty**. Exceptional UX can lead to increased customer satisfaction and loyalty. Satisfied users are more likely to become repeat customers and recommend the product to others, driving organic growth and reducing marketing costs.
**Market positioning**. Companies known for their excellent UX are often seen as innovative and customer-centric, enhancing their market positioning and brand image.

**Error prevention**. Effective UX design can anticipate and prevent common user errors by providing clear instructions, error messages, and feedback, which reduces frustration and the need for support.

body.text: UX Strategies to Boost Your Business
How to leverage UX design for maximum business impact? Start by considering the steps listed below.
UX Audit

[UX audit](/services/ux-audit) is an essential component of UX business strategy for an established product. Design problem examples include poorly placed buttons, inconsistent navigation, ambiguous labels, unclear error messages, and small clickable areas. These annoy users and affect metrics, and businesses may raise customer satisfaction by tackling them.
Personalization

One of the most impactful UX solutions is crafting personalized experiences. Personalization makes interaction more relevant and engaging. When you leverage data and user feedback, you can tailor your offerings to individual preferences. Consequently, your customers are likely to stay with you longer.
Customized suggestions raise sales and enhance customer satisfaction in an online store. In applications, customized interfaces may facilitate and simplify navigating.
Process Innovation and Trend Setting

One of the [UX design challenge](/blog/10-design-challenges-in-web3)examples is streamlining intricate procedures. For instance, redesigning a laborious registration procedure may increase sign-up percentages and reduce dropout rates. Another example of process innovation is streamlining the checkout process to reduce cart abandonment and enhance customer satisfaction. Thought-through UX not only addresses current issues but promotes you as a leader in the field.
Addressing Customer Needs
Effective UX design starts with understanding the user. You conduct research and gather user feedback, which allows you to pinpoint pain points and areas for improvement.

For instance, interviewing gym users and trainers may reveal that existing fitness apps are overly complicated and lack personalized workout plans. Simplifying the interface and adding tailored routines results in a user-friendly app that meets users' needs and boosts engagement.

The user priorities may vary from industry to industry. For instance, in [banking](/blog/how-to-create-the-best-digital-banking-ux), you should balance usability with security, and in [healthcare](/blog/healthcare-ux-ui-challenges-innovations), UI clarity for all user categories (patients and doctors) is imperative.
Uncovering the Core Value

If you emphasize a product or service's core value through UX design, you'll highlight what sets you apart. Clear communication, consistent branding, and continuous improvement based on user feedback point out the most valuable features and benefits. An engaging and visually appealing design fosters an emotional connection with users, which can significantly enhance the product’s perceived value.
Conclusion

Successful [UX design](/services/ui-ux-design) drives business success and growth. It boosts conversion rates, ensures compliance, and broadens audience reach. What’s even more important, it can set your business apart on the market and help to keep your clients satisfied and loyal.

At [Arounda](https://arounda.agency/about), we deliver top-notch UX design solutions that address your unique business challenges. If you are looking for an experienced team to design our new product or [redesign](https://arounda.agency/solutions/product-redesign) an existing one, [let’s have a talk](https://arounda.agency/contact)!

title: What is Skeuomorphism: Definition, History, And Use Cases
author: Valeriia Serohina
excerpt: Skeuomorphism might be a tongue-twister, but it's a crucial aspect of UI design. With its help alone, designers can make digital products more familiar to users and their functions easier to recognize. However, not everyone is a fan, and it

body.text: Skeuomorphism might be a tongue-twister, but it's a crucial aspect of UI design. With its help alone, designers can make digital products more familiar to users and their functions easier to recognize. However, not everyone is a fan, and it's not always the best solution for a project.

As a design agency with extensive experience, [Arounda](https://arounda.agency/about) creates human-centric solutions for the world's top companies. We are deeply familiar with all design styles and approaches, including skeuomorphism, and we want to share our knowledge with you in this article.
What does skeuomorphism look like? Read further to discover and learn which purpose it serves and what alternatives to it to consider for your design projects.
The Definition of Skeuomorphism

Let's start with the skeuomorphism definition. Skeuomorphism is the approach to design that makes items resemble something familiar, such as real-life objects we use in our daily lives. For instance, adding shades and textures to an icon can make it resemble a physical button more. This, in turn, helps a user spot such an icon within an interface and interact with it. That's why this concept most commonly works in [UI/UX designs](/services/ui-ux-design).
History of Skeuomorphism

The concept of skeuomorphism dates back to at least 1890, but its roots trace back even further in history. You can see it already in ancient craftsmanship, where artisans often made new items mimicking the forms and decorations of older and more familiar items. For instance, pottery that looked like silver cups. This trend got new life in the industrial era, with early electric lights resembling candlesticks and gas lamps. The digital age took skeuomorphism to a new level, as tech giants like Apple and Microsoft employed this approach in their solutions.
Skeuomorphism Pros and Cons

Okay, we’ve answered, “What is skeuomorphism design?” However, when is it appropriate to use? Just like with any other technique, there’s no universal approach. Keep your mind open and use it when it will be truly beneficial.
To understand this, let's explore some of the main benefits and drawbacks of skeuomorphism in your projects.
The benefits are:

items: Simplicity. Skeuomorphic design features are intuitive as they resemble real-world objects. This minimizes the need for designers to explain how user interactions should happen and generally makes such interactions smoother.

Feedback. Certain skeuomorphism elements, such as camera shutter sound or sounds or vibrations, can serve as immediate feedback for users trying out a product or service. This, in turn, helps enhance their experience.
Immersion. Incorporating skeuomorphic elements like icons or backgrounds can also help enhance user immersion. This is achieved by aligning digital experiences with familiar real-world ones.

body.text: The drawbacks are:

items: Complexity. Too many skeuomorphic elements can look too complex and create interfaces that are cluttered with unnecessary elements. While these elements can mimic real-world objects, they serve no practical purpose.

Outdated. These days, a lot of skeuomorphic elements in a design can make it look outdated and irrelevant. This largely depends on the examples of skeuomorphism used for a certain project. For instance, using a floppy disk icon to represent the "save" function may confuse younger users who have never seen such items or interacted with them.

Performance. When a designer adds too many skeuomorphic components to an app or a [website](/blog/website-redesign-guide-tips-and-examples), this can impact their performance. Such elements usually require additional resources to load and maintain and can potentially affect the user experience negatively.

body.text: What Is a Skeuomorph Design Used For?
These days, skeuomorphic design isn't as common as it was a decade ago. However, in particular cases it can still be the best choice. Here are some use cases that prove this point.
Enhanced Immersion

Skeuomorphic design helps deepen immersion in video games. For instance, such elements boost the look of the user interface and make environments feel more authentic and engaging. One of the most common examples is old maps used in games like Red Dead Redemption 2.
Assistance to Technologically Challenged Users

Certain countries and older adults may be less familiar with new technologies. In this case, skeuomorphic design can make the user experience more intuitive. When the interfaces resemble familiar physical objects, users who generally struggle with digital tasks can master them with more ease.
Adaptation to New Technologies

Even those of us familiar with modern technologies may need help with mastering new ones. For instance, many people who are proficient with personal computers and the internet might still find it challenging to adapt to the latest advances in augmented reality. In this case, skeuomorphic elements can also be very helpful. With their assistance, AR software may mimic the ‘real-world’ layouts and items, shortening the learning curve for certain users.
Alternatives to Skeuomorphism
Now you know the answer to “What is skeuomorphic design?”, and when it's appropriate to use it. But what should you do when such solutions don't seem the most suitable option?
In this case, you can use alternative styles.
Flat Design

This style prioritizes readability and simplicity over real-world resemblance. Each element is straightforward and serves a single purpose. Such designs can look quite simple yet stylish and user-friendly. For instance, Arounda used flat illustrations and charts when redesigning [Metricly](https://arounda.agency/case/metricly), an AWS cost optimization platform.
Neomorphism

This style is a combination of skeuomorphism and flat design. It uses subtle shadows and color gradients to make the objects look deep and appealing. At the same time, it lacks the familiarity of traditional skeuomorphic elements.
Minimalism

This style focuses on using as few elements as possible. It embraces simplicity and often works with negative space to create clean and uncluttered designs. One of the vivid examples of minimalist style is Arounda's redesign of [Expense](https://arounda.agency/case/xpence), an expense management platform.
Conclusion

Skeuomorphic design might not be the trending one. Still, it helped lay the groundwork for newer approaches and helped users adapt to digital devices. Furthermore, even these days, it is important to know what is skeuomorphism design, as opting for it could benefit certain projects.

title: What is Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) And Its Benefits?
author: Valeriia Serohina
excerpt: No matter how good your tech idea might be, it can still fail to impact users if the product is too complex for them to grasp. So, the question is, how can you help users interact with your product better and with less headache?

body.text: No matter how good your tech idea might be, it can still fail to impact users if the product is too complex for them to grasp. So, the question is, how can you help users interact with your product better and with less headache?

This can be achieved with the help of Human-Computer Interaction design. Its market [is expected to grow](https://www.marketresearchfuture.com/reports/human-computer-interaction-hci-market-11485) to almost $1,7 million by 2030, which clearly shows that this area is here to stay.

Human-Computer Interaction provides the theoretical and research-based foundation for what we do as a [design agency](https://arounda.agency/about). In all our projects, from wellness apps like[Mine’d](https://arounda.agency/case/mined) to AI-driven solutions for businesses such as[SageExpress](https://arounda.agency/case/sageexpress), we focus on humans who will interact with our design, their needs, and capabilities. From this article, you will learn what is HCI and why it’s crucial for today’s tech projects.
Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) definition

Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) is a diverse area that focuses on creating and assessing computer systems and interfaces that people interact with. Its main goal is to make technology easier, more efficient, and more enjoyable to use. To achieve this, HCI users design principles, psychology, ergonomics, cognitive, computer, and behavioral sciences.
Key Elements of HCI Theory
Now that you know the HCI meaning, let’s explore it further by discovering its main components. These are:

items: The user — an individual or group which uses a computer system for a common task. To make the interaction seamless, HCI studies users' needs, goals, and[behavior patterns](/blog/key-principles-of-human-centered-design). It also takes cognitive abilities, emotions, and past experiences into account to improve the interfaces.

Goal-oriented task. When people interact with computer systems, they want to achieve specific objectives that vary in complexity and might require different levels of knowledge and skills. HCI focuses on understanding the time and effort users need to complete such tasks efficiently.

The interface. It plays a vital role in HCI as it directly influences user interactions. All the factors like touch, click, voice commands, screen size, and color contrast can affect how users engage with digital systems. Designers tailor interfaces to help them achieve different user needs and optimize their layouts for various devices like smartphones or computers.

The context. Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) theory has to always consider the environment and circumstances in which users interact with computer systems. Therefore, designers evaluate lighting conditions, network connectivity, and user location to ensure that the system’s performance is optimal in any contest. They also continuously test and refine their projects to adapt interface designs to different usage scenarios.

body.text: How HCI Influences Various Areas
Most likely, you are already familiar with HCI, even if you don’t realize it. That’s because it is present in various areas of life, such as the following:

items: In everyday life, technology is often intertwined with daily routines. Even if a person doesn’t use a personal computer or a smartphone often, they still encounter Human Computer interface in everyday experiences — for instance, when using ATMs or vending machines. Effective HCI design is required to make such interactions seamless and successful.

In sectors that heavily rely on computing technology, HCI can become a driving force for business efficiency. Well-designed systems ensure that workers feel comfortable using technology for their daily tasks.

A deep understanding of HCI is essential for safety systems design. Such systems should be easily used by non-experts, making it easy for them to handle critical situations effectively when necessary.

body.text: Principles of Human-Computer Interaction
To ensure that your designs are user-friendly, you need to follow Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) principles. The most essential of them are the following.

items: HCI-oriented designs should accommodate users with[varying abilities](/blog/what-is-inclusive-design-main-principles-and-patterns) and ensure that everyone can benefit from them.
All the interfaces should be adaptable to [different user preferences and capabilities](/blog/accessible-vs-inclusive-design----whats-the-difference).
Designs should be easy to understand and use with different users' experiences or backgrounds.
Designs should effectively communicate essential information to users, regardless of sensory abilities or environmental conditions.
Interfaces should minimize the risk of errors and negative consequences that can happen due to unintended actions.
Users should be able to interact with interfaces comfortably and without excessive physical strain.

body.text: The Benefits of Understanding and Implementing HCI
Understanding Human-Computer Interaction and implementing its principles in your projects is important for the following reasons.
It helps improve user experience (UX)

HCI helps make digital products and interfaces user-friendly, intuitive, and enjoyable to interact with. This directly impacts user satisfaction, retention, and loyalty, which can be vital metrics for marketing and business success.
It helps increase product adoption

Products and applications that are designed with HCI in mind, are more likely to be adopted by users and used regularly. This can result in higher engagement levels, increased usage metrics, and ultimately, grow your business value.
It helps improve efficiency and productivity within the production teams

HCI helps make tasks easier, faster, and more efficient to perform. This can be especially beneficial for production teams, as it can optimize workflows, reduce errors, and enhance productivity levels.
It helps reduce the costs of training and support

Intuitive interfaces and seamless interactions minimize the need for extensive user training and ongoing support. As a result, organizations can significantly save costs, especially on training programs and customer support resources.
It helps mitigate risks

By understanding user behavior, preferences, and needs through HCI research and testing, companies can identify and address potential usability issues and design flaws early in the product development lifecycle. This reduces the risk of costly redesigns, product recalls, or negative reviews caused by usability issues.
It helps companies remain innovative

HCI encourages a user-centric approach to innovation, where products are designed based on real user needs and feedback. This enables companies to stay ahead of market trends, anticipate user expectations, and adapt their offerings to meet evolving demands.
Conclusion

Well-designed computer interfaces are essential in encouraging users to engage with digital devices in today's technological era. HCI is actively used to achieve that. It creates a seamless interaction between humans and machines, making using an interface or a system much easier. Implementing the HCI principle is essential for companies that want to ensure product adoption and remain competitive.

Since 2016, the Arounda team has developed valuable digital products for people worldwide. Our main goal is to create designs that truly work for people that are comfortable and inclusive in daily use. We are also skilled at working with future-driven technologies, be it for building an MVP or improving an existing product.
