Revenue is on track to grow at an impressive [19.38%](https://www.statista.com/outlook/tmo/public-cloud/software-as-a-service/worldwide) each year from 2025 to 2029, reaching a total market volume of $793.1 billion by the end of that period.

Over the past nine years, [Arounda](/industries/saas) has assisted SaaS startups and companies in launching digital products from concept to implementation. With extensive experience across diverse niches, this article explores the factors influencing SaaS development costs. It provides insights into the pricing of SaaS solutions.
SaaS Development Challenges

It's essential to acknowledge the existence of hidden challenges throughout the SaaS designing process. They underscore the importance of careful budgeting and preparation to overcome potential obstacles:

items: Ensuring the security and privacy of user data. Prioritize security best practices to prevent serious consequences and build trust.
Achieving optimal performance and scalability. Optimize application architecture, choose the right hosting provider, and streamline deployment for peak performance and scalability
Keeping up with evolving technologies and market trends. Stay updated with the latest trends, adapt to emerging technologies, and focus on specific sectors to stay competitive in SaaS.
Addressing the lack of industry expertise. Understand the industry's needs, integrate smoothly into existing workflows, and provide a great user experience to overcome adoption challenges.
Mitigating budget calculation errors. Continuously update, optimize, and innovate to remain relevant, prioritize maintenance, and consider ongoing expenses for long-term success.

body.text: Factors Affecting SaaS Product Pricing
The success of a SaaS product depends on careful planning and understanding the factors that impact costs. Let's explore what’s important during the planning and creation process.
Project Scope
Defining your SaaS project's scope is crucial for estimating costs. It involves determining platform type, target audience, and business objectives.
We recommend developing an MVP as a single tool for new SaaS entrepreneurs to lay the foundation for future growth.
Tech Stack and Functionality

The choice of technology stack impacts development timelines and costs, with feature complexity being a primary factor. To optimize costs without compromising core functionality, prioritize and address essential elements first.
Team Structure

Hiring an in-house team incurs expenses like taxes, workspace, equipment, and benefits. Partnering with product design agencies provides flexibility, allowing payment for dedicated development hours from their available teams for your SaaS platform.
Developers' Hourly Rates

Developer [hourly rates](https://devoxsoftware.com/blog/average-software-developer-hourly-rate/) vary based on factors like the country and skill level. For instance, the average SaaS app developer charges around $24 per hour in Ukraine and $55 per hour in the United States. Therefore, the startup cost for SaaS product development differs across geographical locations.
API Integrations

APIs help seamless connections between software components and third-party services. SaaS products often need internal and external APIs because they enable efficient integration and enhance user experience.
Overhead Costs: Beyond Development
Post-development, overhead costs come into play to ensure the success of your SaaS product:

items: Marketing and advertising efforts are essential to attract users.
Regular updates to enhance security and user experience.
User assistance by a dedicated customer support team.
Ongoing staff training to keep the support team abreast of new features and industry trends.

body.text: How Much Does it Cost to Build a SaaS Application?

The development team's location and project complexity impact the total cost. We base our estimation on average prices for design companies in Eastern Europe. Let's explore the breakdown of the SaaS development process and its costs.
Determining Development Costs

Your development team's location and the project's complexity directly influence the total cost of building a SaaS product. In this analysis, we have used average prices for software development companies in Eastern Europe as a basis for estimation. Let's delve into the breakdown of the SaaS development process and its associated costs.
1. Planning and Discovery

During the planning and discovery phase, a business analyst translates your business needs into a technical specification, typically taking 40 to 260 hours. This stage involves competitor research, market analysis, and feature identification, resulting in deliverables such as a technical specification, wireframes, a development plan, and an MVP plan.
2. UI/UX Design

Creating a user-friendly and industry-specific UX and UI is crucial. It ensures that your SaaS solution incorporates industry-standard terms and symbols. It, in turn, provides a smooth user experience that aligns with the client's business processes. The design takes around three weeks and [costs](https://www.glassdoor.com/Salaries/ux-designer-salary-SRCH_KO0,11.htm) between $15 and $40 per hour.
3. Front-End Development

Selecting the appropriate tech stack is crucial before proceeding with front-end development. The time required varies based on project scope, with rates [ranging](https://www.glassdoor.com/Salaries/us-frontend-developer-salary-SRCH_IL.0,2_IN1_KO3,21.htm) from $25 to $60 per hour. It also helps to consider the expenses for quality assurance and project management specialists at each development stage.
4. Back-End Development

You have two options for server-side development: building a custom back-end or utilizing a back-end as a service product. While custom back-end development provides flexibility, BaaS reduces development time. Creating a customized back-end requires up to 800 hours, with rates [ranging](https://www.glassdoor.com/Salaries/us-backend-developer-salary-SRCH_IL.0,2_IN1_KO3,20.htm) from $25 to $60 per hour.
5. Maintenance
In SaaS, post-release maintenance requires a significant part of the initial development budget. It accounts for up to 50% of the initial budget.

Its maintenance involves updating system components, conducting security checks, performing tests, and fixing bugs. Adding new features is considered a separate process and requires changes in both the front-end and back-end.
Analyzing Factors Affecting Costs
Considering several factors is necessary to understand the cost range for building an MVP.
These factors include complexity, development stages, team type, and geographical location.

1. Complexity. When determining a SaaS application's complexity, you should consider factors like scalability, data security, access control, payment integration, and customization. Complex functionalities, multiple integrations, and high-level customization increase development hours and costs.

2. Development Stages. The cost calculation for a SaaS product should account for the different stages it goes through during development. These stages include validation and planning, UI/UX design, MVP creation, front-end, and back-end development. Each stage's associated hours and costs contribute to the final development budget.
3. Type of Solution. Different types of SaaS solutions come with varying development efforts and costs. Examples include accounting, CRM, email marketing, ERP, mar tech, and project management.

4. Geographic location. The location of the development team impacts the cost of building a SaaS application. For instance, South Asia and Eastern Europe countries generally have lower prices. At the same time, the United States and Australia tend to be more expensive.

Let's say we build a SaaS MVP. You have chosen a product design agency from Eastern Europe with an average hourly rate of $26-44. Usually, it takes from three to six months to create a platform, and the team may consist of three-five specialists. You'll spend from $40,500 to more than $100,000 in this case.
Summary

Discovering the actual cost of your SaaS project might be a complex journey influenced by various factors. Initial estimates may only provide rough approximations. Confidently navigating the pricing landscape is possible by creating detailed technical specifications and obtaining accurate forecasts.

title: How Long Does It Take to Create a Healthcare App?
author: Oleksii Kovalchuk
excerpt: [Research](https://thunderbird.asu.edu/thought-leadership/insights/healthcare-leaders-embrace-new-technology-pandemic-forces-innovation) indicates that emerging trends will propel the global healthcare sector to reach an immense value of $6

body.text: [Research](https://thunderbird.asu.edu/thought-leadership/insights/healthcare-leaders-embrace-new-technology-pandemic-forces-innovation) indicates that emerging trends will propel the global healthcare sector to reach an immense value of $665.37 billion by 2028. This growth aligns with the increasing demand for solutions in the booming healthcare app industry.
Understanding each development stage and approximate timeframes is crucial when creating your solution. It enables you to effectively plan and maintain consistency throughout the whole process.

Since 2016, the Arounda team has assisted many clients in creating human-centric [healthcare designs](/industries/healthcare). Based on our experience, we can estimate the duration of creating a new solution or enhancing an existing one. This article will share how much time you need to make a mobile health app.
Overview of Healthcare App Types

Healthcare apps empower individuals to manage their well-being effectively. Customers use them for various purposes, including tracking fitness goals, monitoring health data, and receiving timely reminders for medical appointments and treatments.
Before we answer the question, “How long does it take to build a healthcare app?” let’s examine the key types of such apps.
Medical reference and information apps

Medical reference and information apps grant immediate access to diverse resources. These tools provide drug information, medical dictionaries, and symptom checkers. They equip healthcare professionals and patients with accurate knowledge at their fingertips.
Telemedicine apps
They enable patients to consult healthcare providers through video conferencing or other digital means. It is especially beneficial for those in remote areas or with travel difficulties.
Fitness and wellness apps
These applications offer features for tracking physical activity, dietary patterns, and stress management. Such tools promote well-being and assist in managing chronic conditions.
Medication management apps

This kind of app assists users in managing and tracking their medications. They include dosage information, schedules, and potential interactions. It enhances medication adherence and reduces the risk of adverse drug events. Also, they promote safer and more effective medication management.
Disease management apps
They support individuals in managing chronic conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or asthma. They track symptoms, provide reminders, and offer educational resources.
Women's healthcare apps
These applications provide valuable support for women's health concerns. They include fertility and menstrual cycle tracking and pregnancy monitoring.
Mental health apps

These applications support mental health conditions such as anxiety, depression, and addiction. They provide interventions like meditation practices, cognitive-behavioral therapy techniques, and other therapeutic approaches. For example, you can check out the [Bold App](/works) we created to help people relax.
Personal health record apps

These apps allow for managing personal health information efficiently. It might include medical history, allergies, and test results. These apps ensure continuity of care and reduce the risk of medical errors.
Key Benefits of Healthcare Apps
Mobile healthcare is the future, offering many advantages for patients and doctors.

Whether seeking medical help or providing care, incorporating mobile health apps into daily life can revolutionize healthcare delivery and experience. Let’s examine in detail why it is worth the time and effort to make a mobile health app.
Improved Health Data Gathering with Mobile Health Apps

Mobile health apps offer convenient access to patient health data, enabling faster retrieval for healthcare providers. Doctors analyze comprehensive clinical data to make well-informed medical decisions. These apps also allow patients to access, organize, and store their medical records. Additionally, certain apps aid in the early detection of chronic conditions, heart disease, and mental health issues.
Reducing Preventable Medical Errors

They give healthcare professionals fast access to clinical resources and help make diagnoses. Doctors and nurses can retrieve medical and drug databases and lab results. Also, they can use tools like drug reference guides and calculators. These resources improve decision-making, reduce errors, and enhance efficiency. Apps offer early warnings about complications for patients, enabling timely treatment planning.
Reducing Costs for Patients and Hospitals

Telemedicine and telehealth services offer cost-effective benefits for healthcare providers and users. Apps reduce costs by minimizing unnecessary procedures, preventing chronic illnesses, and lowering hospital readmission rates. This cost-saving aspect benefits patients and hospitals, making healthcare more affordable and efficient.
Enhancing Patient-Doctor Communications

Apps facilitate convenient and secure patient-doctor communication, allowing patients to schedule appointments, communicate with caregivers, and order prescriptions. It enhances engagement and outcomes while enabling doctors to monitor postoperative patients remotely, benefiting patients and healthcare providers.
Promoting a Healthy Lifestyle

Popular healthy life apps assist individuals in maintaining fitness, following diets, and improving sleep patterns. Integrated with smartwatches and fitness trackers, they enable tracking personal data like sleep patterns, body mass, heart rate, blood pressure, and calorie consumption. This data helps users set realistic fitness goals and achieve a healthier lifestyle.
Estimating the Creation Time for a Healthcare App
Determining the time required to make a mobile health app can be challenging. It involves factors like development processes, technical expertise, and platform selection.
Inception
The project starts with defining the scope, creating a roadmap, planning resources, and setting budgets. This phase typically takes around four to six weeks.

As part of the inception phase, technical documentation plays a vital role. It involves business analysis, specification creation, and prototype design. The time needed for technical documentation varies based on the app's complexity and features. Typically, it ranges from 40 to 80 hours.
While it may seem like a significant investment, it is crucial for a successful app development process.
Design

On average, a design stage takes 80–240 hours. It involves designing a well-crafted health and fitness app, including UX and UI components. However, the actual time can vary based on specific app requirements. For more complex apps with additional features, the design phase may extend to 320–720 hours.
Development

The development stage is the most time-consuming phase. It involves front-end, back-end, and platform-specific development for your chosen platforms. Given the importance of cross-platform availability, it's essential to consider time for iOS and Android platforms.

Front-end development typically takes around 190 to 200 hours, while back-end development can range from 350 to 400 hours. Making a mobile healthcare app for iOS may require 450 to 480 hours. And if you want to make a mobile healthcare app for Android, it can take approximately 380 to 400 hours. In total, the development time ranges from 1.370 to 1.480 hours.
Testing & Quality Assurance

The testing stage ensures the quality and functionality of your app. The time needed for testing depends on the app's features and functions, ranging from 80 to 300 hours. Thorough testing is essential to identify and address issues or bugs, ensuring a high-quality end product.
Post-development

It would be best to allocate time to fix bugs and resolve errors during this phase. Also, it's critical to add finishing touches and maintain and update features continuously. Initially, bug fixes and polishing typically require around 30–50 hours.
Consider that ongoing maintenance and feature updates will require additional time and effort.
Please note that these estimates may vary based on the complexity of the app and the number of issues.
Summary

So, how long does it take to build a healthcare app? It all depends on factors like the complexity of the app and the number of features you want. You can navigate the timeline by having detailed technical specifications and accurate forecasts.

author: Vlad Gavriluk

body.text: FinTech has a clear advantage over traditional financial services with advanced technology and reduced costs. Online banking, digital wallets, automated investment management, and cryptocurrency trading make it more accessible.

The FinTech market is [set to reach](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2022/09/20/2518804/0/en/With-20-5-CAGR-Fintech-Financial-Technology-Market-to-hit-USD-699-50-Billion-by-2030-Top-Companies-Growth-Rate-Recent-Trends-Business-Opportunities-and-Forecasts-Analysis-Adroit-Ma.html) $699.5 billion by 2030. Besides, the number of digital banking users in the US alone is [expected to](https://www.insiderintelligence.com/insights/digital-banking-trends/)be 217 million this year.

With nine years of experience, [Arounda](/) helps Fintech startups and SMEs design, develop, and launch innovative solutions, prioritizing compliance, security, and UX requirements. In this article, we predict the cost of developing a FinTech app. So, stick around to get all the details!
FinTech App Development Steps

Before asking about the cost of developing a FinTech product, it is necessary to know [how to develop a FinTech App](/blog/how-to-develop-a-fintech-app-key-features-and-a-step-by-step-strategy) and its main stages. This knowledge is helpful for budget planning and making informed decisions throughout the process.
Understanding the Scope
Gaining insights into the project's scope and complexity is vital for effective planning. It helps you assess the effort and resources needed for each step.
This knowledge helps you identify the necessary functionalities, target audience, and regulatory considerations for your FinTech product.
App design
The app design stage focuses on creating an attractive UI and delivering a smooth and engaging UX. It involves wireframing, prototyping, and designing the app's layout, navigation, and interactions.
MVP development

In the MVP development stage, developers implement features based on project requirements and integrate technologies and frameworks for optimal app performance. Robust security measures are needed to safeguard sensitive financial data. The MVP represents the product's core features and value proposition as a foundation for future development.
Testing

During the testing stage, the team conducts a comprehensive quality assurance process to ensure the developed MVP is reliably free of bugs and functions. Testing helps identify and resolve issues, resulting in improved app stability.
Deployment

After successful testing and quality assurance, the app is ready for deployment. The development team optimizes the app for iOS, Android, or both platforms. It sets up the necessary app store listings, certificates, and configurations to ensure a smooth release.
The deployment process also involves server setup, database configuration, and integration with third-party services.
Maintenance and update
After deployment, the app requires regular maintenance and updates. The development team collects user feedback and analytics to identify areas for improvement and gather new feature requests.

The app enhances existing features, introduces new functionalities, and addresses performance or security issues through regular updates. This iterative process ensures the app stays relevant, secure, and scalable, aligning with user needs and industry trends.
Factors Affecting FinTech App Development Costs
Calculating the cost of FinTech App development is a complex process influenced by various factors. Some key elements and features that impact the budget include:
Product Requirements
The app requirements are the first component that affects the cost of developing a FinTech app. There are two aspects to app requirements, which are:

items: **The scope of work.** The collection of features and the effort required to develop them determine the extent of work. The size of the project and the number of development hours increase proportionally to its scope.

**The level of product complexity**. The complexity of the software product's concept impacts development, testing, and deployment efforts. More sophisticated logic and concepts increase the difficulty of the project.

body.text: Interactive UI/UX

A user-friendly interface is crucial for a successful financial app, enhancing the overall user experience. Developing [the best digital banking UX](/blog/how-to-create-the-best-digital-banking-ux) requires a holistic approach to design and usability, including intuitive navigation, clear information architecture, and efficient task flows for a seamless user experience. Attention to these design elements greatly contributes to the app's success.
Location of the Development Partner

The location of the development company influences FinTech app development costs. The hourly rate of a team of four or up to seven specialists and the time required to develop the app vary in different countries.

For example, US-based app development specialists generally command higher [rates](https://www.talent.com/salary?job=software+developer), averaging around $53 per hour, while their counterparts in Ukraine typically [charge](https://www.salaryexpert.com/salarycalculator/report) approximately $16 per hour.
Time Required for FinTech App Development

The project's delivery time significantly impacts the cost. Shorter delivery timeframes need increased teamwork, leading to higher prices. The type of mobile app developed also influences the total time.
App Maintenance

It is essential to consider maintenance costs. Custom financial app development is an ongoing process that requires regular upkeep and updates. This maintenance and adding new features and functionalities also contribute to the price.
FinTech Apps: Types and Cost Estimation

Unlock the realm of FinTech apps and delve into their diverse types and estimated costs. Explore the cutting-edge solutions revolutionizing the financial landscape and find the ideal FinTech app to empower your business.
Banking Apps

Digital or Internet banking applications offer comprehensive online financial solutions, eliminating the need for branch visits. FinTech banking apps handle various tasks, from account creation to loan applications.
The cost of developing a FinTech banking app varies based on complexity, ranging from $30,000 to $300,000.
Lending Apps

[The P2P](/blog/peer-to-peer-payment-apps-process-challenges) lending industry is rapidly growing, with companies facilitating digital loan applications within specific limits. Despite the associated risk, this streamlined process leverages technology to provide faster and more accurate financial solutions.
FinTech loan app development costs range from $50,000 to $150,000.
Personal Finance Apps

[Personal finance apps](/blog/personal-finance-apps-best-design-practices) enable customers to manage their finances seamlessly. They can track their income and expenses, create budgets, and ensure adherence. These apps function as personal financial journals, recording all financial transactions.
The cost of developing a unique finance app through a FinTech application development firm usually ranges from $50,000 to $300,000.
Insurance Apps

Insurance-related FinTech companies embrace digital transformation to enhance services and provide affordable coverage through adjustable-rate apps. Carriers develop apps for clients or agents, enabling access to policies across different lines through the installed insurance app.

For example, our team worked on the [Player's Health](https://arounda.agency/case/players-health) insurance platform, delivering a streamlined user flow for purchasing policies and ensuring faster claims processing and prompt deal closure.
Developing an insurance FinTech app typically ranges from $45,000 to $200,000.
Investment Apps
Some businesses may have investment software explicitly designed for their target users. Other examples of these investing solutions include trading applications, cryptocurrency exchanges, and more.
Expect the development cost of a FinTech investment app to range from $60,000 to $120,000.
Summary

The cost of developing a FinTech App depends on each organization's requirements and objectives. It is likely to range between 30,000 and 300,000. The exact figure depends on your application's type, scope, and complexity. Also, take into account delivery timeframes, the location of your development partner, which influences developers’ rates, and app maintenance costs.

We have successfully delivered many FinTech projects, and some of them are showcased in [our portfolio](https://arounda.agency/works). Our deep understanding of the process enables us to provide a personalized approach that aligns with current trends, emphasizing the value of each project.

title: Importance of Web Design in Digital Marketing Strategy
author: Alyona Deieieva
excerpt: The global internet user [count](https://www.statista.com/statistics/617136/digital-population-worldwide/) is staggering, with 5.18 billion people (64.6%) engaging online. This figure keeps growing as digitalization becomes unstoppable.

What Is the Importance of the Website in Digital Marketing?

Making a Strong Initial Impression

A well-designed website makes a positive first impression on visitors. It is often the initial aspect people notice about your brand. A captivating design can generate interest and prompt immediate purchases.
Strengthening Audience Trust
A poor-quality website creates doubts about your brand's reliability. A well-designed website, regularly updated with engaging content, builds trust and credibility.
Enhancing SEO Performance

Web design affects your website's visibility on search engines. A good one improves user experience, which search engines reward with better rankings. Responsive design, easy navigation, and fast loading speed improve SEO performance.
Web Design Tips for Effective Digital Marketing

Discover valuable insights to boost your online presence and improve your digital marketing campaigns. In this article, let's explore revolutionary approaches to web design for digital marketing success.
Enhance User Experience

A simple and user-friendly website has a remarkable ability to attract traffic. Key factors in enhancing UX include easy navigation and optimization for mobile users. Engaging content and adhering to established design best practices are also vital.
Boost Visibility with Effective SEO

Try to strike the right balance between user-friendliness and search engine-friendliness. Incorporating SEO principles into web design ensures your website appears in relevant searches, resulting in organic traffic and maximizing your ROI.
Optimize Conversion Rates for Better Results

A good website aims to drive user actions or conversions, fulfilling its purpose. To maximize conversion rates, focus on effective communication, intuitive navigation, and accessibility. Strategic placement of powerful call-to-action buttons also plays a significant role.
Maximize Website Speed for Higher Conversion Rates

A well-designed website ensures quick loading times for a satisfactory user experience. Enhancing website performance involves optimizing its speed using fewer plugins, file minification, and caching. Additionally, reducing redirects and compressing images improve overall performance effectively.
Optimize Core Web Vitals for Better Performance
Core Web Vitals are specific factors Google uses to gauge a page's usability in real-world scenarios. Their primary components include three web page measurement metrics: LCP, FID, and CLS.
Ensure Responsiveness

Embracing website responsiveness offers several benefits, such as cost reduction, improved user experience, enhanced SEO performance, and simplified device updates. Prioritizing responsiveness is vital to maximizing your online presence.
Master Content Readability

Consider elements like sentence length, font selection, paragraph breaks, and color schemes to craft engaging content. Additionally, ensure a smooth reading experience. Be mindful of passive voice usage and make thoughtful word choices.
Build a Strong Brand

Do not underestimate the importance of a website in digital marketing. It serves as the face of your brand, representing its identity. Align your web design with your brand identity for effective online branding. A well-designed website earns credibility, cultivates trust, and fosters a positive perception among visitors.
Unveil Competitive Strategies

Getting valuable insights from analyzing your competition's website design, features, and update frequency is vital. Create a unique website that sets you apart from competitors and establishes a solid online presence.
Empower Performance with Monitoring

Using tools like Google Analytics helps to track and enhance your website's performance. Analyzing metrics lets you discover insights to customize your design and content and meet your audience's needs. Keep up with search engine algorithms to boost your website's visibility in search results.
Web Design's Impact on Digital Marketing Strategy
Discover the profound influence of web design on your digital marketing strategy. Explore how effective web design can generate exceptional results.
Search Engine Optimization (SEO)

SEO often drives [website redesign](/services/website-redesign), as it plays a significant role in better rankings. To align your digital marketing strategy with Google's algorithm and prevent penalties, ensure your content doesn’t repeat.

E-commerce websites often encounter content duplication issues. It is particularly true when similar products have identical descriptions on the same page. To overcome this challenge, create separate pages for each product. It helps eliminate any doubts about duplicating content.
Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO)

A well-designed website optimizes the conversion rate by reflecting reliability and authority. Balancing simplicity and functionality is crucial. Complexity may slow down the website, while excessive simplicity can lead to customer loss. Maintaining the right balance ensures a satisfying UX and successful CRO.
User Experience

A user-friendly website enhances visitors' perception and interaction with your brand. Prioritize elements like easy navigation, clickable links, and fast loading times. Ensure a seamless user experience by displaying your website correctly across various browsers.
Analytics

Set up your website to collect relevant data. You can track and measure vital information using tools like Google Analytics. It empowers you to evaluate the performance of your website and digital marketing strategy. Customization and advanced techniques may be necessary to achieve desired outcomes.
Branding

Your website design shapes how people perceive your brand. A well-designed website generates a positive impression, establishing your brand's reliability in users' eyes. When visitors land on your website, they form their perception of your brand.
Thus, ensuring effective web design engagement is essential for building a solid and reputable brand image.
Summary

Web design shapes your digital marketing strategy, highlighting the importance of the website in digital marketing. It influences SEO, conversion rates, user experience, analytics, and branding. By prioritizing effective web design, you can maximize your efforts, enhance user experience, and achieve your goals.

title: How to Hire a UX Designer: Top 5 Tips
author: Oleksii Kovalchuk
excerpt: Hiring a UX designer is required for different projects and needs. UX professionals can work on the project concept or fine-tune the existing one, making it more intuitive, user-oriented, and attractive.

body.text: Hiring a UX designer is required for different projects and needs. UX professionals can work on the project concept or fine-tune the existing one, making it more intuitive, user-oriented, and attractive.
This article explains how to hire a UI/UX designer. It covers all the basics, answers the most common questions, and gives tips and hints.
When Do You Need a UI/UX Designer?

You need a UI/UX designer to make your product stand out from the competition. It applies to starting from scratch or improving an existing one. A good designer will ensure your product looks great, meets industry standards, and is easy to use. They'll understand your users' needs and create a design that addresses them in a way that makes sense.

It's common to consider design only from the UI perspective. To put a lot of focus on the appearance while putting aside the usability. But it usually leads to launching a pretty product that people won't understand how to use.
What Defines a Great UX Design?

If a code is a precious gift, [UX design](/services/ui-ux-design) is a box, and UI design is paper and a ribbon. The packaging might be beautiful, and the present itself might be great, but if you don’t know how to open the box, if it takes time, requires tools, or annoys you — the gift might never be reached.

Great UX design creates a satisfying and valuable experience for users. It combines [UI design](/services/ui-ux-design), user research, and usability testing. A well-designed product or service allows users to navigate through the app smoothly. By creating a positive user experience, you increase customer satisfaction, reduce the number of complaints, and increase loyalty.
Key Responsibilities of a UI/UX Designer

First and foremost, a UX designer is responsible for how users interact with software. Whether it’s a website, app, or desktop program, this person determines users' actions to achieve the intended results and strives to make them intuitive.
A UI designer makes the results of a UX designer's work look pretty. They pick colors, play with fonts and visuals to make the product look great and match requirements.
**A UI/UX designer is a combination of both. The list of their responsibilities looks more or less like this:**

items: Collaborate with PM, BA, and engineers to collect user requirements.
Illustrate design concepts.
Create graphic user interface elements: menus, tabs, widgets, etc.
Create navigation buttons and search fields.
Deliver UI mockups and prototypes that present appearance and functionality.
Create unique [graphic designs](/services/graphic-design).
Present their work to internal teams and stakeholders.
Identify and resolve UX issues.
Make improvements based on user feedback.

body.text: UI/UX Designer’s Skill Set

A UI/UX designer's portfolio often combines both UI and UX cases. It provides the software visuals and examples of the analysis and thinking behind the solutions. Some designers have stronger UI skills, while others are better at UX. When looking for a UI/UX designer, pay more attention to whichever skill your company and your product need.
Technical Skills

items: Understanding of Agile and project management in general.
Ability to conduct interviews and surveys, and compile reports.
Running usability tests.
Prototyping, wireframing, and creating mockups.
Excellent knowledge of design tools and related software like Sketch, Figma, Photoshop, etc.

body.text: Soft Skills

items: Ability to work both in a group and independently
Outstanding verbal and written communication abilities
Multitasking
Time management

body.text: Mistakes to Avoid When Hiring a UX Designer
The hiring process might be tricky, even for experienced recruiters. How to hire a designer with lower risks? Avoid these common and costly mistakes.
Hiring a One-man Band

One person might be good at many things but can’t be great at everything. Opt for a specialist that is well experienced in the most crucial field for you than someone who does many things at a moderate level.
Not Defining a List of Must-have Skills
Consider the vital, the desired, and the optional skills. It will help you set priorities and choose a designer who matches your expectations.
Not Giving Enough Time for a Test Task

The candidate might be overwhelmed with test tasks for several companies or projects. They might also combine job search with work in their current position. It’s always better to give enough time and get well-thought work.
Underestimating a Сompetition
Now is the time when markets are fiercely competitive. Do research and offer competitive benefits and compensation.
Questions To Ask a UX Designer During the Interview
To interview UX designers, prepare a list to help you determine their personal qualities, skills, experience, and attitude. Use the following examples for inspiration.
General Questions

items: How do you keep your skills up to date?
How do you stay current with design trends?
Do you prefer individual or teamwork?
How do you handle work-related stress?
What qualities do you think make you a good UX designer?
What are some of your weaknesses/space for improvement as a UX designer?
What was your most significantt professional accomplishment/challenge?
What did you enjoy most about your previous company/position/project?

body.text: Technical Questions

items: Take a glance at one of our products. How would you improve the UX?
What techniques do you use to decide which features to add?
How do you validate/conduct usability testing?
Walk me through resolving the design problem.
What analytical tools and data do you usually use to evaluate your designs?
How do you define success after a product's launch?

body.text: Personal Questions

items: What made you apply for this position/company/project?
Where do you see yourself professionally in the nearest future/five years?
Which of your projects are you most proud of?
What/who inspires you?
How do you handle negative feedback?
What helps you adapt to a new working environment?

body.text: Hiring Options: In-House vs. Freelancers vs. Outsourcing
How to hire a UI/UX designer, according to your specific needs? There are three main options: an in-house specialist, a freelancer, or a dedicated specialist from an agency or outsourcing company.
In-House

The main pro of hiring an in-house designer is that they will adapt to your company culture, develop needed skills, work according to your policy, and you will have control over the design process. But you take care of employment regulations, paying a salary and benefits, covering sick leaves, and dealing with taxes.
You also have to provide a designer with constant work. The hiring process is usually time-consuming, so it’s not an option if you have an urgent task.
Freelancers

Freelancers complete tasks for your company as contractors. It might be short-term or long-term cooperation, or you can cross paths from time to time. In this scenario, you are free from employment-related issues. You can also choose from many profiles on freelance platforms. It’s handy when you need someone ASAP.
But really great professionals are rarely available ASAP since they are in huge demand. Sometimes hiring turns into betting.
Outsourcing

This approach means that you hire a UI/UX designer from an agency and cooperate on a contract basis. The designer works as an in-house specialist, but you are not responsible for paying taxes and employment benefits.
You can manage designers yourself or delegate these responsibilities to your outsourcing partner. The agency can scale up your team when the project requires it.
If you hire dedicated designers from a reputable agency, you can be sure they are competent. Agency designers usually have plenty of experience in varied projects and follow recent trends.
Conclusion

A successful mobile or web solution can’t exist without an attractive and user-friendly interface. An experienced and dedicated UI/UX designer combines outstanding aesthetic taste with competency in technical tools, strategic thinking, and research skills.

Now, that you know how to hire a designer, you can pick the option that suits you. Hiring from an agency or tech company is best for most business tasks. A dedicated designer is professional and reliable, and an agency can take care of management and team expansion.

body.text: Given their crucial role in business success, businesses should prioritize learning how to recruit UX designers.
Where To Look For UI/UX Designers?
On the topic of how to recruit UX designers, the main question is, "Where to look for them?". Below, we outline some of the best sources to help you find top-notch UX designers.

items: **Job boards and career websites.** Websites like Indeed, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/arounda/mycompany/), and Glassdoor have vast databases of potential candidates. They allow you to post job descriptions, set requirements, and even shortlist applicants.

body.text: Once you find potential candidates, evaluating their skills, portfolio, and cultural fit is crucial.
How To Evaluate UX Designers?
It involves a comprehensive approach to examining their technical and soft skills. Below are the steps you can follow to ensure you assess candidates effectively:
Review portfolio

A UX designer's portfolio is the first place to evaluate their skills and potential. Look for a range of projects that demonstrate the breadth of their abilities. Focus on functionality, usability, and problem-solving approach reflected in their designs.
Assess design process
Ask them to walk you through a project from start to finish. Focus on how they identified and addressed user needs, adapted to feedback, and made changes along the way.
Evaluate understanding of UX principles
In the interview, ask questions to gauge their grasp of UX principles. They should well understand basic concepts, including:

items: [Human-centered design](/blog/key-principles-of-human-centered-design);
[Prototyping](/blog/ux-prototypes-low-fidelity-vs-high-fidelity);
[Inclusive design](/blog/what-is-inclusive-design-main-principles-and-patterns);
[Heuristic evaluation](/blog/heuristic-evaluation-ux-a-strategic-tool-in-enhancing-design);
[User flows](/blog/mobile-app-design-process---the-ultimate-guide).

body.text: Technical skills and tools

Ensure they are proficient in tools like Sketch, Adobe XD, and Figma. They may also need to know [wireframing](/blog/wireframes-what-they-are-how-they-support-ux), prototyping, coding, analytics, and research tools.
Practical assessment
Assign a design challenge to see how they perform in a real-world scenario. It should be a short exercise reflecting the work they'll be doing in the role.
Communication and collaboration skills

UX designers interact with developers, product managers, marketers, and other stakeholders. They should be able to articulate their ideas, accept feedback, and work collaboratively to achieve the best outcome.
Cultural fit

It's also essential to evaluate if the candidate fits well within your company culture. Do their values align with those of your organization? Are they open to the kind of working environment you have (e.g., remote, flexible hours, etc.)?

You can make a more informed hiring decision by considering all these factors. Part of knowing how to evaluate UX designers is asking insightful interview questions that uncover their design abilities.
UI/UX Designer Interview Questions
It's crucial to ask questions that cover a wide range of topics. Here are some sample UI/UX designer interview questions that you may consider:
**Understanding their design process:**

items: "Can you describe the design process you follow when starting a new project?"
"How do you identify and incorporate user needs into your designs?"
"Can you describe when you had to pivot your design approach based on user feedback or business needs?"

body.text: **Technical skills and problem-solving:**

items: "What are your go-to design tools, and why do you prefer them?"
"Can you give an example of a complex design problem you encountered and how you solved it?"
"How do you validate your design decisions?"

body.text: **Collaboration and communication:**

items: "How do you handle feedback and critique about your designs?"
"Tell us about a time when you had to explain your design decisions to non-designers."
"Describe a time when you had to collaborate with developers or other stakeholders to bring a design to life."

body.text: **User-centric design and empathy:**

items: "How do you approach user research? Can you share an example from your experience?"
"Describe a project where you made a significant change based on user feedback."
"How do you balance your designs' business objectives and user needs?"

body.text: **Portfolio specific:**

items: "Can you walk us through your favorite project in your portfolio?"
"What was the most challenging project you've worked on, and how did you handle it?"
"For project X in your portfolio, what key user needs were you addressing?"

body.text: **Culture and personal growth:**

items: "How do you handle tight deadlines or stressful situations?"
"What steps do you take to keep updated with the latest design trends and technologies?"
"What does a good work culture look like to you?"

body.text: These UI/UX designer interview questions should give you an understanding of the candidate's abilities.
Common Mistakes When Evaluating Designers

Now you know how to evaluate UX designers, but there's something else important in this process. Employers sometimes make mistakes that could lead to less-than-optimal outcomes. Here are some common ones and how to avoid them.
Focusing solely on aesthetics

While a beautiful portfolio can be impressive, focusing solely on visual appeal can overlook the crucial aspects of UX design. It is a problem-solving, user-centric design and usability. Always delve into how designers approach and solve design problems.
Relying on impersonal tests
While design tests can be valuable, they should reflect real-world problems. Avoid generic or abstract tests, as they may not give you an accurate view of the designer's capabilities.
Neglecting continued learning
An employer might make the mistake of not asking about a designer's learning methods. What steps do they take to stay updated with the latest design trends?
Final thoughts

Knowledge of how to evaluate UX designers goes beyond examining their portfolio. The comprehensive approach to hiring is key to ensuring that you bring on board good designers who are fit for your team.

author: Valeriia Serohina

body.text: In today's competitive landscape, captivating customers' hearts is crucial for business success. Being indispensable and the top choice in your industry demands understanding customers' emotions at every interaction. Experience design is the key to achieving this.

At Arounda, we strategize and delve deep into our clients' audiences. For example, with the [Mintyswap project](https://arounda.agency/case/mintyswap), we focused on customer desires, forging lasting connections. Studying the NFT environment helped us develop a trendy and competitive application.

This article sheds light on the importance of experience design in business, backed by real-life cases and valuable insights into its benefits. Don't leave customer satisfaction up to chance. Let us guide you toward creating exceptional experiences that set your business apart.
What is Experience Design?

The meaning of experience design is to create captivating and meaningful connections with people, whether in the real world or online. Experience design not only evokes solid emotions but also leaves a lasting impact. It's carefully curating every aspect, from visuals to sounds, scents, and flavors.

This strategic process is versatile and applicable to various scenarios. It can be inventing innovative products, crafting compelling marketing stories, or enhancing workplace policies for happier employees. At its core, it solves problems, elicits positive feelings, and encourages desired behaviors in users.

Experience design is an ongoing journey of refinement. It involves rigorous testing, continuous iteration, and gathering user feedback to ensure a flawless experience. Knowing the people we design for and using their insights as our guide makes it an art of problem-solving. It helps address users' needs and desires.

As an outward-focused strategy, experience design has transformed renowned brands. It reshapes their offerings and elevates customer engagement. This approach drives business success. It delivers unforgettable experiences that users cherish and remember.
A Case of Experience Design in Action
Let's look at how [Airbnb](https://airbnb.design/category/case-study/) leveraged experience design to undergo a transformative journey.

In 2009, the company faced a critical challenge with minimal revenue and stagnant growth, bringing it to the brink of failure. Recognizing the need to attract and keep customers, Airbnb adopted a [design thinking](https://review.firstround.com/How-design-thinking-transformed-Airbnb-from-failing-startup-to-billion-dollar-business) approach.

Initially, the company generated only **$200 weekly**, split among the three founders. They soon realized the importance of understanding their customers' pain points. They discovered that poorly presented listings with unappealing amateur photographs hindered bookings. They took a hands-on approach to address this, renting a camera in New York and replacing the images with high-resolution photos. The impact was immediate and astonishing – the weekly revenue doubled to **$400** within one week.

Airbnb's customer-centric approach was a turning point, realizing the impact of exceptional experiences and design on acquiring and retaining customers. Immersing themselves in their customers' perspectives taught them firsthand the value of understanding needs and desires.

This design thinking approach fueled continuous innovation, crafting meaningful user experiences. It makes Airbnb stand out and achieve remarkable growth and global recognition. Today, Airbnb thrives by creating resonating experiences, fueling its business success.
Benefits of Experience Design
To avoid being verbose, we suggest you assess the impact of experience design on specific product areas in each business.
Customer Acquisition

A well-crafted experience design provides a competitive advantage in attracting and retaining customers. A user-friendly and intuitive design builds trust with the target audience. It makes it easier to convince them to choose your business over competitors.
Improves Customer Retention

Memorable and impactful experiences keep users engaged and interested, leading to repeat customers. Customers who perceive your business as valuable are more loyal and prefer your products and services.
Reduces Development Time and Cost

Focusing on experience design from the start saves time and resources. Businesses that invest in creating well-designed and functional products avoid the need for costly redesigns and fix issues before they arise. This effort led to a smoother development process.
Increased Insights From User Engagement

Experience design provides valuable insights into how and why customers use your product or service. By optimizing the user experience, businesses better understand what attracts and retains customers. This knowledge enables them to shape strategies accordingly.
Reduce Troubleshooting and Support Costs

A well-thought-out experience design minimizes issues and complexities. It leads to fewer support calls and troubleshooting needs. This efficiency reduces the burden on engineering and support teams, saving costs and resources.
Experience Design and User Experience Design Differences
Experience and [user experience design](/services/ui-ux-design) are closely related disciplines, sharing common ground yet exhibiting subtle distinctions.

[User experience design](/services/ui-ux-design) revolves around the end-user's interaction with digital products, emphasizing interactivity and usability. Experience design extends beyond digital products, encompassing all aspects of the customer journey, both physical and digital.
So, let's dive deep and explore these two things' differences.
Summary

Experience design is about creating memorable and engaging experiences for users in the real world and online. It's not just about making things look good; it's about understanding the users and crafting experiences that evoke emotions and leave a lasting impact.

title: Offboarding UX: Strategies and Best Practices
author: Valeriia Serohina
excerpt: In the realm of User Experience and [User Interface design](/services/ui-ux-design), the [onboarding](/blog/user-onboarding-design-best-practices-guide-with-examples) process often garners much attention. Initial impressions play a decisive

body.text: In the realm of User Experience and [User Interface design](/services/ui-ux-design), the [onboarding](/blog/user-onboarding-design-best-practices-guide-with-examples) process often garners much attention. Initial impressions play a decisive role in setting the stage for a long-lasting relationship. However, a lesser-explored but equally crucial aspect of UX is offboarding.

Arounda specializes in crafting [comprehensive user experiences](https://arounda.agency/works). We understand the critical role of offboarding UX/UI in user satisfaction and brand perception. This article will explore the fundamental principles of offboarding UX and the best practices to follow.
What is Offboarding?

Firstly, it is crucial to define the concept. "Offboarding UX" refers to the user's experience when they leave a digital product or service. It can be deleting an account, unsubscribing from a newsletter, or exiting an app.
Offboarding UX is the final touchpoint a user has with your product. It impacts their perception of your brand, likelihood to return, and potential to recommend you.
Importance of Offboarding and End-Of-Life Experiences

When discussing offboarding [UX design](/services/ui-ux-design), one might ask, "Why focus on users who are leaving?" The answer lies in the multi-faceted impact it can have on both users and the product itself. Well-designed offboarding and end-of-life experiences are crucial for several reasons:

items: **Feedback and Improvement.** Offboarding is a valuable opportunity to collect feedback from users. When a user decides to discontinue a service, they often have specific reasons to do so. By providing a platform for users to share their experiences, you can gather actionable insights to improve.

**User Respect and Autonomy.** A well-designed offboarding process shows respect for user autonomy. It gives them a sense of control, allowing them to discontinue service easily. It can significantly impact their overall perception of the brand and foster trust.

**Positive Closure.** A good offboarding or end-of-life experience provides positive closure. Even if users are leaving, they will appreciate a smooth exit process. This positive closure increases the chances of them returning it if you launch a new product or their circumstances change.

body.text: Offboarding UX Best Practices
To better understand offboarding UX/UI, we must delve into the best methodologies to create a streamlined experience.
Make it Easy

One of the cardinal rules in offboarding UX design is to keep the process simple and intuitive. Users should be able to find the exit without trawling through layers of convoluted menus or navigating a maze of options. The more complex or concealed the offboarding process is, the more likely it is to breed frustration and negativity in users.
Such experiences can shadow their entire interaction with your brand. Whether it's account deletion or service cancellation, ensure the process is straightforward.
Ask for Feedback

Offboarding UX is an opportunity to turn a harmful situation into a source of improvement for your product. It's a crucial moment to gather feedback and understand why a user is leaving. Ask users about their reasons for leaving, their experiences with your product, and any suggestions they might have.

It's also a chance to show that you value their opinion and constantly strive to improve your offering. However, balancing this with respect for the user's time and patience is crucial. Ask for feedback, but don't demand it. Don't make it mandatory to delete an account or cancel a service.
Allow for Re-Engagement

Offboarding does not necessarily mean the end of the user's relationship with your brand. During offboarding, tactfully remind users of the value they're forgoing. You can offer alternatives to complete disengagement, such as pausing their subscription. If applicable, consider giving them a chance to take a break and return when ready.
Ensuring that your approach doesn't appear desperate or manipulative is vital. Users should feel free to leave and have the option to return in a way that suits their current needs.
Maintain a Positive Tone
The tone of communication during the offboarding process impacts the user's perception of your brand. Aim to keep your language positive, respectful, and appreciative throughout.

Even if users are leaving, express gratitude for the time they spent with your product. A heartfelt thank-you and a warm invitation to return at their convenience can leave a lasting impression. Remember, the end goal of offboarding is not just to facilitate a smooth exit but also to foster goodwill.
Challenges of Offboarding UX Creation
Here is why creating a good offboarding UX can be a complex task:

items: **Balancing Persistence and Respect.** Striking the right balance between keeping the user and respecting their choice to leave is a significant challenge. Push too hard, and you risk alienating them; be too timid, and you might miss a retention opportunity.

**Collecting Feedback. **Offboarding offers an opportunity to get user feedback. Yet, it takes effort to make this process smooth and manageable. It's crucial to ask the right questions at the right time without overwhelming or annoying the user.

**Data Deletion. **Compliance with privacy regulations such as GDPR requires businesses to delete user data upon request. Ensuring thorough data removal while maintaining system integrity can be technically challenging.

**Resource-Intensiveness.** Creating a comprehensive offboarding process can be time-consuming and resource-intensive. It might divert valuable resources from other areas like product development or marketing.

body.text: Building a good offboarding UX can change how you manage your service's lifecycle, even with these challenges. It's an opportunity to leave a lasting, positive impression on departing users and transform a goodbye into a "see you again."
Offboarding UX Examples
Let's delve deeper into offboarding UX examples from companies that implement the best practices.
Spotify

Known for its impressive UX, Spotify also applies this dedication to its offboarding process. Spotify asks users to give a reason when they cancel their Premium subscription. They can choose from cost, usage frequency, or switching to a competitor.

This step not only enables Spotify to gather critical user feedback but also allows them to address user concerns. For instance, if a user selects cost as a reason, Spotify informs them about any available discounted plans. But, providing a basis for cancellation is optional, and users can skip this step.
Netflix

Netflix's offboarding process is straightforward and respectful. It allows users to cancel their subscriptions with a few clicks without any unnecessary complications. It embodies the "make it easy" principle.

Netflix also adopts a potent re-engagement strategy. Netflix tells users it will store their profiles, preferences, and viewing details for ten months. They can return within that period and find everything as they left it.
This policy encourages users to return and resume their experience without starting from scratch. It fosters a sense of user loyalty and maintains a positive brand perception.
Provide the Best Offboarding UX With Arounda!

Although often overlooked, offboarding UX is crucial to the overall user experience. A user-focused offboarding process can boost user satisfaction. It offers helpful insights and builds trust. It leaves the door open for the user to come back in the future.

[Arounda](/) pays attention to offboarding as well as onboarding in our UX/UI designs. We maintain a balance between both to ensure a comprehensive and respectful user experience.
