title: Types of SaaS Software: Categories and Examples
author: Vlad Gavriluk
excerpt: Did you know that businesses of different sizes use from [42 to 158](https://www.bettercloud.com/resources/state-of-saas/) SaaS apps? It means that SaaS is a profitable software licensing model that attracts more companies’ attention.

body.text: Did you know that businesses of different sizes use from [42 to 158](https://www.bettercloud.com/resources/state-of-saas/) SaaS apps? It means that SaaS is a profitable software licensing model that attracts more companies’ attention.
What about predictions?

Well, the SaaS market isn’t slowing down anytime soon. By 2034, it could skyrocket to more than [$1.2 trillion](https://www.precedenceresearch.com/software-as-a-service-market) (to compare, in 2025, this number is $408 billion). That’s some serious growth, moving steadily at about 13.3% each year.
So, it’s time to grow your business or idea.

If you want to integrate software as a service solution into your business processes or create your own, then today’s article is just for you. Here you will learn about the main types of SaaS products and the advantages of this model.

[Arounda](/) has prepared this article relying on its profound expertise in the software as a service niche. For more than nine years in the tech market, our team has successfully delivered multiple SaaS projects. So let’s explore this topic together.
What Are the Benefits of SaaS Solutions?
Do you want to learn about the main advantages of software as a service? Let’s first make sure you understand the SaaS definition.

Software as a service (SaaS) is a software distribution strategy where customers can access products via the Internet on a subscription basis. This model eliminates the need to install desktop applications, as SaaS solutions use cloud computing technology and are available to users on a remote server.
Let’s now look at the main advantages of SaaS:
Suitable for All Niches

Any industry can benefit from integrating at least one SaaS product into its processes. Such software offers various functions, from personnel administration to customer relationship management. As a result, every business will find something to suit its needs.
Cost-Effective

Companies can choose the SaaS subscription plan that fits them best, and it’s usually cheaper than buying traditional software. Plus, businesses don’t need to spend money on hardware and infrastructure.
Accessible
Since SaaS products are in the cloud, anyone with internet access can use them. Such programs do not need to be specially installed on the computer. It is enough to have only a web browser.
Scalable

The company can change the subscription model anytime and expand the number of services it needs from one or another SaaS product. In addition, the cloud environment, which is among the key components of SaaS, allows businesses to scale as quickly and profitably as possible.
Secure
Cloud technologies offer a high level of data security because they are more decentralized. Therefore, SaaS product users can be sure of their private information safety.
User-Friendly
You don’t need to be a tech expert when employing SaaS solutions. As a rule, the suppliers of such products have already taken care of their intuitiveness and ease of use.

These are only the main advantages of software as a service products that we could mention. But in reality, there are much more of them. For example, such software easily integrates with third-party services, or you can get significant benefits from free trials, etc.
What Are Horizontal and Vertical SaaS?
Another thing you should know about SaaS products is that they are divided into two B2B SaaS categories: horizontal and vertical. Let’s discuss each of them separately.
Horizontal SaaS

The horizontal SaaS model combines software as a service products that are suitable for use by businesses in various industries. Organizations can scale their services or distribute products easily since horizontal SaaS enables them to serve a broad audience from different niches.
Vertical SaaS

The vertical SaaS, in contrast to horizontal, offers software as a service solutions specifically for individual niches. For example, it can be separate products for trade, marketing, finance, or other industries. Such SaaS solutions focus on the problems of a specific niche and help to solve them.
To recap the distinction, horizontal SaaS is multipurpose software for various industries, and vertical SaaS is products developed for specific niches.
Types of SaaS Solutions and Examples

Vertical and horizontal categories are the key SaaS types. However, there are numerous different software as a service products that we have to discuss. So let’s take a look at some tools from the SaaS industry you can pay attention to:
Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Software
CRM software is one of the most used SaaS applications. Such products allow businesses to easily and conveniently communicate with their customers.

CRM solutions enable companies to collect customer data, analyze it, and, based on this, significantly improve relations with their clients. Thanks to such software, businesses gain customers’ loyalty, increase sales, and promote their products and services.
Some CRM SaaS examples include such services as [Zendesk](https://www.zendesk.co.uk), [Salesforce](https://www.salesforce.com), and [Mailchimp](https://mailchimp.com).
Human Resources (HR) Software
HR is also one of the SaaS industry segments. These are products designed for personnel management to help businesses streamline this process.

Thanks to HR tools, companies can easily manage employees’ work schedules and assign vacations or sick leaves. Other functions of such software include administration of salaries or benefits, monitoring employee performance, the appointment of interviews, etc.
HR software also allows you to store all employee data on one platform, and easy access to this information helps significantly improve the work of the human resources department.
The most used SaaS applications for HR include [Bullhorn](https://www.bullhorn.com), [People HR](https://www.peoplehr.com/en-gb/), and [Breathe HR](https://www.breathehr.com/en-gb/).
Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Software
Such SaaS products are best suited for large companies. This software allows you to monitor business processes and plan organizations’ resources.
Among the functions of ERP software, we can highlight financial management, production, inventory, risk administration, invoicing, and even marketing.
An example of such software is [Oracle NetSuite](https://www.netsuite.com/portal/home.shtml).
Project Management (PM) Software
Project management tools are designed to manage tasks effectively for one or several projects. This software allows you to plan tasks, monitor their execution, and communicate with team members.
The list of SaaS software for project management includes [Trello](https://trello.com) and [Confluence](https://www.atlassian.com/software/confluence).
Analytics Software

Analytical SaaS software enables businesses to study input and output data better to help improve their overall processes. For example, for eCommerce website owners, these can be tools for analyzing user flow.
Some analytics SaaS software includes [Google Analytics](https://analytics.google.com), [NapoleonCat](https://napoleoncat.com), and [Heap](https://heap.io).
AI Data Software

Another type of SaaS solutions rapidly gaining popularity is AI tools for data analysis. They differ from conventional analytical apps as they offer deeper insights and faster analysis of large data sets.
An example of such a digital product is [TensorFlow](https://www.tensorflow.org).
Communication Software
Some SaaS solutions aim at fostering collaboration. They enable convenient online communication between colleagues, students, etc.
Examples of such software include [Slack](https://slack.com) and [Zoom](https://zoom.us).
Content Management Systems (CMS)
Content management systems are another example of SaaS products. These tools help edit and add content to websites easily and quickly. Such solutions are best suited for eCommerce businesses.
The most popular examples of CMS are [WordPress](https://wordpress.com), [Magento](https://www.magento.com), and [Joomla](https://www.joomla.org).
Accounting and Billing Software
Any business needs software to process payments and manage finances in general. It is where SaaS for accounting and billing will come in handy.

Such software enables businesses to conveniently monitor money flow, conduct and receive transactions, and maintain financial reporting. In addition, such SaaS tools will make it possible to streamline some processes within the company, such as administrating salaries, calculating benefits, or paying taxes.
Examples of such software include [QuickBooks](https://quickbooks.intuit.com) and [Chargify](https://www.chargify.com).

During our company’s operation, we implemented over 130 projects, over 20 of which are SaaS products in various niches. Our expertise includes creating HR management software, AI data tools, CRM, and analytics products.

By cooperating with us, you will get numerous advantages, the first of which is our in-depth background in developing SaaS solutions. We also offer you a flexible team committed to long-term collaborations and highly qualified specialists.
Final Thoughts

SaaS is a prominent niche, so unsurprisingly, such software is in high demand among businesses. Implementing software as a service solution will give companies more flexibility, scalability, data security, and cost efficiency.

If your way is to integrate such software into your processes or create your own, then we hope our article clarifies SaaS for you. If you still have questions about developing such digital products, do not hesitate to contact our experts.

title: How to Design a CRM System
author: Valeriia Serohina
excerpt: No business can exist without customers. And modern consumers are very demanding of the products and services they get. Yet, finding the key to your customers’ hearts will result in a devoted audience and higher profits.

body.text: No business can exist without customers. And modern consumers are very demanding of the products and services they get. Yet, finding the key to your customers’ hearts will result in a devoted audience and higher profits.

Want to know your customers better? Adopt a CRM platform. Stats say that this tech will improve your sales by [87%](https://financesonline.com/crm-software-statistics/) and increase your customer satisfaction by [74%](https://financesonline.com/crm-software-statistics/). Adding to that, it will boost your overall business efficiency by [73%](https://financesonline.com/crm-software-statistics/).

Having a CRM system is one thing. [91%](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/customer-relationship-management-crm-market) of companies with over ten employees have already adopted it. Another is how this system works and how user-friendly it is. [50%](https://blog.hubspot.com/sales/salespeople-hate-crm) of sales leaders still struggle with their CRM product because of its inconvenience.

What’s the solution to this problem? It’s all about the system’s design. Thus, in this post, Arounda will explain why the customer relationship management platform’s UI/UX matters. We’ll also tell you about CRM design tips and processes.
Our digital product agency has over five years of experience designing human-centric software that can benefit any business. We’ll use our extensive expertise to share valuable CRM insights with you.
What Is a CRM System, and What Are Its Main Features?
Before we tell you how to design CRM system, let’s figure out what kind of software it is.

A customer relationship management (CRM) platform is software that enables effective communication with customers. Implementing this tool in business operations improves customer relations, increases profits, and optimizes company processes.
The foundation of the CRM platform is customer data analytics. Accordingly, such a system offers the following features:

items: **Data collection.** This tool collects all customer information, such as contacts, behavior on your platform, reactions to marketing efforts, and more.
**Data storage. **This CRM system feature helps store the collected information conveniently. As a rule, most CRMs use cloud storage.
**Data access.** Thanks to the CRM platform, you can quickly access any information about your customers for further analysis.

body.text: In addition to these features, the CRM system consists of two main components:

items: **CRM dashboard UI.** It is part of the system that provides access to all client data and analytic tools.
**CRM software. **It is a part of the system that contains other functions besides the dashboard, for example, customer support.

body.text: We mentioned the main elements of CRM, but such a system offers much more diverse features. Some examples include email marketing, file sharing, or reporting. In general, such a platform can be adjusted to the needs of each specific business.
Why Does CRM Design Matter?
You can develop CRM with top-notch functionality, but it won’t matter if your clients don’t know how to use it. That’s the primary reason design is so crucial.
While CRM UX design plays a significant role in the convenience of your customers, they are not the only ones who will benefit from it. Here’s what your business will get:
Better ROI

Get a better return on investment by improving the design of your CRM system. It is possible thanks to several factors. First, you make it easier for users to interact with your platform; they don’t need much time to learn how to use your software. Second, a user-friendly system means your customers will use it more often.
Potential Customers Tracking
A well-thought-out CRM platform will not allow you to miss a single customer. Now you can easily track them thanks to the convenient dashboard design and stay in touch with your leads.
Consistent Communication

[74%](https://www.lxahub.com/stories/customer-experience-stats-trends) of customers use several communication channels before making a purchase. Do you think they want to interact with a business that communicates messily? A well-designed CRM system provides unified access to all customer information, so there are no misunderstandings in communication.
Saved Time

With a high-quality CRM strategy, you and your team will not waste time figuring out various work points. All the information is easily accessible, and the employees can quickly familiarize themselves with it. A good UX will also enable your customers to interact productively with you.
Main Steps of the CRM Design Process
Let’s now look at how to build a CRM system from scratch. There are a few steps to make your platform’s design perfect.
1. Conduct Primary Analysis

If you are using one of the available software as a service CRMs, you need to examine its initial design. Look at each feature and its popularity among users and evaluate how customers behave on the platform.
If you are building a CRM system from scratch, your designers need to think through the user flow and create a customer journey map.
2. Carry Out Competitor Analysis

After you have analyzed the initial information on your CRM system, you can move on to studying your competitors. See what features your opponents offer and think about which ones you can implement or improve. Also, look through the SaaS CRM design examples.
3. Handle User Interviews

You have roughly decided on your CRM platform’s features at this step. But what’s critical is to check whether your potential audience needs these functionalities. To do this, you need to conduct interviews with real users.
Conducted surveys will allow you to understand what users expect from your CRM and which features are more relevant to them.
4. Develop Information Architecture

This step is a transition from various research directly to the design process. Now you finally decide which features will be available on your platform and how all elements will be displayed. As a result, your designers create the information architecture of your CRM platform.
5. Create Wireframes and Design Prototypes
At this stage, you develop initial versions of what your platform will look like once finished. Your designers create wireframes and prototypes to visualize your ideas and test them in practice.
6. Finalize Your CRM Platform’s Design
After you have looked at the ready-made prototypes, you can decide on the best solution for your platform. Now your team can complete the design work.
CRM Design Best Practices and Useful Tips

The process may seem relatively straightforward when you look at the steps to build a CRM design. However, that’s only the tip of the iceberg. In fact, CRM platform design is a more complex process that requires particular attention.
That’s why we have prepared tips for you, thanks to which you can make your mobile or web application design user-friendly and profitable for your business.
Define Your Goals First

The market and the CRM system’s design analysis won’t help if you haven’t set clear goals that you want to achieve. Think about what purpose your platform should serve. It can be attracting more customers, keeping existing ones, or increasing sales.
Consider Every User

As a rule, different departments of your company will use your CRM system. It may be the customer support, sales, or marketing team. Think about each worker and the platform tools they may need to serve your customers properly.
Try Innovation

Want to beat your competition? Don’t be afraid to implement innovative solutions in your CRM system. The main thing is that your decisions about integrating new technologies must be balanced. Cloud storage, mobile CRM, and social media integration are among the latest trending innovations. It applies to design as well. See what’s trending and adopt it.
Make It Simple

Do not overload your CRM platform’s design with unnecessary elements. It’s especially true of its dashboard. If you fill your dashboard with a confusing bunch of graphs, numbers, and tables, it will only repel and confuse users.
Develop Intuitive Navigation

The simplicity of your platform is only half the battle. The practical convenience of the CRM system stems only from an intuitive design. It’s precisely why your designers conduct UX research and create a user flow.
Study Feedback
It is a straightforward tip but still very important. Who but your users will point out errors and inconveniences in your system? Carefully study the feedback and improve your platform’s design.
Provide Seamless Communication

Consider a database where all customer information and actions will be stored. It will significantly facilitate the work of service representatives. Your customers will be able to communicate with any of your workers and not feel any difference or discomfort because your employees will have all the customer data at their fingertips.
Use Analytics

Be sure to use analytics tools to improve your CRM UX design. It will help you determine popular features, the customer’s behavior before buying, etc. Many ideas for design improvements can come from past data.
Final Thoughts

CRM systems can make your business profitable. You will attract loyal customers, grow sales, and increase your company’s overall efficiency, but there is one ‘but.’ All this will be possible only if you pay close attention to your platform’s design.
Our specialists have prepared this guide specifically to show how critical the CRM platform’s design is for your business. And also to help you navigate this process.
We are at your service if you want to adopt a CRM system or improve an existing one.
[All you need to do is to drop us a line.](https://arounda.agency/contact?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=how-to-design-a-crm-system)

title: Native vs. Cross-Platform Development: Pros & Cons Revealed
author: Andrii Medintsev
excerpt: Today, people open about 10 apps a day and use around 30 different ones each month. And the modern mobile app market is flourishing with native and cross-platform applications. What about numbers? By 2030, the global mobile app market is ex

body.text: Today, people open about 10 apps a day and use around 30 different ones each month. And the modern mobile app market is flourishing with native and cross-platform applications. What about numbers? By 2030, the global mobile app market is expected to grow fast, rising at an annual rate of [14.3%](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/mobile-application-market).

You can also enter this thriving market by launching your own mobile app. The first thing to consider is the difference between native and cross-platform development. In this article, we’ll elaborate on this matter and explain which app type might best suit your business needs.

[Arounda team](https://arounda.agency/about) shares valuable insights, pros, and cons of native and cross-platform app development, as we have sufficient expertise in this area, delivering mobile solutions for over 9 years.
What Is Native App Development?

Let’s first discuss what is meant by native apps. Those are applications functioning on particular devices and operating systems. For example, a native app for iPhone won’t work on any Android smartphone.

Now we’ll dive into what is native software development. It involves the creation of mobile apps solely for one platform. In this case, different programming languages, development environments, frameworks, and other tools specific to Android or iOS are used.
For instance, to create a mobile app for Android, you’ll require Kotlin or Java programming language, an Android Studio development platform, and Android UI for application design.
As for iOS applications, you may need the following tools: Swift or Objective-C programming language, XCode development platform, and UIKit or SwiftUI for app design.
Native applications provide an exceptional user experience and show high performance, as they are built with tools specific to each platform.
What Is Cross-Platform App Development?
Cross-platform apps are often confused with hybrid ones. So, to avoid misunderstandings, let’s first clarify the difference.
Cross-platform applications are mobile apps adapted for use on several platforms and various devices at once. It becomes possible thanks to specific cross-platform technologies.
Hybrid applications are web apps wrapped in a native app shell. To create such products, developers use web technologies in combination with platform-specific tools.

But let’s get back to the point. What is cross platform development? It’s the creation of universal mobile applications for different platforms. To develop one, you’ll need such technologies as React Native, Xamarin, or Flutter.

Compared to native development, cross-platform involves writing single code, which can then be used for Android and iOS. It saves development time and resources, but such applications are not as productive as native ones.
Native vs. Cross-Platform Apps Development: Pros and Cons

We suggest you compare the two approaches to creating applications by looking at their main advantages and disadvantages. As a result, you can determine the ideal strategy for your mobile app development project.
Let’s start with native apps.
Pros of Native App Development
We have gathered the main advantages of native app development for you.
Exceptional Performance

Native apps use technologies that are specific to a particular platform. In this case, the code is much simpler compared to cross-platform development. As a result, native applications work more productively, for example, display mobile UI elements faster.
Broader Functionality

Native development allows you to work with various tools and APIs of the chosen platform. As a result, there are no limitations on how many different functionalities you can include in your application.
Decent User Experience
When creating native applications, developers must follow the general guidelines of each platform. The same applies to mobile app design.

As a rule, native applications show a better user experience, providing more flexibility and opportunities for app screen design. In addition, such digital products are more intuitive since they aim at users who are well acquainted with this or that platform.
Top-Notch Security

Native development makes it possible to provide more reliable and platform-specific security standards than cross-platform apps. What’s more, it’s easier for developers to implement security features in native applications.
Stable Support and Updates
Android and iOS are industry giants when it comes to operating systems. Accordingly, developers can expect regular updates and proper support for these platforms.
Cons of Native App Development
Now let’s look at some of the disadvantages of this approach.
More Expensive and Time-Consuming

Want to reach as many people as you can? If so, it can be expensive for you to develop native apps for Android and iOS individually. Additionally, you should know that coming up with two solutions could take quite a lot of time.
No Code Reusability
When developing separate native apps, your teams must write new code for each platform. That is, iOS code cannot be used for Android and vice versa.
Having learned the advantages and disadvantages of creating native applications, let’s move on to cross-platform ones.
Pros of Cross-Platform App Development
Here are some of the benefits you will get from cross-platform development.
Cost-Effective

Compared to native applications that require two separate teams to create iOS and Android solutions, you can save a lot by choosing cross platforms development. In this case, you need one team to write code and design a universal mobile interface for all devices and operating systems.
Code Reusability
In contrast to native, cross-platform development allows the reuse of code for all operating systems. That is, your developers will employ a single codebase.
Faster Development
The logical advantage of cross-platform applications is that their development is much faster. Your team writes one front-end and one back-end code and creates adaptable mobile app screens.
Cons of Cross-Platform App Development
Let’s now look at the disadvantages of cross-platform development.
Poorer Performance

Although cross-platform applications can be quickly created and much cheaper, such solutions do not compare in performance with native applications. Cross-platform apps require an additional abstraction layer and rendering process and, thus, work more slowly.
Limited Functionality
Of course, with one code base, you can create a universal solution for iOS and Android at once. However, adapting the code for each platform loses the application’s functionality.
Worse User Experience

By developing a cross-platform application, you will not be able to provide the same exceptional user experience as in the case of a native one. You will create a consistent Android and iOS app design but will lack customization.
What to Consider When Choosing an Approach to Build a Mobile App

Now that you know about the main approaches to mobile app development and the advantages and disadvantages of each, you can move on to the main thing — the choice. Let’s find out what you should pay attention to choose a suitable development approach for your business.
Here are some suggestions:
Consider Your Budget
It is probably the first thing you must start from when choosing between native and cross-platform development. The latter is a definite winner, requiring less cost and time.
Consider Your Hiring Capabilities

Of course, this factor directly affects your financial capabilities, but think about the following. To create native applications, you’ll need two separate teams, which may take a long time to find suitable specialists. Moreover, native development requires specific knowledge and experience.
With a cross-platform approach, you can quickly assemble an expert team that will work with accessible technologies.
Think About Your Time to Market

Does your business strategy require an immediate launch of a mobile application on the market? Then a cross-platform solution is right for you. However, it’s good to keep native applications in mind too. For example, you might build one product for Android first and expand to iOS later.
Pay Attention to Your App’s Performance

Be sure to consider how fast and productive your mobile app will be. Will it be a heavy-duty solution or something simpler? Undoubtedly, it is best to create a native application in terms of performance.
Consider Your App’s Security

Application security is a critical factor in choosing a development approach. As we’ve said, native apps offer an advanced level of security, but there are also examples of how to provide the same in cross-platform solutions.
Think About Your App’s Customization and UX

Modern users highly value a top-notch user experience. It is what you can achieve in iOS and Android app design. Native applications offer much more tools and opportunities for various customizations, so we advise you to pay attention to them.
Final Thoughts
Mobile app development can be profitable if you choose the right approach for your business. We hope our definitive guide helped you decide between native and cross-platform apps.

Arounda has profound experience creating native iOS and Android applications and cross-platform mobile solutions. If you need a similar digital product, our experts are ready to help. So don’t hesitate and [contact us](https://arounda.agency/contact) right now.

body.text: If you want to make money online, create a digital product. Why so? According to [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/664770/online-shopping-frequency-worldwide/), online is the most likely place to meet your customers, with 75% of people shopping online at least once a month.

Digital products may take many forms, from online courses to mobile apps — but whatever you pick, it’s vital to develop it thoughtfully and invest enough effort in its creation and launch before calculating the revenue streams it will generate.

For startups, creating and launching a digital product the right way may seem intimidating, but it doesn’t have to be! In fact, once you break this complicated process down into the following steps, you’ll find that it’s actually straightforward. We’re here to explain how to create a digital product that generates profit.
**This article reveals four main steps in digital product development: **

items: discovery
ideation
idea validation & testing
MVP & digital product launch.

body.text: In addition to describing what these steps involve, we’ll provide recommendations, checklists, and secret tips from our practice to make your digital product launch as smooth as possible.

With over five years of experience in the digital market, Arounda has already launched more than 130 digital products. Such expertise allows us to share guidelines and tips for making profitable digital solutions that stand out online.
Step 1: Discovery Phase

The first step in [digital product design](/) is identifying the acute problem your product idea is about to solve. Why so? Because the existing problem links your concept to reality and ensures people will really need your product in the long run. In other words, it will let you [test your idea’s viability](/blog/why-is-a-discovery-phase-essential-for-project-success) and make your product market-driven.

But how to make sure the problem is worth solving? Customer pain is the answer. You should identify how big a pain point this problem creates for those who suffer from it. People, or your target audience, will be willing to spend money on a solution if any pain is involved.

It’s a good idea to take note of the potential willingness of your target audience to spend money (e.g., the amount of money they would pay for an app). These insights will help you figure out how many resources you should invest into development and marketing efforts before the release date and what kind of ROI (return on investment) this product could bring.

As a result of the discovery phase in digital product development, you should be able to envision the solution as a clear roadmap. This digital product plan will let you visualize the goals and deliverables of your product journey.
5 Steps in Discovery Phase:
1. Identifying your target audience and its problem
2. Collecting information about the customers’ pain
3. Business analysis to gather extra information
4. Identifying solution requirements and tools
5. Product roadmap
Step 2: Ideation Phase

Ideation is a term in psychology that refers to the initial process of generating ideas or possible solutions. When you launch a digital product, ideation means brainstorming all the possible solutions to explore new ideas and learn more about your customer.

For this phase, it’s worth inviting different specialists, including marketing, engineering, and customer service. This way, every team member can share their thoughts on how they envision the product will be used by customers and what issues might come up for them. This discussion will make your solution even more effective in solving customer pain.
The result of the ideation phase is the creation of a strategy that will provide concrete guidelines to product launch.
Useful Methods for Ideation Phase:
1. Brainstorming: Keep the group of 5-7 people as diverse as possible.
2. Prototyping: Put down the idea into a prototype or a [design system](/blog/design-systems-explained-why-your-digital-product-may-need-one) you can visualize.
3. Storyboarding: Use the narrative as another idea visualization method.
4. The Five Whys: Toyota method of asking 5 Whys to get to the problem root.
5. 6-3-5: 6 people write down three ideas in 5 minutes and pass the ideas around the table for other team members to review and add their thoughts.
Step 3: Idea Validation & Testing Phase

At this stage, your task is to gather as much data as possible to refine and improve your final idea. It’s time to conduct market research, meaning collecting facts and stats about your target audience, reviewing competition in your niche, and checking on the details about the problem you’ve identified. In this case, idea validation means discovering if the demand for your product is there.

Once your idea is validated, it’s time for testing, meaning finding out whether or not your launch roadmap is feasible and gathering more data until the idea is honed sharply so that it can cut glass. A working approach here is to develop and test several hypotheses regarding your product's success and pick the most valuable one.

You can use different methods to test the hypotheses, ranging from conducting client interviews to building landing pages. [Usability testing](/blog/usability-testing-ensure-the-success-of-your-business-online) can also be effective here to validate and test user experience while navigating inside your digital product.
Purpose of Usability Testing:
1. Checking product simplicity
2. Ensuring the product doesn’t take long to navigate
3. Improving navigation till it’s catchy and intuitive
4. Figuring out the level of customer satisfaction
Step 4: MVP of a Digital Product & Launch

[MVP](/blog/startup-failure-the-branding-mistakes-that-kill-early-stage-firms), or a minimum viable product, is a product with limited functionality that solves customer pain. In other words, it’s the bare minimum you need to start a campaign, launch, and collect feedback before working on the full version of your product.
Goal

The goal of an MVP is to find a product-market fit that will solve as the foundation for you to empower your solution further. For example, if you are creating a mobile application, you might create an MVP that has three core functions:

items: signup
dashboard access
one purchase transaction per customer.

body.text: This way, you can start a pre-sale campaign for your e-book before investing in your complete online course's production, design, and promotion.

It’s essential when creating your MVP that there are many scenarios where customers would use your service. Therefore, we recommend focusing on the core problem only but building enough features to address each of these scenarios in the MVP. In the pre-sale e-book campaign example, it’s worth adding all the payment processors you can get to let different users complete transactions in the easiest way possible.
Beta-launch

For launch, it’s important to polish the digital product till it’s bug-free and works smoothly in different browsers. If you’re not sure about that, it’s worth going for beta-launch to collect extra customer feedback, see what works and what’s not in practice, and evaluate your digital product's potential value and price.
Pricing
Regarding the pricing models, you can go for the following:

items: free trial (to let users get hooked and pay for your services later),
pricing by use (to offer several options for money in addition to the basic functionality for free)
pay as you go (meaning offering your digital product for many right away).

body.text: The exact choice depends on the value you deliver and your digital product type.
Digital Product Launch Checklist: 9 Conditions of a Successful Digital Product
1. You’ve met your audience and know what your customers want.
2. You’ve designed a solution that solves the particular pain point for your target audience.
3. You’ve determined the exact results your digital product will bring.
4. You have a working hypothesis you’ve tested carefully.
5. You know the unique selling point that will make you stand out from the market competition.
6. You have a solid strategy and all the resources needed to cover it.
7. All your product documentation is ready.
8. You have all the tools to evaluate the results you’ll collect.
9. You didn’t launch the full version of the product to all your target audience right away.

As you can see, launching a digital product is not a hard task if you have a real problem and a working solution that can solve it. All the rest is a matter of a well-defined roadmap that includes market insights, best ideas, and tested hypotheses.

Identifying target audience
Idea generation and visual presentation
Creating information architecture
MVP of digital product

title: What Is Customer Development? Definition, Process, Examples
author: Vlad Gavriluk
excerpt: Did you know that [35%](https://www.cbinsights.com/research/startup-failure-reasons-top/) of startups fail as there’s no market need for their products? So if you target too broad or the wrong audience, you run the risk of failure.

body.text: Did you know that [35%](https://www.cbinsights.com/research/startup-failure-reasons-top/) of startups fail as there’s no market need for their products? So if you target too broad or the wrong audience, you run the risk of failure.

What should you do to prevent this negative involvement? Adopt a customer development strategy. This approach will help you understand your core audience better, along with its requirements and pain points.

As a component of the Lean startup methodology, customer development assists in validating your idea in advance. So even before product creation, you can ensure there will be a demand for it. You’ll also have the opportunity to choose the most relevant software features at the customer development stage.
"As a component of the Lean startup methodology, customer development assists in validating your idea in advance. So even before product creation, you can ensure there will be a demand for it."

But what is this approach, and why is customer development important? Today’s article will be a comprehensive answer to this question. Here you’ll also find customer development process examples and guidelines.

Being an agency that makes human-centered products, Arounda can tell you much about the customer development approach. We have over five years of expertise in the niche, having launched over 130 products successfully. So let’s move on to today’s topic.
What Is Customer Development?

**Customer development** is a methodology developed by Steve Blank. Startups can use this approach to determine their target audience and its needs. As a result, the company can create a digital product that will fully meet customer expectations.
**Customer development methodology includes:**

items: Defining and testing market assumptions for a specific product
Verifying the problem to be solved by the proposed product
Creating the most suitable solution to meet the target audience’s requirements

body.text: "The primary goal of the customer development strategy is to reduce risks during startup creation and to obtain a thorough understanding of the market and core audience."
As a part of the Lean Startup methodology, the customer development phase is intermediate between the business model creation and the Agile software development stages.
Benefits and Importance of Customer Development
A customer development strategy can help a startup product significantly. Let’s see how exactly.
Customer-Centered Products

The customer development methodology is primarily about your audience. With this approach, you identify your potential users and gain a deep understanding of the problems your product is meant to solve. As a result, you create software that is indeed end-user-oriented.
Reduced Risks and Saved Money

When you apply the customer development approach, you invest wisely in product creation. Before spending money, you confirm the viability of your idea and the value of your software to customers. Guided by valid data and facts, you can significantly reduce the risks associated with product development and launch.
Smart Use of Resources

As already mentioned, don’t make hasty decisions and don’t spend money until you are sure of your digital product’s prospects. This way, customer development allows you to stretch your resources for longer. It is especially attractive to your potential startup investors, as this way, they’ll see that you have a well-thought-out growth strategy.
Only Necessary Solutions

Customer development will also help in creating your minimum viable product (MVP). You’ll know which software’s features will satisfy your target audience. In this way, you implement only relevant solutions for your users and do not waste time and money on developing unnecessary features.
What Are the Examples of Customer Development?

In its essence, customer development involves conducting surveys among customers and showing them potential solutions. Such research is necessary to evaluate which of your ideas or their variants is most relevant to your audience. Let’s look at some cases where the customer development process has come in handy.
Dropbox

[Dropbox](https://www.dropbox.com) is one of the most popular file-sharing services today. It is not surprising, since at the time of its launch, there were no alternative products, and those solutions on the market were far from perfect.
Despite having many top developers on the Dropbox team, the project was not immediately successful. The staff struggled with marketing and blew a fortune trying to draw new clients.

Then the Dropbox team decided to focus their efforts on customer development. The conducted research allowed this company to realize that traditional marketing approaches would not give positive results in attracting users, as there were no such solutions on the market then.
As a result, Dropbox has concluded that the best way to raise awareness of its product is through a word-of-mouth marketing strategy.
Buffer
[Buffer](https://buffer.com) is an app for managing various social network accounts in one place. This software is popular and has many premium clients.

The problem was that the company did not understand why its solution was in demand. The Buffer team needed to know why customers decided to buy their tools and therefore opted to use a customer development strategy regularly.
Currently, Buffer conducts surveys among its users through its Twitter channel and uses the collected information to improve the product’s functionality.
Groove

[Groove](https://www.groove.co) is a help desk tool that helps businesses increase sales and improve the customer experience. The company has been successful because of its subscription monetization model.
Although Groove could attract new customers effortlessly, it had a churn problem. Then the team decided to apply a customer development strategy to find out why users leave their product.

As a result, Groove adjusted its strategy and learned more about the needs of its customers. They narrowed their target audience to small and medium businesses and provided them with a more personalized approach. All this helped to reduce churn.
Customer Development Process: Main Steps

It seems you already know almost everything about customer development, except for the most important thing — how exactly this process takes place. That is why we have prepared a step-by-step guide for you.
**It is worth starting with the fact that the customer development approach consists of four stages:**
1. Customer discovery
2. Customer validation
3. Customer creation
4. Company building
Now let’s look at each of them in more detail.
Stage 1. Customer Discovery
The stage of customer discovery consists in finding and defining your target audience. You also need to understand your users’ pain points and needs. This is how you do it:

items: First, you must formulate your idea and vision of your product.
Next, you must develop hypotheses about your product that need to be tested.
The next step is to test all your hypotheses and collect the results. You must find out if your product can meet your user’s demands.
Finally, you need to ensure that you know exactly what the customer’s problem is, how your product can solve it, and how willing the user is to pay for your software.

body.text: Stage 2. Customer Validation

Customer validation is the stage when you practically check whether your product can solve the problems of your potential users. After confirmation, you can develop a sales strategy for your software and think through your business model. Here’s what you typically do at this stage:

items: You need to find customers who may be interested in your product.
Next, you should conduct a survey directly among your target audience.
Finally, it would help if you understand your product’s profitability, market, and relevance.

body.text: Stage 3. Customer Creation

The customer creation step involves developing a strategy for your company’s future growth and scaling. You should assemble a clear plan for your transition from a startup to an established business. Here’s what you need to do:

items: First of all, you need to determine in which market your company will operate: in a new market, in an existing one, or will it be a new segment of an existing market.
Next, you need to decide on the positioning of your company and digital product.
After that, you can directly prepare for the launch of your product, that is, start its front-end development and back-end development.
Finally, you have to create demand for your product.

body.text: Stage 4. Company Building
The last step of the customer development strategy is company building. This stage involves the transformation of a startup into a mature business. How can you do that? Follow this algorithm:

items: First, determine your core customers and think through a plan for your business’s sales, marketing, and growth.
Next, you should consider your company’s management, managing style, and business culture.
In addition, you should identify your company’s departments.
Finally, establish effective communication between the departments of your company.

body.text: Final Thoughts

Customer development is a fundamental strategy to make sure that there will be a market for your product. This process allows you to test the viability of your idea by analyzing information from your audience.

We hope today’s article helped you learn how to build a digital product that will most likely succeed. And if you need assistance with customer development, Arounda is at your service. We’ve completed numerous thriving projects and can do the same for you. [**So feel free to contact us**](https://arounda.agency/contact?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=what-is-customer-development-definition-process-examples)!

body.text: About [81%](https://www.edelman.com/sites/g/files/aatuss191/files/2019-07/2019_edelman_trust_barometer_special_report_in_brands_we_trust.pdf) of consumers worldwide state they should trust a company before buying its products or services. Want to build trust with your customers? Then pay particular attention to your branding.

Your brand image doesn’t end with the choice of logo and corporate colors. It’s only a part of a larger whole since branding is about broadcasting your vision, values, and goals. It also evokes emotions in your customers and motivates them to come back to you again and again.

Do you want to gain recognition and make your company stand out from the crowd? Today’s article is for you! We’ll tell you about [brand identity](/services/brand-identity) and its importance for your digital product. We’ll also share some branding tips to help you succeed.

In this post, Arounda will draw on its profound experience in delivering branding design for numerous companies. Our specialists know how to build a strong image that will convey the individuality of your product. You’ll see this in the example of our [Lunchcrafters](https://www.dropbox.com/s/32xp5wk8q4o5w2s/_%E2%9C%85%20Arounda%20-%20Case%20Studies.pdf?dl=0) project.
What Exactly Is Brand Identity?

As for a digital product owner, branding helps you differentiate from the competition and declare yourself. These are not only physical attributes that your customers directly interact with but also intangible things.
If we talk about the physical features of your brand, they are its name, logotype, slogan, visual identity, tone of voice, and even typography.

Another more elusive component is your customers’ perception of the product. These are the emotions that your brand evokes, customers’ reactions to your messages, their experience when interacting with your product and support service, etc. It’s also how your audience feels about your company’s values.

**Brand identity**, in turn, is a collection of all attributes that aim to make the right impression on your customers. In other words, your brand’s DNA consists of your product characteristics, company values, and client expectations of your business.
Why Is Brand Identity Significant for Your Digital Product?
Since brand identity represents your business and products, you cannot do without branding services. So let’s look at the main reasons you should opt for them.
Represent Your Values ​​and Vision
Brand identity enables you to convey your company’s core ideas, views, and values ​​through digital products. This way, you can stand out in the market and gather an audience that shares your vision.
Boost Brand Awareness

When developing a brand identity, you first consider those aspects that will show your business from the best, non-trivial sides. Then, you also work on visual identity design, aka the ‘face’ of your product. It will help attract your customers’ attention and make your business memorable.
Differentiate Your Product from Competitors

It does not matter what niche your digital product belongs to, but if you want to attract more users, you need qualities that will make you distinct. Developing a brand identity system will help you find those attributes that will be unique to your product.
Position Your Brand and Build Customer Loyalty

You can achieve successful results by working on branding. You form the loyalty of your customers by meeting their expectations and leaving positive emotions from interaction with your product. How you position your brand also affects how your audience reacts.
Increase Your Revenue

A strong brand identity works for you, helping you attract more customers and, as a result, increase your profits. The more unique your product, the easier it is for you to draw your audience’s attention. You can get much more in the long run by investing in a branding digital identity.
Arounda’s Experience with Brand Identity
Arounda has profound expertise in creating brand identities. Our branding agency makes products that impress the digital environment with their uniqueness.
**You will require the services of our branding designer if you:**

items: Want to broadcast the values ​​and personality of your brand
Aim to create a unique brand unlike any other on the market
Want to position your brand appropriately and gather a loyal audience

body.text: **Let’s talk a little about our approach and process to developing a brand identity.**
1. First of all, our branding studio creates mood boards with concepts that best reflect your vision.
2. Next, our visual identity designer creates logo concepts based on pre-made mood boards.
3. After that, our experts develop your brand’s color palette and typography.
4. Finally, we break down visual guidelines with all the elements that will help represent your company.
For your part, you receive the following deliverables: logotype, color palette, typography, style-forming elements, corporate identity features, brand guidelines, and brand book.

[Lunchcrafters](https://www.dropbox.com/s/32xp5wk8q4o5w2s/_%E2%9C%85%20Arounda%20-%20Case%20Studies.pdf?dl=0) is one of the products for which we created a brand identity. It’s a food delivery service where customers can get tasty meals that they can eat right away.

Lunchcrafters wanted to emphasize deliciousness, high-quality ingredients, affordable prices, and a unique customer approach. Our designers were able to convey these ideas through bright and fresh colors. We also communicated this vision through the product’s logo, web design, and UX/UI.
How to Build a Strong Brand Identity?
We have prepared a detailed guide on how you can develop your brand identity and potentially succeed. Let’s take a look at this process step by step.
1. Define Your Brand Vision
The first thing you need to do is to realize what mission your brand carries. Without this understanding, you will not be able to translate your ideas and values ​​to customers.
Your brand vision is the ideas behind your company and digital product. In other words, it is the primary purpose of your business and its value to potential customers.
To formulate your vision, you can write down your ideas, look for branding inspiration in other already successful companies, and leave with a clear understanding of your business’s purpose.
2. Design Your Logo
After you have decided on your digital product vision, you can proceed to logo design.

The logo is one of the critical elements of your brand identity, so you should pay specific attention to it. Consider how the logotype will look on different product forms, for example, a website, a mobile app, or your goods.

To create a decent logotype, you need to do some research. Look at how the logos of other companies in your niche look; this way, you can roughly decide on a relevant style. Next, choose the shape of your logotype and its colors.
3. Choose Your Brand’s Typography

Typography is another critical part of your brand identity. Fonts in your product can raise the awareness of your business as much as a logo. When choosing typography, remember that the text should be readable, recognizable, and match your logotype.
4. Choose Color Palette
Creating a color palette for your business is another way to make your product distinct and memorable. Some companies, like Tiffany & Co., went as far as patenting their signature colors.
Therefore, you should choose several colors that best reflect your ideas and harmoniously combine them.
5. Consider Other Branding Elements

In addition to the critical visual attributes of your brand, there are other matters to consider. These are things like promoting your product on social media. Also, it is the purchase of a domain name for your company. Other branding ideas include conducting offline events to connect with your community even more.

It’s also crucial to take care of your tone of voice. It is the tone that the brand follows in communication with its customers. These are the company’s internal rules of interaction with clients, uniform for all channels: websites, newsletters, social networks, and phone calls. Make sure your brand communication is consistent.
6. Maintain Your Brand Identity

Once you have developed a branding strategy, your journey does not end. Regularly review key performance metrics and customer feedback about your business. Based on the collected information, you can make some changes to your brand identity and satisfy your audience even more.
Final Thoughts

[Brand identity](/services/brand-identity) is critical to the growth and prosperity of any digital product. It is what makes it more recognizable and memorable. Branding also affects the perception of the product by customers and helps build trust with them.

Thanks to solid brand identity, you will be able to stand out from the competition and become a real market leader. Yet, developing a branding strategy requires in-depth analysis and expert skills. In other words, the help of a branding agency is the best solution for your product.

If you need brand identity services, Arounda can help. We have in-depth expertise in this area and have assisted in translating the vision of our numerous clients. So, do not hesitate to [contact our team](https://arounda.agency/contact?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=brand-identity-grow-your-product-and-increase-vitality).

title: A Step-by-Step Guide on Mobile App Development Process
author: Andrii Medintsev
excerpt: Have you ever thought about creating a mobile application? That’s a good idea. People in the US spend about 90% of their mobile time using apps. And the mobile app market is growing continuously and will reach [$645.46 billion](https://www.

body.text: Have you ever thought about creating a mobile application? That’s a good idea. People in the US spend about 90% of their mobile time using apps. And the mobile app market is growing continuously and will reach [$645.46 billion](https://www.skyquestt.com/report/mobile-application-market) by 2032 at a CAGR of 13.8%.

So, mobile app development is promising for businesses. There is a demand for such software solutions, and this market is subject to constant investment. Moreover, mobile applications are suitable for any niche, whether FinTech or eCommerce.

That’s why today, [Arounda](/) has prepared an introduction to mobile application development for you. We’ve created such solutions for over nine years and can describe this process step-by-step. See our detailed guide below.
Key Stages of the Mobile App Development Process

A mobile app development project typically consists of seven steps, which we’ll now discuss. The process may vary slightly according to the needs and goals of individual solutions, but the sequence remains as follows:
Step 1. Strategy
The strategy stage, or the discovery process, begins with working on your idea. Here you define your product’s goals and consider what are the requirements for developing an app.

Your team, in particular, gathers information about the market, your competitors, and your target audience. Developers choose the tech stack, platform, and application features according to your idea. Additionally, the designers come up with mobile app screens and UX concepts.
Also, at this step, you estimate the approximate cost of the application and choose a monetization model that will directly bring you profits.
Step 2. Analysis and Planning

You have detailed information about your mobile application’s market, potential users, and needs at this step. Your team analyzes all this data and produces a precise development plan. You’ll get a product roadmap at the end of this stage.
Step 3. Mobile App Design
Now, your team moves on to the [UI/UX design](/services/ui-ux-design) of the mobile app.

First, designers work on user experience. They think through the information architecture of your application, that is, what data and content will be in your product and how it will be displayed. The focus always remains on user interaction.

Next, designers sketch wireframes that are concepts of your app design’s visual structure. At the same time, specialists are working on a style guide or a design system. These will include all the information about the general look of your product, for example, fonts, main colors, buttons, etc.
After that, your designers come up with mockups, for example, app screen design and other visuals. They also make sure that the design of your product is consistent.
The finale is the creation of application design prototypes.
Step 4. Mobile App Development

This stage has your developers involved. They implement the app features using the selected technology stack. As a result of this step, you’ll have a ready-made front-end and back-end of the mobile application.
Step 5. Mobile App Testing
After the Android or iOS app design is ready and your developers have implemented the front-end and back-end, it’s time to bring your product to perfection. For this, you need QA specialists.

These experts will test your product for functionality, performance, security, and usability. They will also check the compatibility of your mobile application with different devices and versions of operating systems. QA specialists can also test the app among real users.
As a result of all this work, your team will be able to identify bugs and limitations of your product and fix them before launching the app.
Step 6. Mobile App Deployment

At this stage, you directly release your mobile app to the market. Here you choose distribution models according to the application’s operating system. Apple App Store or the Google Play Store are examples of where you can distribute your product.
In this step, you also use various marketing strategies to make your app popular among users.
Step 7. Post-Launch Support and Maintenance

It’s the last and never-ending step. It involves continuous improvement and support of your application. These can be releases of new features, improvements to existing ones, implementation of any design changes, or bug fixes.
The Mobile App Development Process
Let’s take a closer look at the development process in which your engineers are directly involved.
Mobile application development consists of two parts: front-end and back-end. Let’s talk about each of them.
Front-End Development
This part of building your product involves developing what is visible to users. That is, it is a mobile UI.
In this regard, your specialist can use several approaches, depending on your app’s platform:

items: **Platform-specific. **It is nothing but native app development. The front-end expert will work separately on iOS or Android app design and development.
**Cross-platform. **In this case, the front-end developer will create a mobile interface for various platforms, both iOS, and Android. To do this, the specialist will use universal code and tools.

**Hybrid.** Such development involves using tools both for platform-specific and cross-platform app development. In this case, the specialist employs standard code, which he then wraps in technology for native applications.

body.text: Front-end developers also synchronize the visible part of the app with the back-end to ensure its proper operation.
Back-End Development

Back-end developers work with the server part of the mobile application. This process is critically important because your product’s overall performance and scalability directly depend on the back-end’s quality.
Unlike the front-end, where the developer works with the application’s visible part, the back-end handles the code. The specialist works with databases, frameworks, APIs, and hosting.
Post-Launch Support and Maintenance Stage Explained
Let’s focus on the post-launch support and maintenance stage separately. This phase requires a lot of effort from your team to keep your app running smoothly.
We mentioned the testing phase in our example project plan for mobile app development. Now we’ll say more: you need QA specialists’ services even after the application’s release.

When your mobile application is already on the market and gradually gathering users, this doesn’t mean you can relax. Next, you need to collect feedback from your audience, analyze it, and implement improvements based on it.
There is no 100% protection from bugs missed during the development stage. Now you will need to fix them, so testing is a must.

Of course, putting your users’ needs first is critical. Your audience will tell you about inconveniences or suggest interesting features to implement. Based on this, you can constantly update your product and earn even more loyal users.
How Long Does Mobile App Development Take?
Each project is unique, so it is challenging to say how long it takes to develop a mobile application. Let’s consider the factors that affect the development time:

items: **The number of team members. **The larger your staff is, the faster they will implement your idea and vice versa.

**The number and complexity of the application’s features.** A basic mobile application with core functionality will take much less time to develop than, for example, a complex one with many functions.

**Selected technologies. **According to the chosen tech stack, the development time will also vary. For example, if one programming language is implemented quickly, another may require more time and effort.
**Design features.** The design and its complexity also affect the development time.

body.text: Furthermore, consider variables such as force majeure or changes in the original product requirements. All of this will also force your team to push back the deadlines.
Yet, we managed to estimate the approximate development time for a simple, average, and complex mobile app:
The best option for you will be to contact the development company directly. They will determine the development time as accurately as possible.
Final Thoughts

As you can see, mobile app development is a challenging but, at the same time, promising process. Given the rapid growth of the mobile solutions market and widespread smartphone use, you need such a product for your business.
To develop a mobile application, you need an entire team. Front-end and back-end developers, UI/UX designers, business analysts, project managers, and QA specialists are necessary.

If you are looking for such a team, we’ve got good news for you. Arounda provides full-cycle [mobile app design](/services/mobile-design) and development services, so we can help you. If you are interested in our offer, [feel free to contact our team](https://arounda.agency/contact?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=a-step-by-step-guide-on-mobile-app-development-process).
